notes.title: Sentence Boundaries: Periods, Run-ons, Comma Splices, and Fragments
notes.en: An independent clause has a subject, a verb, and a complete idea; it can stand alone as a sentence. When two independent clauses meet, you must separate them correctly—usually with a period. A comma alone between two independent clauses is a comma splice, and no punctuation is a run-on. Never use a period to cut off a phrase or a dependent clause (that makes a fragment). Watch out: the second clause often begins with a phrase ("With a pressure cooker, …", "Built into the rocks, …") that hides its subject.
notes.zh: 獨立子句有主詞、動詞，意思完整，可以單獨成為一個句子。兩個獨立子句相接時，必須正確分開，最常用句號。兩個獨立子句之間只用逗號連接，叫做「逗號拼接」(comma splice)，是錯誤的；完全沒有標點叫做「連寫句」(run-on)，也是錯誤的。不可以用句號把片語或從屬子句單獨切開，否則會變成「句子片段」(fragment)。注意：第二個子句常以片語開頭（例如 With a pressure cooker, …），要找出它真正的主詞與動詞。
examples: Jamaican British artist Willard Wigan is known for his remarkable microsculptures. Creations so small that they are best viewed through a microscope, Wigan’s sculptures are made from tiny natural materials, such as spiderweb strands. [Digital SAT 6, Module 1, Q24]

What increases is the rate at which the water turns to vapor. With a pressure cooker pot, though, an airtight seal traps the vapor in the pot, creating pressure that allows the temperature of the water to increase past its boiling point. [Digital SAT 7, Module 1, Q24]

notes.title: Comma + FANBOYS (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so)
notes.en: A comma can join two independent clauses—but only when it is followed by one of the seven coordinating conjunctions: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so (FANBOYS). The pattern is IC, but IC. Put the comma before the conjunction, not after it. If the words after and/but have no new subject, you are only joining two verbs, so use no comma ("The archivist catalogued the letters and scanned each page").
notes.zh: 逗號可以連接兩個獨立子句，但後面必須加上七個對等連接詞之一：for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so（口訣 FANBOYS）。句型是 獨立子句, but 獨立子句.，逗號放在連接詞前面，不是後面。如果 and / but 後面沒有新的主詞，只是連接兩個動詞，就不加逗號（例：The archivist catalogued the letters and scanned each page.）。
examples: The liquid metals in Earth’s core circulate constantly, and this circulation generates electrical currents that flow between Earth’s North and South magnetic poles. [Digital SAT 6, Module 2, Q28]
No one was hurt, but in two hours the original Globe was gone. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q20]

notes.title: The Semicolon Between Two Independent Clauses
notes.en: A semicolon works like a "soft period." It joins two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction: IC; IC. Test it exactly like a period: the words on both sides must be able to stand alone as sentences. Never put a semicolon before a phrase or a dependent clause. (A semicolon is not normally used with FANBOYS: write ", but", not "; but".)
notes.zh: 分號就像「較輕的句號」，用來連接兩個意思密切相關的獨立子句，中間不需要連接詞：獨立子句; 獨立子句. 判斷方法和句號完全一樣：分號左右兩邊都必須能單獨成為完整句子。分號後面不可以接片語或從屬子句。（分號通常不和 FANBOYS 一起用：寫「, but」而不是「; but」。）
examples: Oddly, there is no evidence that any type of bottle gourd is native to the Western Hemisphere; either the fruit or its seeds must have somehow been carried from Asia or Africa. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q18]
Sher-Gil longed to return to her childhood home of India; only there, she believed, could her art truly flourish. [Digital SAT 8, Module 1, Q27]

notes.title: Conjunctive Adverbs Starting the Second Clause: “; however,” / “. However,”
notes.en: Words like however, therefore, thus, rather, instead, for example, by contrast, in fact are conjunctive adverbs (transition words), not conjunctions. They cannot join two independent clauses by themselves. When the transition begins the second clause, put a semicolon or period before it and a comma after it: IC; however, IC. or IC. However, IC. Using only commas ("IC, however, IC") creates a comma splice.
notes.zh: however, therefore, thus, rather, instead, for example, by contrast, in fact 等是「連接副詞」（轉折詞），不是連接詞，不能單獨連接兩個獨立子句。當轉折詞放在第二個子句開頭時，它前面要用分號或句號，後面加逗號：獨立子句; however, 獨立子句. 或 獨立子句. However, 獨立子句. 如果前後都只用逗號（IC, however, IC），就是逗號拼接錯誤。
examples: However, the differences between the 1881 first edition and the 1908 edition of his novel A Portrait of a Lady are extreme, even by James’s standards; in fact, some critics regard the two editions as two different novels altogether. [Digital SAT 6, Module 2, Q29]

Geoscientists have long considered Hawaii’s Mauna Loa volcano to be Earth’s largest shield volcano by volume, measuring approximately 74,000 cubic kilometers. However, according to a 2020 study by local geoscientist Michael Garcia, Hawaii’s Pūhāhonu shield volcano is significantly larger, boasting a volume of about 148,000 cubic kilometers. [Digital SAT 4, Module 1, Q28]

notes.title: Conjunctive Adverbs Ending the First Clause: “, however;” / “, though;”
notes.en: This is the SAT's favorite hard pattern. Sometimes the transition word belongs to the first clause because it contrasts that clause with the previous sentence. Then it goes at the end of clause 1 with a comma before it, and the semicolon comes after it: IC, however; IC. To decide, ask: Which idea is the adverb contrasting? If clause 2 simply explains or supports clause 1, the adverb belongs to clause 1. The semicolon must always sit exactly at the boundary between the two independent clauses.
notes.zh: 這是 SAT 最常考的難題型。有時轉折詞屬於第一個子句，因為它是把第一個子句和前一句做對比。這時轉折詞放在第一個子句的結尾，前面加逗號，分號放在它後面：獨立子句, however; 獨立子句. 判斷方法：問自己「這個轉折詞在對比哪兩個想法？」如果第二個子句只是在解釋或支持第一個子句，轉折詞就屬於第一個子句。分號永遠要放在兩個獨立子句的交界處。
examples: Only five of these dances are included in international ballroom dance competitions, however: rumba, samba, cha-cha-cha, paso doble, and jive—the last of which is grouped with the other Latin dances despite not having Latin roots. [Digital SAT 6, Module 2, Q24]
Siderophiles are much more abundant in the mantle than predicted in that model, however. [Digital SAT 10, Module 1, Q30]

notes.title: Conjunctive Adverbs Interrupting One Clause: “, however,”
notes.en: When there is only one independent clause, a transition word like however or though is an interrupter. Set it off with a comma on both sides: Subject, however, verb… A semicolon is wrong here because there is no second independent clause for it to separate—it would split the subject from its verb. Tip: if the words after the transition are only a phrase (e.g., "feeling that…"), there is no clause boundary, so use commas only.
notes.zh: 當句子裡只有一個獨立子句時，however、though 等轉折詞是插入語，前後都要加逗號：主詞, however, 動詞… 這時不能用分號，因為沒有第二個獨立子句可以分隔；用分號會把主詞和動詞切開。小技巧：如果轉折詞後面只是片語（例如 feeling that…），就沒有子句交界，只用逗號。
examples: Tadpole shrimp (Triops longicaudatus) embryos, for example, can pause development for over ten years during extended periods of drought. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q28]
Larch trees, for instance, lose their needles every fall. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q27]

notes.title: “Though”: Adverb (= however) vs. Conjunction (= although)
notes.en: Though has two jobs. (1) As an adverb meaning however, it is set off by commas: at the end of a sentence ("…far higher than projected, though."), in the middle of a clause ("The novel, though, still raises questions"), or at the end of clause 1 before a semicolon or colon. (2) As a conjunction meaning although, it begins a dependent clause and takes no comma after it ("Though the museum is small, its collection…"). Test: if you can replace it with however, it is an adverb; if you can replace it with although, it is a conjunction.
notes.zh: though 有兩種用法。(1) 當副詞，意思是「然而」(= however)，要用逗號隔開：可放在句尾（…far higher than projected, though.）、子句中間（The novel, though, still raises questions），或第一個子句的結尾、分號或冒號之前。(2) 當連接詞，意思是「雖然」(= although)，引導從屬子句，後面不加逗號（Though the museum is small, its collection…）。判斷方法：能換成 however → 副詞；能換成 although → 連接詞。
examples: Hopper’s subsequent career would involve more than just equations, though: as a pioneering computer programmer, Hopper would help usher in the digital age. [Digital SAT 8, Module 1, Q22 (adverb)]
Even though bats prefer very sweet nectar, the plants that attract them have evolved to produce nectar that is only moderately sweet. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q19 (conjunction)]

notes.title: The Colon Introducing an Explanation
notes.en: A colon must come after a complete independent clause. It introduces something that explains, defines, or specifies what the first clause announced. What comes after the colon may be another complete clause. Ask: Could I put "namely" or "that is" here? If yes, and the left side is a full sentence, the colon is correct. Use a semicolon instead when the second clause merely adds or contrasts rather than explains.
notes.zh: 冒號前面必須是完整的獨立子句。冒號後面的內容用來解釋、定義或具體說明前面子句提到的事情，可以是另一個完整子句。判斷方法：能不能在這裡換成「namely（也就是）」或「that is（即）」？如果可以，而且冒號左邊是完整句子，冒號就是正確的。如果第二個子句只是補充或對比，而不是解釋，就用分號。
examples: A recent study explains why: making sugar is energy-intensive, and it is more advantageous for plants to make a large amount of low-sugar nectar than a small amount of high-sugar nectar. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q19]

Public-awareness campaigns about the need to reduce single-use plastics can be successful, says researcher Kim Borg of Monash University in Australia, when these campaigns give consumers a choice: for example, Japan achieved a 40 percent reduction in plastic-bag use after cashiers were instructed to ask customers whether they wanted a bag. [Digital SAT 10, Module 2, Q18]

notes.title: The Colon Introducing a List or a Specific Item
notes.en: A colon can also introduce a list, a noun phrase, or even a single word that names what the clause announced ("three goals: …", "the ideal city for a young artist: Paris"). The rule is still the same: the words before the colon must form a complete sentence. A transition word can end that clause before the colon ("…competitions, however: rumba, samba…").
notes.zh: 冒號也可以引出清單、名詞片語，甚至一個單字，用來說明前面子句所提到的東西（例如 three goals: …、the ideal city for a young artist: Paris）。規則不變：冒號前面必須是完整句子。轉折詞也可以放在冒號前、第一個子句的結尾（…competitions, however: rumba, samba…）。
examples: Amrita Sher-Gil was living in what must have seemed like the ideal city for a young artist: Paris. [Digital SAT 8, Module 1, Q27]
In addition, Zufall suggested selling the product under a child-friendly name: Play-Doh. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q20]

notes.title: Colon Traps: No Colon After a Verb, “such as,” or “including”
notes.en: Because a colon needs a complete clause before it, it is illegal right after a verb (are, were, include), a preposition, or the words such as / including. These words already lead into the list, so they are followed by no punctuation at all. Fix a verb + colon by completing the clause first: ✘ "The goals were: …" → ✔ "The goals were threefold: …" or ✔ "The goals were to …"
notes.zh: 因為冒號前面必須是完整子句，所以冒號不可以直接放在動詞（are, were, include）、介系詞，或 such as / including 後面。這些字本身就會引出後面的清單，後面什麼標點都不加。如果是「動詞 + 冒號」的錯誤，要先把子句補完整：✘ The goals were: … → ✔ The goals were threefold: … 或 ✔ The goals were to …
examples: In assessing the films of Japanese director Akira Kurosawa, many critics have focused on Kurosawa’s use of Western literary sources but have missed his equally deep engagement with Japanese artistic traditions such as Noh theater. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q22 (no punctuation after “such as”)]

Formed in 1967 to foster political and economic stability within the Asia-Pacific region, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations was originally made up of five members: Thailand, the Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. [Digital SAT 2, Module 1, Q21 (complete clause before the colon)]

notes.title: Commas After Introductory Elements and Dependent Clauses
notes.en: A dependent clause starts with a word like because, although, while, when, if, since, whenever. It cannot stand alone. When it comes first, put a comma after it before the main clause. When a while/whereas contrast clause comes second, use a comma before it. An essential clause that tells when/under what condition at the end of the sentence usually takes no comma ("…is added whenever…"). Introductory phrases (participial, prepositional, infinitive) are also followed by a comma—after the whole phrase, never inside it. A dependent clause can never be separated from its main clause by a period, semicolon, or dash.
notes.zh: 從屬子句以 because, although, while, when, if, since, whenever 等字開頭，不能單獨成句。從屬子句放在句首時，後面加逗號再接主要子句。表示對比的 while / whereas 子句放在後面時，前面加逗號。放在句尾、說明「何時／在什麼條件下」的必要子句通常不加逗號（…is added whenever…）。開頭的片語（分詞片語、介系詞片語、不定詞片語）後面也要加逗號——加在整個片語之後，不要加在片語中間。從屬子句和主要子句之間絕對不能用句號、分號或破折號分開。
examples: When they were first introduced to western Europe from Byzantium in the eleventh century, table forks were met with much resistance. [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q20]

Featuring jagged peaks of black ink surrounded by hazy swirls of blue and green paint, Zhang Daqian’s 1983 painting Panorama of Mount Lu is inspired by the tradition of qinglü shanshui, a type of Chinese landscape painting characterized by the use of blue and green hues to depict ethereal, otherworldly landscapes. [Digital SAT 7, Module 1, Q23]

notes.title: Essential Appositives: Title + Name Takes No Commas
notes.en: An appositive is a noun that renames another noun. When a title or description comes directly before a name ("plant cell biologist Yuree Lee," "portrait artist Marie-Denise Villers," "the chemical compound aluminum oxide"), the name is essential—it tells us which person or thing—so no commas are used. Also remember that no comma may separate the whole subject from its verb.
notes.zh: 同位語是用來重新說明另一個名詞的名詞。當頭銜或描述直接放在名字前面時（plant cell biologist Yuree Lee、portrait artist Marie-Denise Villers、the chemical compound aluminum oxide），這個名字是必要的，告訴我們「是哪一位／哪一個」，所以不加逗號。另外也要記得：整個主詞和它的動詞之間不能加逗號。
examples: When writing The Other Black Girl (2021), novelist Zakiya Dalila Harris drew on her own experiences working at a publishing office. [Digital SAT 1, Module 2, Q19]
Brazilian biologist Mariana Nery believes the answer might be found in whales’ DNA. [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q18]

notes.title: Other Essential Elements: “that” Clauses, Titles of Works, Essential Phrases
notes.en: Any word group that identifies which one is essential and takes no commas: a that-clause ("a company that specializes in…"), the title of a work after a common noun ("her 2019 novel Gingerbread offers…"), an essential participial phrase ("Students enrolled in the course must…"), or an essential time clause at the end of a sentence ("…is added whenever…"). Adding commas would either split the subject from its verb or change the meaning.
notes.zh: 凡是用來指明「是哪一個」的字組都是必要成分，不加逗號：that 子句（a company that specializes in…）、普通名詞後面的作品名稱（her 2019 novel Gingerbread offers…）、必要的分詞片語（Students enrolled in the course must…），以及放在句尾的必要時間子句（…is added whenever…）。如果加上逗號，會把主詞和動詞切開，或改變句子的意思。
examples: Former First Lady of the United States Eleanor Roosevelt and Indian activist and educator Hansa Mehta were instrumental in drafting the United Nations’ Universal Declaration of Human Rights, a document that outlines the basic freedoms to which all people are entitled. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q20]

Researchers studying the “terra-cotta army,” the thousands of life-size statues of warriors found interred near the tomb of Emperor Qin Shi Huang of China, were shocked to realize that the shape of each statue’s ears, like the shape of each person’s ears, is unique. [Digital SAT 9, Module 1, Q26]

notes.title: Nonessential Elements: Paired Commas
notes.en: A nonessential element adds extra information; if you delete it, the sentence is still complete and still means the same thing. It must be set off by matching punctuation on both sides—usually a pair of commas. Most SAT questions give you the opening comma earlier in the sentence and ask you to supply the closing one. Deletion test: remove the words between the commas—the remaining sentence must be grammatical.
notes.zh: 非必要成分是額外補充的資訊；刪掉它，句子仍然完整，意思也不變。它的前後必須用相同的標點隔開，最常見的是一對逗號。SAT 題目常常在前面已經給了開頭的逗號，要你補上結尾的逗號。刪除測試：把兩個逗號之間的字刪掉，剩下的句子必須合乎文法。
examples: Bengali author Toru Dutt’s A Sheaf Gleaned in French Fields (1876), a volume of English translations of French poems, has enhanced scholars’ understanding of the transnational and multilingual contexts in which Dutt lived and worked. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q24]

In 2016, engineer Vanessa Galvez oversaw the installation of 164 bioswales, vegetated channels designed to absorb and divert stormwater, along the streets of Queens, New York. [Digital SAT 4, Module 2, Q25]

notes.title: Nonessential Elements: Paired Dashes
notes.en: Paired dashes work exactly like paired commas but give more emphasis. The key rule: whatever mark opens the interrupter must close it. If it opens with a dash, it must close with a dash—never mix a dash with a comma. Always scan left in the sentence to see whether a dash has already opened an interrupter.
notes.zh: 一對破折號的功能和一對逗號完全相同，只是語氣更強調。關鍵規則：插入語用什麼標點開始，就要用同樣的標點結束。以破折號開始，就必須以破折號結束——絕對不可以破折號配逗號。一定要往左看，確認句子前面是否已經用破折號開啟了插入語。
examples: Earth’s auroras—colorful displays of light seen above the northern and southern poles—result, broadly speaking, from the Sun’s activity. [Digital SAT 9, Module 2, Q28]

Working from an earlier discovery of Charpentier’s, chemists Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna—winners of the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry—re-created and then reprogrammed the so-called “genetic scissors” of a species of DNA-cleaving bacteria to forge a tool that is revolutionizing the field of gene technology. [Digital SAT 4, Module 2, Q24]

notes.title: Participial Phrases (分詞構句) at the End of a Sentence, Including “thus / thereby + -ing”
notes.en: A participial phrase begins with an -ing or -ed verb and has no subject and no main verb, so it can never stand alone. When it comes after a complete clause to describe a result or add information, attach it with a comma—never a semicolon or period. The same rule applies to thus / thereby + -ing ("…, thus protecting the livestock"; "…, thereby leading to his demise"). Also: commas and periods go inside closing quotation marks.
notes.zh: 分詞片語以 -ing 或 -ed 動詞開頭，沒有主詞，也沒有主要動詞，所以不能單獨成句。它放在完整子句後面、用來說明結果或補充資訊時，要用逗號連接——絕不能用分號或句號。thus / thereby + V-ing 也一樣（…, thus protecting the livestock；…, thereby leading to his demise）。另外，逗號和句號要放在結尾引號的裡面。
examples: Upon recovering two years later, Henry resumed his reign, forcing an angered Richard from the royal court and precipitating a series of battles later known as the Wars of the Roses. [Digital SAT 1, Module 1, Q28]

A firefly uses specialized muscles to draw oxygen into its lower abdomen through narrow tubes, triggering a chemical reaction whereby the oxygen combines with chemicals in the firefly’s abdomen to produce a glow. [Digital SAT 9, Module 1, Q30]

notes.title: Absolute Phrases and Appositives at the End of a Sentence
notes.en: Two more phrase types attach to a complete clause with a comma. An absolute phrase is a noun + participle with no main verb ("…to be quilts, the stitching barely visible…"). An appositive at the end of a sentence is a noun phrase that renames the noun right before it ("…the “tragedy of the commons,” the view that…"); a summative appositive such as a finding that… renames the whole idea before it. Because neither is an independent clause, a semicolon or period before it is always wrong. A single dash may also be used for emphasis.
notes.zh: 還有兩種片語用逗號接在完整子句後面。獨立分詞構句（絕對片語）是「名詞 + 分詞」，沒有主要動詞（…to be quilts, the stitching barely visible…）。句尾同位語是用來重新說明前一個名詞的名詞片語（…“tragedy of the commons,” the view that…）；a finding that… 這類總結式同位語則是重新概括前面整件事。這兩種都不是獨立子句，所以前面用分號或句號一定是錯的。也可以用一個破折號來加強語氣。
examples: Known as the Brass Era, this period in automotive design is remembered for its grandeur and artistry, its vehicles highly prized by collectors for their ornate detailing and gleaming brass fittings. [Digital SAT 9, Module 2, Q25 (absolute phrase)]

As such, Ostrom’s work is a repudiation of the “tragedy of the commons,” the view that individuals will inevitably overexploit a finite shared resource if given unfettered access to it. [Digital SAT 8, Module 2, Q31 (appositive at the end)]

notes.title: The Single Dash
notes.en: A single dash acts like a colon (or an emphatic comma) at the end of a sentence. It must follow a complete independent clause, and it introduces an explanation, a list, an example, or a summarizing phrase. A single dash can never follow a dependent clause. If a dash was already used earlier in the sentence to open an interrupter, the next dash must close it.
notes.zh: 單一破折號在句尾的作用就像冒號（或語氣較強的逗號）。它前面必須是完整的獨立子句，後面用來引出解釋、清單、例子或總結的片語。單一破折號絕不能放在從屬子句後面。如果句子前面已經用破折號開啟了插入語，下一個破折號就必須用來結束它。
examples: In this state, embryonic development is paused for as long as two years—longer than the life span of an adult killifish. [Digital SAT 2, Module 1, Q20]
At the age of twelve, she entered a contest to have a story published in American Girl magazine—and won. [Digital SAT 8, Module 1, Q19]

notes.title: Where Punctuation Is Illegal: Subject–Verb, Verb–Object, Preposition–Object
notes.en: Many SAT answers are no punctuation. Never put a single comma, colon, semicolon, or dash between a subject and its verb, between a verb and its object, or between a preposition and its object. The SAT makes subjects very long ("The strings inside the instrument") so that the blank falls right before the verb. Find the verb: if the blank sits between the full subject and that verb, choose no punctuation—unless you are closing a pair of commas or dashes opened earlier.
notes.zh: 很多 SAT 題目的正確答案是不加標點。絕對不可以在主詞和動詞之間、動詞和受詞之間，或介系詞和受詞之間加上單一的逗號、冒號、分號或破折號。SAT 常把主詞寫得很長（The strings inside the instrument），讓空格剛好落在動詞前面。先找出動詞：如果空格位於完整主詞和動詞之間，就選不加標點——除非你是在結束前面已經開啟的一對逗號或破折號。
examples: The Progressive Era in the United States witnessed the rise of numerous Black women’s clubs, local organizations that advocated for racial and gender equality. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q24]

In the historical novel The Surrender Tree, Cuban American author Margarita Engle uses poetry rather than prose to tell the true story of Cuban folk hero Rosa La Bayamesa. [Digital SAT 9, Module 2, Q20]

notes.title: Semicolons + Commas in a Complex Series (Three Ideas)
notes.en: List items are normally separated by commas. But when the items already contain commas (a name + description, a city + country, a title + appositive), separate the items with semicolons so the reader can see where each item ends: item 1, detail; item 2, detail; and item 3, detail. Look ahead for "; and" before the last item—it tells you the list uses semicolons. The semicolon goes at the end of each item, never inside it.
notes.zh: 清單中的項目通常用逗號分開。但當每個項目本身已經含有逗號時（人名 + 說明、城市 + 國家、作品名 + 同位語），項目之間要改用分號，讓讀者看清每一項在哪裡結束：項目一, 說明; 項目二, 說明; and 項目三, 說明. 先往後看最後一項前是否有「; and」，有的話就代表這個清單用分號。分號放在每個項目的結尾，不可放在項目中間。
examples: These include overseeing the Library of Congress’s collections, which boast more than 162 million items; managing the US Copyright Office, which registers copyright claims and advises Congress on copyright law; and appointing the US poet laureate. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q23]

Buchi Emecheta’s celebrated literary oeuvre includes The Joys of Motherhood, a novel about the changing roles of women in 1950s Lagos; A Kind of Marriage, a television play about the private struggles of a newlywed couple in Nigeria; and Head Above Water, her autobiography. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q26]

notes.title: Apostrophes with Nouns: Plurals vs. Possessives
notes.en: (1) Simple plural = no apostrophe (stories, hands, antennas). (2) Singular possessive = 's (the screw's threads). (3) Regular plural possessive = s' (the rocks' migration). (4) Irregular plural possessive = 's (people's stories, children's museum). Two steps: first decide whether the noun is singular or plural (look for clues like a, one vs. 162, all five); then ask whether it owns the next noun ("the threads of the screw"). If it owns nothing, it takes no apostrophe.
notes.zh: (1) 一般複數：不加撇號（stories, hands, antennas）。(2) 單數所有格：加 's（the screw's threads）。(3) 規則複數所有格：加 s'（the rocks' migration）。(4) 不規則複數所有格：加 's（people's stories, children's museum）。兩個步驟：先判斷名詞是單數還是複數（看 a, one 或 162, all five 等線索）；再問它是否擁有後面的名詞（the threads of the screw）。如果沒有擁有任何東西，就不加撇號。
examples: Currently, archaeologists’ efforts are aided by drones that capture high-resolution aerial photographs of the lines. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q28 (plural possessive + simple plurals)]
Additionally, they help regulate a plant’s water loss. [Digital SAT 7, Module 1, Q27 (singular possessive)]

notes.title: Apostrophes with Pronouns: its / it's, their / they're / there
notes.en: Possessive pronouns never take an apostrophe: its, their, whose, yours. A word with an apostrophe is a contraction: it's = it is/it has, they're = they are, who's = who is. There is a place or "there is/are." Test by expanding the contraction: if "it is" or "they are" makes sense, use the apostrophe form. Also match number: its for a singular noun (including collective nouns like committee), their for plural nouns.
notes.zh: 所有格代名詞永遠不加撇號：its, their, whose, yours。有撇號的字是縮寫：it's = it is / it has，they're = they are，who's = who is。there 表示地點或「there is / are」。判斷方法：把縮寫展開，如果 it is 或 they are 講得通，就用有撇號的形式。另外要注意單複數：單數名詞（包括 committee 這類集合名詞）用 its，複數名詞用 their。
examples: Like other amphibians, the wood frog (Rana sylvatica) is unable to generate its own heat, so during periods of subfreezing temperatures, it survives by producing large amounts of glucose, a sugar that helps prevent damaging ice from forming inside its cells. [Digital SAT 4, Module 1, Q20]

When, in 2017, Cambridge University students Lucy Moss and Toby Marlow decided they wanted to develop a musical together, one of their goals was for their female actor friends to have good parts to play. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q30]

notes.title: Question Marks: Direct vs. Indirect Questions
notes.en: A direct question uses question word order (helping verb before the subject: "how do they affect…") and ends with a question mark. It often stands alone and is followed by a new sentence. An indirect question is reported inside a statement after verbs like investigated, wondered, debated, wanted to understand; it uses statement word order ("how people perceive…") and ends with a period.
notes.zh: 直接問句使用疑問句語序（助動詞在主詞前面：how do they affect…），句尾用問號，通常單獨成句，後面接著另一個新句子。間接問句是放在陳述句裡、跟在 investigated, wondered, debated, wanted to understand 等動詞後面的問句，使用陳述句語序（how people perceive…），句尾用句號。
examples: How did whales, once no bigger than seals, evolve to become the largest animals on Earth? [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q18 (direct question)]
Neuroscientist Karen Konkoly wanted to determine whether individuals can understand and respond to questions during REM sleep. [Digital SAT 10, Module 2, Q27 (indirect question)]

notes.title: Commas with Conjunctive Adverbs: however, though, thus, therefore
notes.en: Conjunctive adverbs (however, though, thus, therefore, nevertheless, consequently, moreover, instead, rather, indeed) are not conjunctions. They can't join two independent clauses by themselves, so the punctuation depends on where the adverb sits.
examples: IC**; however,** IC. / IC**. However,** IC.
Everyone called him a walking dictionary**; however,** he disliked the nickname.

notes.title: Participial Phrases (分詞構句) and Commas
notes.en: A participial phrase begins with a participle (-ing, -ed/-en, or having + past participle) and has no subject and no finite verb. It can never stand alone, so it is never separated from its clause by a period or semicolon.
examples: Comma after it; the next word must be the doer
Examining satellite images**,** the biologist noted…

notes.title: Semicolons + Commas to Separate Three Ideas (Complex Series)
notes.en: When list items already contain commas, separate the items with semicolons.
examples: Romeo and Juliet, a classic example of dramatic irony**;** Othello, a study of jealousy**;** and Macbeth, a portrait of ambition
Lima, Peru**;** Quito, Ecuador**;** and La Paz, Bolivia

notes.title: Every Clause Needs a Finite (Main) Verb
notes.en: Every sentence—and every clause inside it—needs a finite verb: a verb that shows tense and agrees with its subject (claim, enter, have used, explains, helped). Nonfinite forms cannot do this job: the infinitive (to claim), the gerund or present participle (claiming), and the perfect participle (having claimed). When the blank comes right after the subject, ask: Does this sentence already have a main verb? If not, the blank must be finite. Tip: look past long subjects (e.g., "His energetic gestures … and his habit of barreling after a hit ball") to find where the main verb must go, and use time clues ("A decade later," "For thousands of years") to choose the tense.
notes.zh: 每個句子（以及句中的每個子句）都需要一個限定動詞（主要動詞）：它會顯示時態，並與主詞一致（如 claim、enter、have used、explains、helped）。非限定動詞不能當主要動詞，包括不定詞（to claim）、現在分詞／動名詞（claiming）和完成式分詞（having claimed）。當空格緊接在主詞後面時，先問自己：「這個句子已經有主要動詞了嗎？」如果沒有，空格就必須填限定動詞。小技巧：遇到很長的主詞（例如 His energetic gestures … and his habit of barreling after a hit ball），要找到主詞結束的位置，主要動詞就在那裡；再用時間線索（A decade later、For thousands of years）判斷時態。
examples: A decade later, Land used his technology to invent the world’s first instant camera, the Polaroid Land camera. [Digital SAT 5, Module 1, Q21] (finite verb used; to invent is nonfinite)

In January 2023, Nery and her colleagues published a study showing changes over time in four whale genes associated with body size. [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q18] (finite verb published; showing is nonfinite)

notes.title: Finite Verbs in Relative Clauses (who / that / which + verb)
notes.en: A relative clause begins with who, that, or which and describes a noun. It is still a clause, so it needs its own finite verb (which provided …, that specializes …). A participle or infinitive after which/that (which providing, which to provide) is wrong. The relative pronoun is also needed to connect the clause to the noun: "a company that specializes"—without that, "specializes" would have no subject. Use that with no comma for essential (restrictive) information; use a comma + which for extra (nonrestrictive) information. Remember: the relative clause's verb does not replace the sentence's main verb—the main clause needs one too.
notes.zh: 關係子句以 who、that 或 which 開頭，用來修飾名詞。它仍然是子句，所以必須有自己的限定動詞（which provided …、that specializes …）。在 which/that 後面接分詞或不定詞（which providing、which to provide）都是錯的。關係代名詞也不能省略，它負責把子句連接到名詞上：a company that specializes——少了 that，specializes 就沒有主詞。表示必要的（限定）資訊時用 that，前面不加逗號；表示補充的（非限定）資訊時用逗號 + which。記住：關係子句裡的動詞不能取代整句的主要動詞，主要子句也需要自己的動詞。
examples: Former First Lady of the United States Eleanor Roosevelt and Indian activist and educator Hansa Mehta were instrumental in drafting the United Nations’ Universal Declaration of Human Rights, a document that outlines the basic freedoms to which all people are entitled. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q20] (that + finite outlines)

Clear glass, which is classified as transparent, allows all (or almost all) light to pass through; wax paper, which is classified as translucent, allows only some light to pass through. [Digital SAT 6, Module 2, Q22] (each which clause has its own verb is classified; main verbs allows)

notes.title: Participial Phrases as Modifiers (-ing / -ed)
notes.en: A participial phrase is a nonfinite phrase that describes a noun; it is not a main verb. Use the present participle (-ing) for an active meaning (the noun does the action) and the past participle (-ed/-en) for a passive meaning (the action is done to the noun). The phrase can appear in several places: introductory ("Created by businessman William A.G. Brown, the saloon …"); supplementary, set off by a pair of commas between subject and verb ("Richard Serra, intending …, assembles …"); directly after a noun ("a type of painting characterized by …"); or at the end as a result phrase after a comma ("…snow and ice cover, forcing the monkeys to hunt …"). Test: if the sentence already has its main verb, the blank must be nonfinite—a finite verb would create two main verbs or a comma splice.
notes.zh: 分詞片語（分詞構句）是用來修飾名詞的非限定片語，不是主要動詞。表示主動（名詞自己做動作）時用現在分詞（-ing）；表示被動（動作施加在名詞上）時用過去分詞（-ed/-en）。分詞片語可以出現在不同位置：句首（Created by businessman William A.G. Brown, the saloon …）；補充說明，放在主詞和動詞之間、前後用逗號隔開（Richard Serra, intending …, assembles …）；直接放在名詞後面（a type of painting characterized by …）；或放在句尾、逗號後面，表示結果（…snow and ice cover, forcing the monkeys to hunt …）。判斷方法：如果句子已經有主要動詞，空格就必須是非限定形式；填入限定動詞會造成兩個主要動詞或逗號連接句（comma splice）。
examples: Powered with energy collected by solar panels during the day, the blinking LEDs keep lions away at night, thus protecting the livestock without risking harm to the endangered lions. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q22] (introductory past participle Powered; result phrase protecting)

Because the hole’s small size restricts light to a single ray, all light passing through the hole can only arrive at a single destination, eliminating diffraction and ensuring a clear image. [Digital SAT 6, Module 1, Q25] (passing modifies light; result phrase eliminating … ensuring)

notes.title: Absolute Phrases (noun + participle)
notes.en: An absolute phrase is a noun (or pronoun) + participle (or adjective) that adds detail to a whole sentence: "…, its vehicles highly prized by collectors." It has its own "subject" but no finite verb, so it can be attached to a complete sentence with just a comma. If you put a finite verb in the blank (its vehicles were highly prized), you create two independent clauses joined by only a comma—a comma splice. Recognize the pattern: comma + possessive/noun (its, their, his, the stitching) + blank. Choose the present participle (-ing) for active meaning (their facades still astonishing visitors) and the past participle (-ed) for passive meaning (her hands scarred by …).
notes.zh: 獨立分詞構句（absolute phrase）的結構是名詞（或代名詞）＋分詞（或形容詞），用來為整個句子補充細節：…, its vehicles highly prized by collectors。它有自己的「意義上的主詞」，但沒有限定動詞，所以只要用逗號就能接在完整句子後面。如果在空格填入限定動詞（its vehicles were highly prized），就會變成兩個獨立子句只用逗號相連，形成逗號連接句（comma splice）。辨認方式：逗號＋所有格或名詞（its、their、his、the stitching）＋空格。表示主動用現在分詞（-ing）（their facades still astonishing visitors），表示被動用過去分詞（-ed）（her hands scarred by …）。
examples: From afar, African American fiber artist Bisa Butler’s portraits look like paintings, their depictions of human faces, bodies, and clothing so intricate that it seems only a fine brush could have rendered them. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q26] (absolute phrase: their depictions … so intricate)

When viewed up close, however, the portraits reveal themselves to be quilts, the stitching barely visible among the thousands of pieces of printed, microcut fabric. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q26] (absolute phrase: the stitching barely visible)

notes.title: Infinitives: Purpose and After Certain Verbs
notes.en: The infinitive is to + base verb (to tell, to forge, to include). The SAT tests it in two main ways. (1) Infinitive of purpose: when the sentence already has its main verb, to + verb explains why (= in order to): "Engle uses poetry rather than prose to tell the true story …" (2) After certain verbs: some verbs must be followed by an infinitive, not an -ing form or a bare verb—decide to, agree to, plan to, hope to, want to, refuse to, attempt to, fail to, need to. "The committee decided to include …" Watch out: an -ing phrase in the same position may illogically modify the nearest noun, and a finite verb would create a second main verb.
notes.zh: 不定詞的形式是 to＋原形動詞（to tell、to forge、to include）。SAT 主要用兩種方式考它：（1）表示目的的不定詞：當句子已經有主要動詞時，to＋動詞 用來說明「為什麼」（＝in order to）：Engle uses poetry rather than prose to tell the true story …（2）特定動詞後面接不定詞：有些動詞後面必須接不定詞，不能接 -ing 或原形動詞，例如 decide to、agree to、plan to、hope to、want to、refuse to、attempt to、fail to、need to：The committee decided to include … 注意：在同一位置使用 -ing 片語，可能會不合邏輯地修飾前面最近的名詞；使用限定動詞則會多出第二個主要動詞。
examples: In 1943, in the midst of World War II, mathematics professor Grace Hopper was recruited by the US military to help the war effort by solving complex equations. [Digital SAT 1, Module 1, Q27] (infinitive of purpose to help)

When, in 2017, Cambridge University students Lucy Moss and Toby Marlow decided they wanted to develop a musical together, one of their goals was for their female actor friends to have good parts to play. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q30] (wanted to develop: infinitive after want)

notes.title: Parallel Verb Forms (after modals and in compound predicates)
notes.en: When one subject has two or more verbs joined by and / or / but, those verbs form a compound predicate and must be parallel—the same form and tense. After a modal verb (can, could, will, would, may, might, must, should), every verb in the series takes the base form: "The lock would increase the salinity … and create a natural barrier" (= would create). In a past-tense series, all verbs are past: "The map describes …, shows …, and includes …" To solve: find the subject, find the first verb in the pair or list, and match the blank to it. -ing forms, infinitives, or a different tense break the parallel structure.
notes.zh: 當一個主詞有兩個以上的動詞，由 and / or / but 連接時，這些動詞構成複合述語，必須平行——形式和時態都要一致。在情態助動詞（can、could、will、would、may、might、must、should）後面，系列中的每一個動詞都要用原形：The lock would increase the salinity … and create a natural barrier（＝would create）。如果是過去式的系列，所有動詞都要用過去式；現在式的系列則都用現在式：The map describes …, shows …, and includes … 解題步驟：先找主詞，再找這組動詞中的第一個動詞，讓空格的形式與它一致。使用 -ing、不定詞或不同時態都會破壞平行結構。
examples: The map describes the area of a plot of land, shows a river valley, and includes the cardinal directions. [Digital SAT 7, Module 1, Q19] (three parallel present-tense verbs)
In 1613, a prop cannon malfunctioned during a performance and ignited the Globe’s thatched roof. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q20] (parallel past-tense verbs malfunctioned … and ignited)

notes.title: Simple Present for General Facts, Processes, and “Today”
notes.en: Use the simple present (is, reach, survives, indicates) for three situations: (1) general facts that are always true (science, nature, definitions); (2) repeated processes that happen the same way every time (“Atoms travel… until they reach…”); and (3) statements about now, often signaled by time markers such as today, currently, nowadays, or now. Check the other verbs in the passage: if they are in the present (is unable, travel, are diverted), the blank is usually present too. Traps: a past date elsewhere in the passage (e.g., “in 1963”) does not control a sentence that begins with “Today.” Avoid had + past participle and will forms when nothing points to an earlier past or to the future.
notes.zh: 簡單現在式（is、reach、survives、indicates）用在三種情況：(1) 一般事實，永遠成立的科學、自然現象或定義；(2) 反覆發生的過程，每次都照同樣步驟進行（Atoms travel… until they reach…）；(3) 描述現在的狀態，常見時間標記有 today、currently、nowadays、now。解題時先看文章中其他動詞：若都是現在式（is unable、travel、are diverted），空格通常也用現在式。陷阱：文中別處出現過去年份（例如 in 1963），並不會影響以 Today 開頭的句子。沒有「更早的過去」或「未來」線索時，不要選 had + 過去分詞或 will。
examples: Today, the museum is able to display close to 30% of its collection. [Digital SAT 6, Module 1, Q27] (“Today” → simple present is)

The liquid metals in Earth’s core circulate constantly, and this circulation generates electrical currents that flow between Earth’s North and South magnetic poles. [Digital SAT 6, Module 2, Q28] (general scientific process → circulate, generates, flow)

notes.title: Simple Past for Completed Events and Specific Past Dates
notes.en: Use the simple past (affected, malfunctioned, discovered) for an action that started and finished in the past. The strongest clue is a specific past time: a year (“in 1613”), a decade (“during the 1930s”), or a phrase such as “in the eighteenth century,” “a decade later,” or “at that time.” The neighboring verbs usually confirm it (was, plagued, reached, ignited). Traps: the present perfect (has malfunctioned) cannot be used with a finished past time like “in 1613,” and will forms point to the future. The past perfect (had + past participle) is only needed when you must show that one past action happened before another past action (see Section 3).
notes.zh: 簡單過去式（affected、malfunctioned、discovered）用來表示在過去開始、也在過去結束的動作。最明顯的線索是明確的過去時間：年份（in 1613）、年代（during the 1930s），或 in the eighteenth century、a decade later、at that time 等片語。前後動詞通常也會是過去式（was、plagued、reached、ignited）。陷阱：現在完成式（has malfunctioned）不能和 in 1613 這種已結束的過去時間連用；will 則表示未來。只有在需要強調某個過去動作發生在另一個過去動作之前時，才用過去完成式（had + 過去分詞，見第 3 節）。
examples: In 1974, Mexican chemist Mario Molina and US chemist F. Sherwood Rowland discovered that chemicals called CFCs were harmful to the ozone layer. [Digital SAT 8, Module 1, Q28] (“In 1974” → discovered)
In 1966, Emmett Ashford became the first African American to umpire a Major League Baseball game. [Digital SAT 8, Module 2, Q22] (“In 1966” → became)

notes.title: Past Perfect: “By + Past Time” and the Earlier of Two Past Events
notes.en: The past perfect is had + past participle (had doubled, had laid, had won). Use it when an action was already complete before another point in the past. Two common signals: (1) by + a past time (“By the end of the 1990s, the organization had doubled…”; “By 1869, workers had laid…”); (2) two past events, where the earlier one takes had (“When Carter opened the tomb in 1922, robbers had already entered it”). Words such as already, previously, earlier, before, and by the time often appear. Traps: has/have + past participle (present perfect) connects the past to now, not to a past moment, so it is wrong after “by the end of the 1990s.”
notes.zh: 過去完成式的形式是 had + 過去分詞（had doubled、had laid、had won）。當一個動作在過去某個時間點之前就已經完成時使用。常見兩種線索：(1) by + 過去時間（By the end of the 1990s, the organization had doubled…；By 1869, workers had laid…）；(2) 兩件過去的事，較早發生的那件用 had（When Carter opened the tomb in 1922, robbers had already entered it）。already、previously、earlier、before、by the time 等字也常出現。陷阱：現在完成式 has/have + 過去分詞 是把過去連到現在，而不是連到過去某個時間點，所以在 by the end of the 1990s 後面不能用。
examples: Previously, only one other woman, Kathryn Bigelow of the United States, had been named best director at the Oscars, making Zhao the second woman and the first Asian woman to win the award. [Digital SAT 10, Module 1, Q29] (Bigelow’s award came before Zhao’s 2021 award)

In 1986, conceptual artist Sophie Calle asked twenty-three people, all of whom had been born without sight, to describe “their image of beauty” in rich detail. [Digital SAT 5, Module 1, Q26] (being born came before Calle asked them)

notes.title: Present Perfect: Since, For, and Up to Now
notes.en: The present perfect is has/have + past participle (has made, have studied). Use it for an action or situation that began in the past and continues up to now, or whose result still matters now. Key signals: since + starting point (“since 1990,” “since its launch”), for + length of time (“for more than a century”), ever since, so far, up to now, and in recent years. Compare: “In 1990, NASA launched Hubble” (finished past time → simple past) vs. “Since 1990, Hubble has made over a million observations” (from then until now → present perfect). Traps: had + past participle stops at a past point, not now; the simple past cannot go with “since” or “ever since” when the action continues to the present.
notes.zh: 現在完成式的形式是 has/have + 過去分詞（has made、have studied）。用來表示從過去開始、一直持續到現在的動作或狀態，或其結果到現在仍有影響。重要線索：since + 起點（since 1990、since its launch）、for + 一段時間（for more than a century）、ever since、so far、up to now、in recent years。比較：In 1990, NASA launched Hubble（已結束的過去時間 → 簡單過去式）vs. Since 1990, Hubble has made over a million observations（從當時到現在 → 現在完成式）。陷阱：had + 過去分詞 只延伸到過去某一點，不是到現在；動作持續到現在時，since、ever since 後面不能用簡單過去式。
examples: Archaeologists have known of the lines since the 1920s, when a researcher spotted some from a nearby foothill, and they have been studying the markings ever since. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q28] (“since the 1920s… ever since” → have known, have been studying)

For thousands of years, people in the Americas have used the bottle gourd, a large bitter fruit with a thick rind, to make bottles, other types of containers, and even musical instruments. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q18] (“For thousands of years” → have used)

notes.title: Tense Consistency and the Literary Present
notes.en: Keep verbs in the same tense unless the time actually changes. If a story about the past is told in the simple past (advised, suggested), the next event in the sequence also takes the simple past. There is one special rule: when you describe what happens inside a novel, poem, play, or film, use the literary present (connects, experiences, places), even if the book was written long ago or the story is set in the past. So look at the parallel verb in the sentence: in “Bình connects…, while Linda ______,” the blank must also be present. Traps: had + past participle and was + -ing change the time relationship without any reason; will forms move the story into the future.
notes.zh: 除非時間真的改變，否則動詞要保持同一時態。如果一段過去的故事是用簡單過去式敘述（advised、suggested），接下來同一串事件也要用簡單過去式。另有一條特別規則：描述小說、詩、劇本或電影裡發生的情節時，要用文學現在式（connects、experiences、places），即使作品寫於很久以前，或故事背景設在過去也一樣。所以要看句中平行的動詞：在 Bình connects…, while Linda ______ 中，空格也必須是現在式。陷阱：had + 過去分詞、was + -ing 會無故改變時間關係；will 則把情節移到未來。
examples: She places Thomas’s journey from the American South to the Midwest in the early 1900s within the larger context of the Great Migration. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q30] (literary present places, even though the events are set in the early 1900s)
As Zamboni’s machine moved along the rink’s surface, it first scraped off the top layer of ice. [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q26] (consistent simple past: moved… scraped)

notes.title: Find the True Subject: Ignore Prepositional Phrases and Interrupters (Singular Subjects)
notes.en: The verb must agree with its true subject, and the SAT hides that subject behind extra words. Cross out prepositional phrases (of the good spaces, between the two instruments), participial phrases (representing the mountain itself), and anything set off by commas or dashes (like the shape of each person’s ears). The noun right before the blank is often a trap noun: in “the shape of each statue’s ears ___ unique,” the subject is shape, not ears. Singular subject → singular verb (is, was, has, -s verb). Words such as each, every, either, neither, one, the number are singular too.
notes.zh: 動詞要和真正的主詞一致，而 SAT 常用多餘的字把主詞藏起來。請先刪去介系詞片語（of the good spaces、between the two instruments）、分詞片語（representing the mountain itself），以及用逗號或破折號隔開的插入語（like the shape of each person’s ears）。空格前最近的名詞常常是陷阱名詞：在 “the shape of each statue’s ears ___ unique” 中，主詞是 shape，不是 ears。單數主詞 → 單數動詞（is、was、has、動詞加 -s）。each、every、either、neither、one、the number 也都是單數。
examples: A harpsichord may look just like a piano, but the difference between the two instruments is easy to hear. [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q19] (subject “the difference,” not “instruments” → is)

The Lion Light system, developed by Kenyan inventor Richard Turere, consists of LED lights installed around the perimeter of livestock pastures. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q22] (singular “system” + interrupter → consists)

notes.title: Plural Subjects with Long Modifiers or Interrupters
notes.en: The reverse trap: the subject is plural, but a long modifier ends with a singular noun right before the blank (Vermeer, a painter…; Goldin, winner of…; the organism uses…). Find the head noun of the subject (objects, references, accomplishments, toxins, frameworks) and use a plural verb: are, were, have, base verb without -s (represent, reveal, attest, increase, underlie). Tip: bracket everything between the first comma and the matching comma, and read the subject straight into the verb.
notes.zh: 這是相反的陷阱：主詞是複數，但中間很長的修飾語最後剛好接一個單數名詞（Vermeer, a painter…；Goldin, winner of…；the organism uses…）。請找出主詞的中心名詞（objects、references、accomplishments、toxins、frameworks），並使用複數動詞：are、were、have、不加 -s 的原形動詞（represent、reveal、attest、increase、underlie）。小技巧：把第一個逗號到對應逗號之間的內容括起來，直接把主詞和動詞連起來讀。
examples: The forty-seven geothermal springs of Arkansas’ Hot Springs National Park are sourced via a process known as natural groundwater recharge, in which rainwater percolates downward through the earth—in this case, the porous rocks of the hills around Hot Springs—to collect in a subterranean basin. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q24] (plural “springs,” not “Park” → are)

Typically, underlines, scribbles, and notes left in the margins by a former owner lower a book’s value, but when the former owner is a famous poet like Walt Whitman, such markings, known as marginalia, can be a gold mine to literary scholars. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q21] (compound subject “underlines, scribbles, and notes” → lower)

notes.title: Gerund and Clause Subjects Are Singular; Titles of Works Are Singular
notes.en: Three kinds of subjects are always singular, even when they contain plural nouns: (1) a gerund phrase (Using one of these songs, landing on one of the good spaces); (2) a noun clause beginning with that, what, whether, how, why (That the center lay in North Dakota…, Whether the city was abandoned…); (3) the title of a work (a book, painting, or film), even if the title looks plural (A Sheaf Gleaned in French Fields, The Two Fridas). Each one names a single action, idea, or work, so it takes is, was, has, or an -s verb.
notes.zh: 有三種主詞永遠是單數，即使裡面含有複數名詞：(1) 動名詞片語（Using one of these songs、landing on one of the good spaces）；(2) 以 that、what、whether、how、why 開頭的名詞子句（That the center lay in North Dakota…、Whether the city was abandoned…）；(3) 作品名稱（書、畫作、電影），就算看起來像複數也一樣（A Sheaf Gleaned in French Fields、The Two Fridas）。它們都代表「一個」動作、想法或作品，所以要用 is、was、has 或加 -s 的動詞。
examples: Increasing the heat on an uncovered boiling pot of water does not increase the temperature of the water. [Digital SAT 7, Module 1, Q24] (gerund subject “Increasing the heat…” → does)

That the geographic center of North America lay in the state of North Dakota was conceded by all involved; establishing its precise coordinates proved more divisive. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q26] (noun-clause subject “That…” → was)

notes.title: Agreement in Relative Clauses: The Verb Agrees with the Antecedent
notes.en: In a relative clause (that, which, who + verb), the relative pronoun has no number of its own. It copies the number of its antecedent, the noun it refers to. Find that noun: a document that outlines (singular), structures that absorb (plural). Watch for one of the + plural noun + who/that: the verb usually agrees with the plural noun (one of the few astronauts who are). In many of whom, the subject many is plural. Relative clauses that state a definition or a lasting fact normally use the simple present.
notes.zh: 在關係子句（that、which、who + 動詞）中，關係代名詞本身沒有單複數，它跟著先行詞（它所指的名詞）走。先找出先行詞：a document that outlines（單數）、structures that absorb（複數）。注意 one of the + 複數名詞 + who/that：動詞通常跟那個複數名詞一致（one of the few astronauts who are）。many of whom 中的主詞 many 是複數。表示定義或持續事實的關係子句通常用簡單現在式。
examples: Stomata, tiny pore structures in a leaf that absorb gases needed for plant growth, open when guard cells surrounding each pore swell with water. [Digital SAT 1, Module 2, Q27] (antecedent “structures” (plural) → that absorb)

In 2011, these two writers joined forces to found CAKE Literary, a book packaging company that specializes in the creation and promotion of stories told from diverse perspectives for children and young adults. [Digital SAT 4, Module 2, Q21] (antecedent “company” (singular) → that specializes)

notes.title: Inverted Sentences (“Gone are…,” “Among X is/are…”), “Each One,” and “In Conjunction With / Along With”
notes.en: In an inverted sentence, the verb comes before the subject: Among the clubs’ leaders was Josephine St. Pierre Ruffin. Put the sentence back in normal order (Ruffin was among the leaders) to find the subject. Opening phrases such as Among…, In…, Gone…, Etched into… are not the subject. Each one of, each, and every are singular: each one of the couplets is. Finally, phrases like in conjunction with, along with, together with, as well as are only interrupters; they do not make a singular subject plural (only and does).
notes.zh: 倒裝句中動詞在主詞前面：Among the clubs’ leaders was Josephine St. Pierre Ruffin。先把句子改回正常語序（Ruffin was among the leaders）再找主詞。句首的 Among…、In…、Gone…、Etched into… 都不是主詞。each one of、each、every 都是單數：each one of the couplets is。最後，in conjunction with、along with、together with、as well as 只是插入語，不會把單數主詞變成複數（只有 and 才會）。
examples: In Death Valley National Park’s Racetrack Playa, a flat, dry lakebed, are 162 rocks—some weighing less than a pound but others almost 700 pounds—that move periodically from place to place, seemingly of their own volition. [Digital SAT 2, Module 1, Q27] (inverted; subject “162 rocks” → are)

In Marisol’s 1968 sculpture Mi Mama y Yo, gone are the types of pop culture references that made the Parisian-born Venezuelan American artist a star at the height of the pop art movement. [Digital SAT 10, Module 1, Q26] (inverted; subject “the types” → are)

notes.title: Agreement Combined with Tense and Parallel Verbs (has/have + Present Perfect)
notes.en: Many SAT items test two things at once: number and tense. First choose singular or plural, then choose the tense from clues in the passage. Words such as before, since, for, over the past…, ever since point to the present perfect: has + past participle for singular subjects, have + past participle for plural subjects. When one subject has several verbs in a series, all the verbs must be parallel: the same form and the same number (The map describes…, shows…, and includes…).
notes.zh: 許多 SAT 題目同時考兩件事：單複數和時態。先決定單數或複數，再從文中線索判斷時態。before、since、for、over the past…、ever since 等字表示要用現在完成式：單數主詞用 has + 過去分詞，複數主詞用 have + 過去分詞。當一個主詞後面接一連串動詞時，所有動詞必須平行：形式相同、單複數也相同（The map describes…, shows…, and includes…）。
examples: The versatile performer has appeared in everything from television commercials to action movies, but voice acting, specifically, has become a notable part of his career. [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q23] (singular subjects + present perfect → has)

A study published by Rice University geoscientist Ming Tang in 2019 offers a new explanation for the origin of Earth’s continents: geological structures called arcs, towering ridges that form when a dense oceanic plate subducts under a less dense continental plate, melts in the mantle below, and then rises and bursts through the continental crust above. [Digital SAT 4, Module 2, Q26] (singular “a dense oceanic plate” → parallel subducts, melts, rises, bursts)

notes.title: Pronoun–Antecedent Agreement: Singular (it / its; Collective Nouns)
notes.en: A pronoun must match its antecedent, the noun it refers to. A singular antecedent takes it / its / itself. On the SAT the antecedent is often far from the pronoun, or hidden behind an interrupter (dashes, commas, along with…). Cross out the interrupter and ask, “What does the pronoun point back to?” In “a given industry—water and electricity are two well-known examples—carries high costs,” the pronoun refers to industry (singular), not to examples. Collective nouns such as organization, committee, team, jury, museum, company, government, union name one group, so the SAT treats them as singular: the organization doubled its membership. A single animal species (the wood frog) is also singular. (Quick reminder: its is possessive; it’s = it is. See the punctuation handout for the apostrophe rules.)
notes.zh: 代名詞必須和它的先行詞（它所指的名詞）一致。單數先行詞要用 it / its / itself。SAT 常把先行詞放得離代名詞很遠，或用插入語（破折號、逗號、along with…）把它藏起來。請先刪去插入語，再問自己：「這個代名詞指的是哪個名詞？」例如 “a given industry—water and electricity are two well-known examples—carries high costs” 中，代名詞指的是 industry（單數），不是 examples。集合名詞如 organization、committee、team、jury、museum、company、government、union 代表「一個」團體，SAT 一律視為單數：the organization doubled its membership。單一物種（the wood frog）也是單數。（提醒：its 是所有格；it’s = it is，撇號規則請見標點符號講義。）
examples: Like other amphibians, the wood frog (Rana sylvatica) is unable to generate its own heat, so during periods of subfreezing temperatures, it survives by producing large amounts of glucose, a sugar that helps prevent damaging ice from forming inside its cells. [Digital SAT 4, Module 1, Q20] (singular “the wood frog” → its, it, its)
By the end of the 1990s, the organization had doubled its initial membership. [Digital SAT 2, Module 1, Q21] (collective noun “the organization” → its)

notes.title: Pronoun–Antecedent Agreement: Plural (they / their / them)
notes.en: A plural antecedent takes they / their / them / themselves. Plural antecedents include plural nouns (customers, table forks, two woodcuts) and compound subjects joined by and (Watson and Crick). The antecedent may be in an earlier sentence or may be renamed (table forks → the eating utensils), so read back until you find it. Watch for three traps: (1) a nearby singular noun that is not the antecedent; (2) vague pronouns such as this, that, some, one, you that do not match the antecedent; (3) choices that look alike but are contractions (they’re = they are, it’s = it is). The possessive of they is their.
notes.zh: 複數先行詞要用 they / their / them / themselves。複數先行詞包括複數名詞（customers、table forks、two woodcuts）以及用 and 連接的複合主詞（Watson and Crick）。先行詞可能在前一句，也可能換了說法（table forks → the eating utensils），所以要往前讀，找到它。注意三個陷阱：(1) 附近有一個單數名詞，但它不是先行詞；(2) this、that、some、one、you 等指代不清或不一致的代名詞；(3) 看起來很像的縮寫（they’re = they are，it’s = it is）。they 的所有格是 their。
examples: Larch trees, for instance, lose their needles every fall. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q27] (plural “Larch trees” → their)

Alternatively, contaminated soil can be detoxified via phytoremediation: plants that can withstand high concentrations of metals absorb the pollutants and store them in their shoots, which are then cut off and safely disposed of, preserving the health of the plants. [Digital SAT 4, Module 2, Q28] (plural “the pollutants” → them; plural “plants” → their)

notes.title: Reflexive Pronouns and Determiner–Noun Number (this / these, that / those)
notes.en: Use a reflexive pronoun (myself, itself, themselves…) when the object is the same thing as the subject: the barnacles attach themselves. A reflexive must match the subject in number: singular itself, plural themselves. If the object is someone or something different, use an ordinary object pronoun (them, it). Demonstratives must match in number too: this / that + singular noun, these / those + plural noun (these letters, this building). When this or that stands alone as a pronoun, it refers to one idea or event (making this the first time…). Those often replaces a plural noun in comparisons (the teeth in this layer and those in that layer).
notes.zh: 當受詞和主詞是同一個人或事物時，用反身代名詞（myself、itself、themselves…）：the barnacles attach themselves。反身代名詞必須和主詞單複數一致：單數用 itself，複數用 themselves。如果受詞是不同的人或事物，就用一般受格代名詞（them、it）。指示詞也要單複數一致：this / that + 單數名詞，these / those + 複數名詞（these letters、this building）。this 或 that 單獨當代名詞時，指的是一個想法或事件（making this the first time…）。those 常在比較句中代替複數名詞（the teeth in this layer and those in that layer）。
examples: When viewed up close, however, the portraits reveal themselves to be quilts, the stitching barely visible among the thousands of pieces of printed, microcut fabric. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q26] (subject “the portraits” = object → reflexive plural themselves)

In 2011, these two writers joined forces to found CAKE Literary, a book packaging company that specializes in the creation and promotion of stories told from diverse perspectives for children and young adults. [Digital SAT 4, Module 2, Q21] (plural noun “writers” → these)

notes.title: Dangling Modifiers I: The Subject Must Come Right After an Introductory -ing / -ed Phrase
notes.en: An introductory participial phrase (Wanting…, Featuring…, Named…, Woven…, Created…) has no subject of its own. It describes the first noun after the comma, which must be the doer (for -ing) or the thing acted on (for -ed). Ask: “Who or what is doing / receiving this action?” Then pick the choice that puts that noun right after the comma. If the phrase is followed by there, it, the award, $300, or a possessive that shifts the focus, the modifier is dangling. The same rule applies when a conjunction introduces the -ing phrase (since uncovering…, while studying…). Tip: passive voice (…was sponsored by the commission) usually creates the dangling error; the correct choice is often active.
notes.zh: 句首的分詞片語（Wanting…、Featuring…、Named…、Woven…、Created…）本身沒有主詞，它修飾的是逗號後的第一個名詞。這個名詞必須是動作的執行者（-ing 現在分詞）或承受者（-ed 過去分詞）。先問：「是誰／什麼在做（或被做）這個動作？」再選出把那個名詞放在逗號後面的選項。如果逗號後接的是 there、it、the award、$300，或是轉移焦點的所有格，就是懸垂修飾語（dangling modifier）。連接詞加 -ing 片語（since uncovering…、while studying…）也適用同樣規則。小技巧：被動語態（…was sponsored by the commission）常造成懸垂錯誤，正確選項通常是主動語態。
examples: Created by businessman William A.G. Brown, the saloon was known to offer elegant accommodations and an inclusive environment. [Digital SAT 6, Module 1, Q19] (the saloon was created → “the saloon” right after the comma)

Featuring jagged peaks of black ink surrounded by hazy swirls of blue and green paint, Zhang Daqian’s 1983 painting Panorama of Mount Lu is inspired by the tradition of qinglü shanshui, a type of Chinese landscape painting characterized by the use of blue and green hues to depict ethereal, otherworldly landscapes. [Digital SAT 7, Module 1, Q23] (the painting features the peaks → “Zhang Daqian’s 1983 painting” right after the comma)

notes.title: Dangling Modifiers II: Introductory Prepositional, Appositive, and “As a…” Phrases
notes.en: The same rule holds for other introductory modifiers. (1) Preposition + -ing (Upon recovering…, In assessing…, By reducing…, Despite being…): the noun after the comma must be the one that recovers, assesses, reduces, or is cheap. (2) Appositive phrase (a noun phrase that renames: A member of the Cherokee Nation, …; One of the few explorers…, …): the noun after the comma must be the same person or thing the appositive names. (3) “As a / As the…” phrase (As the librarian of Congress, …): the subject must be the person who holds that role. Wrong choices often begin with there is / it was, a possessive (Henry’s reign), a thing (the focus, the mitigation), or a passive verb.
notes.zh: 其他句首修飾語也適用相同規則。(1) 介系詞 + -ing（Upon recovering…、In assessing…、By reducing…、Despite being…）：逗號後的名詞必須是「康復、評論、減少、便宜」的那一方。(2) 同位語片語（重新命名的名詞片語：A member of the Cherokee Nation, …；One of the few explorers…, …）：逗號後的名詞必須和同位語指的是同一個人或事物。(3) “As a / As the…” 片語（As the librarian of Congress, …）：主詞必須是擔任該角色的人。錯誤選項常以 there is / it was、所有格（Henry’s reign）、事物（the focus、the mitigation）或被動語態開頭。
examples: As the fourteenth US librarian of Congress, Carla Hayden has many responsibilities. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q23] (“As the… librarian” → the person “Carla Hayden” right after the comma)

A member of the Cherokee Nation, Mary Golda Ross is renowned for her contributions to NASA’s Planetary Flight Handbook, which provided detailed mathematical guidance for missions to Mars and Venus. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q20] (appositive “A member…” renames “Mary Golda Ross”)

notes.title: Logical Comparisons and Modifier Placement
notes.en: A comparison must compare like with like: a trait with the same trait, a group with a similar group. Compare the shape of each statue’s ears with the shape of each person’s ears, not with each person. To avoid repeating the noun, use that of (singular) or those of (plural): the atomic arrangement of silica glass vs. that of alumina glass. An introductory comparison phrase (Compared to…, Unlike…, Like…) works like any modifier: the noun right after the comma must be the thing being compared. In Compared to that of alumina glass, that = the atomic arrangement, so the subject must be silica glass’s atomic arrangement. In general, place every modifier next to the word it describes.
notes.zh: 比較必須同類相比：特徵比特徵、群體比同類群體。要比較 the shape of each statue’s ears 和 the shape of each person’s ears，而不是和 each person 比。為了避免重複名詞，可以用 that of（單數）或 those of（複數）：the atomic arrangement of silica glass 對比 that of alumina glass。句首的比較片語（Compared to…、Unlike…、Like…）和其他修飾語一樣：逗號後的名詞必須是被比較的東西。在 Compared to that of alumina glass 中，that = the atomic arrangement，所以主詞必須是 silica glass’s atomic arrangement。總之，修飾語要緊靠它所修飾的字。
examples: Researchers studying the “terra-cotta army,” the thousands of life-size statues of warriors found interred near the tomb of Emperor Qin Shi Huang of China, were shocked to realize that the shape of each statue’s ears, like the shape of each person’s ears, is unique. [Digital SAT 9, Module 1, Q26] (shape compared with shape)

Hence, the shell is often incorrectly assumed to be an exoskeleton, a rigid outer casing like that of a crustacean or an insect, when in fact it is an endoskeleton, a part of the turtle’s internal bone structure, more akin to a spine or a pair of ribs. [Digital SAT 5, Module 1, Q30] (“that of” = the outer casing of a crustacean)

notes.title: Contrast: however, by contrast, in contrast, on the other hand, conversely
notes.en: A contrast transition tells the reader that the next sentence goes in the opposite direction from the one before it. Use it when two things are compared and they are different (wolves vs. dogs, lower vs. higher elevations), or when a new finding disagrees with an old belief. However is the general all-purpose contrast word. By contrast / In contrast compare two different subjects side by side. On the other hand presents a second, opposing side. Conversely means the exact reverse situation is true. The test: if you can mentally insert “but” between the two sentences, you need a contrast word.
notes.zh: 對比轉折詞（contrast）表示後一句和前一句的方向相反。當兩件事互相比較而且不同（例如：狼 vs. 狗、低海拔 vs. 高海拔），或是新的發現推翻舊的看法時，就用對比轉折詞。However 是最通用的「然而」；By contrast / In contrast 用來並排比較兩個不同的對象；On the other hand 提出「另一方面」相反的一面；Conversely 表示「正好相反」的情況。判斷方法：如果兩句之間可以放入「但是（but）」，就需要對比轉折詞。
examples: When viewed up close, however, the portraits reveal themselves to be quilts, the stitching barely visible among the thousands of pieces of printed, microcut fabric. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q26] (from afar they look like paintings; up close they are quilts)

With a pressure cooker pot, though, an airtight seal traps the vapor in the pot, creating pressure that allows the temperature of the water to increase past its boiling point. [Digital SAT 7, Module 1, Q24] (an uncovered pot vs. a pressure cooker)

notes.title: Concession, Correction, and Exception: still, nevertheless, nonetheless, though, even so, instead, rather, on the contrary
notes.en: These transitions are also “turning” words, but each has a special job. Concession words (still, nevertheless, nonetheless, even so, though) mean “even though the first sentence is true, the next thing still happens.” The second sentence is surprising given the first (Paris was ideal, still she wanted to leave). Exception is a kind of concession: the first sentence gives the usual rule (typically…) and the next gives the case that breaks it. Correction / replacement words (instead, rather, on the contrary) mean “not that — this.” The first sentence states something that is rejected, avoided, or false, and the second gives the replacement or the truth. Clue: look for words like avoid, not, might assume, typically before the blank.
notes.zh: 這類也是「轉折」詞，但各有特別的功能。讓步（concession）：still, nevertheless, nonetheless, even so, though 表示「雖然前一句是真的，但後面的事情仍然發生」，後一句在前一句的情況下顯得出乎意料（巴黎很理想，但她仍然想回印度）。例外（exception）也是一種讓步：前一句說一般情況（typically 通常），後一句說打破常規的例子。更正／取代（correction）：instead, rather, on the contrary 表示「不是那樣，而是這樣」——前一句的說法被否定、避免或是錯誤的，後一句提出取代的做法或真相。線索：空格前出現 avoid、not、might assume（可能以為）、typically 等字時，要特別注意。
examples: To humans, it does not appear that the golden orb-weaver spider uses camouflage to capture its prey; rather, the brightly colored arachnid seems to wait conspicuously in the center of its large circular web for insects to approach. [Digital SAT 2, Module 1, Q26] (correction: not camouflage — rather, waiting in plain sight)

Jetties can sometimes have the opposite effect, though; obstructing the natural flow of sand along the shore can lead to increased erosion in some areas. [Digital SAT 8, Module 2, Q26] (concession: jetties are built to prevent erosion, though they can cause it)

notes.title: Addition: in addition, additionally, moreover, furthermore, also
notes.en: An addition transition adds another point of the same kind to the list. The two sentences are parallel: both describe a function, a requirement, a concern, or a piece of evidence about the same topic, and the second is new, not a restatement or a detail of the first. In addition and additionally are neutral; moreover and furthermore add a point that builds an argument. Test: can you say “and another thing is…”? If yes, use an addition word. Trap: if the second sentence only explains or narrows the first, that is specification (Section 5), not addition; if it is one case of the first, that is example (Section 4).
notes.zh: 遞進／附加轉折詞（addition）是在清單中再加上同一類的另一點。兩句是平行的：都在講同一主題的功能、規定、顧慮或證據，而且第二句是新的資訊，不是換句話說，也不是前一句的細節。In addition、additionally 語氣中性；moreover、furthermore 常用於論證中「此外、而且」。判斷方法：能不能說成「還有另一點是…」？可以的話就選 addition。陷阱：如果第二句只是解釋或具體說明第一句，那是具體說明（Section 5）；如果第二句是第一句的一個例子，那是舉例（Section 4）。
examples: In addition, Zufall suggested selling the product under a child-friendly name: Play-Doh. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q20] (a second suggestion added to the first)

The first computerized spreadsheet, Dan Bricklin’s VisiCalc, improved financial recordkeeping not only by providing users with an easy means of adjusting data in spreadsheets but also by automatically updating all calculations that were dependent on these adjustments. [Digital SAT 1, Module 2, Q24] (addition inside one sentence: not only… but also)

notes.title: Example and Illustration: for example, for instance
notes.en: An example transition introduces one specific case of a general category named in the sentence before. Look for a general, plural noun phrase before the blank (hybrid works, surprising adaptations, not all conifer species) and then one named member of that group after the blank (The Emperor’s Babe, tadpole shrimp embryos, larch trees). For example and for instance mean the same thing. These words often appear in the middle of the sentence, right after the subject, set off by commas: Larch trees, for instance, lose… Test: can you say “one case of this is…”? If yes, use an example word. Trap: specifically adds precise detail about the same idea; for example gives one case out of many.
notes.zh: 舉例轉折詞（example）用來介紹前一句所說的一般類別中的一個具體例子。先找空格前的一般性、複數名詞片語（例如 hybrid works 混合作品、surprising adaptations 驚人的適應方式、not all conifer species 並非所有針葉樹），再看空格後是不是該類別中一個具名的成員（The Emperor’s Babe、蝌蚪蝦胚胎、落葉松）。For example 和 for instance 意思相同，常出現在句子中間、主詞後面，前後用逗號隔開：Larch trees, for instance, lose… 判斷方法：能不能說成「其中一個例子是…」？可以就選舉例。陷阱：specifically 是對同一件事提供更精確的細節；for example 是從許多情況中舉出一個例子。
examples: Her 2014 novel Boy, Snow, Bird, for instance, is a complex retelling of the story of Snow White, while her 2019 novel Gingerbread offers a delicious twist on the classic tale of Hansel and Gretel. [Digital SAT 2, Module 1, Q28] (examples of fiction inspired by the Brothers Grimm)

For instance, the colorful calico rockfish (Sebastes dalli) can survive for a little over a decade, while the rougheye rockfish (Sebastes aleutianus) boasts a maximum life span of about two centuries. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q21] (examples of how rockfish life spans vary)

notes.title: Specification and Elaboration: specifically, in particular, that is, in other words
notes.en: A specification transition takes a general or vague statement and makes it more precise. The sentence before the blank uses a broad word (broadly speaking, challenged prevailing views, extremely influential, certain grains, likely responsible), and the sentence after the blank tells exactly how, exactly what, or exactly which. Specifically gives the precise details; in particular singles out the exact items meant (certain grains → maize and wheat, in particular). That is and in other words restate the same idea in clearer or simpler words; they add no new information. Test: does the second sentence answer “How exactly?” or “Which exactly?” about the first? Then use specifically / in particular. Does it say the same thing again in plainer words? Then use that is / in other words.
notes.zh: 具體說明轉折詞（specification）把前一句籠統、模糊的說法變得更精確。空格前通常有概括性的字眼（broadly speaking 大致來說、challenged prevailing views 挑戰主流看法、extremely influential 影響極大、certain grains 某些穀物），空格後則說明到底如何、到底是什麼、到底是哪些。Specifically「具體來說」提供精確細節；in particular「尤其是、特別是」點出確切所指的項目（certain grains → maize and wheat, in particular）。That is 和 in other words「也就是說、換句話說」是用更清楚或更簡單的方式重述同一個意思，不增加新資訊。判斷方法：第二句是在回答第一句的「到底怎麼做？到底是哪些？」嗎？是的話選 specifically / in particular。第二句只是換句話再說一次嗎？那就選 that is / in other words。
examples: Specifically, an extra “leap second” (the 86,401st second of the day) is added whenever time based on the planet’s rotation lags a full nine-tenths of a second behind time kept by precise atomic clocks. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q23] (exactly how time measurements are adjusted)

Chondrites are stony meteorites that are undifferentiated—that is, their contents have not melted and separated into distinct layers. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q25] (“that is” defines the term undifferentiated)

notes.title: Emphasis and Confirmation: in fact, indeed, certainly
notes.en: An emphasis transition confirms and strengthens the claim just made. The first sentence makes a claim with an evaluative word (impressive, whimsical yet perplexing, extreme); the next sentence gives stronger evidence or a more extreme version of the same point. In fact often introduces a concrete fact or a surprising intensification (extreme → in fact, critics call them two different novels). Indeed means “yes, truly” and supports the claim with vivid proof. Certainly stresses that something is sure. The direction does not change, so contrast words are wrong. Test: can you say “and to prove it / and even more than that…”? Then use an emphasis word. Trap: emphasis vs. example — for example gives one case of a group; in fact / indeed strengthens a single claim.
notes.zh: 強調／證實轉折詞（emphasis）用來確認並加強前面剛說的論點。第一句通常含有評價性的字眼（impressive 令人印象深刻的、whimsical yet perplexing 奇幻又令人困惑的、extreme 極端的）；下一句則提出更有力的證據或程度更強的說法。In fact「事實上」常引出具體事實或更進一步的強調（差異極大 → 事實上，有些評論家認為是兩本不同的小說）。Indeed「的確、確實」用生動的證據支持前述說法。Certainly「當然、無疑」強調確定性。因為語意方向沒有改變，所以對比轉折詞是錯的。判斷方法：能不能說成「而且可以證明／甚至更…」？可以就選強調轉折詞。陷阱：強調 vs. 舉例——for example 是從一個群體中舉出一例；in fact / indeed 是加強單一論點。
examples: Indeed, contrary to the popular myth of the lone genius, theirs is not the first paradigm-shifting theory to have emerged from multiple scholars working in parallel. [Digital SAT 6, Module 1, Q30] (confirms that simultaneous discovery was no coincidence)

Literary agents estimate that more than half of all nonfiction books credited to a celebrity or other public figure are in fact written by ghostwriters, professional authors who are paid to write other people’s stories but whose names never appear on book covers. [Digital SAT 4, Module 1, Q19] (“in fact” stresses the surprising truth)

notes.title: Cause and Effect / Consequence: therefore, thus, as a result, consequently, for this reason, in turn
notes.en: A cause-and-effect transition tells the reader that the next sentence is a result of the one before it. The first sentence gives a cause (a process, a problem, a need); the second sentence gives what happens because of it. As a result, consequently, therefore, and thus all mean “because of this, …”. For this reason points back to a reason just stated (scientists need unchanging standards → for this reason, metrologists developed the SI). In turn shows a chain: A causes B, and B in turn causes C. Test: can you connect the two sentences with “so”? If yes, you need a cause-and-effect word. Trap: make sure the direction is right. If the second sentence gives the reason for the first (not the result), a result word is wrong.
notes.zh: 因果轉折詞（cause and effect）表示後一句是前一句造成的結果。前一句提出原因（一個過程、一個問題、一個需求），後一句說明因此發生了什麼。As a result、consequently、therefore、thus 都是「因此、結果」的意思。For this reason「基於這個原因」指回剛剛說過的理由（科學家需要不變的標準 → 因此計量學家制定了國際單位制）。In turn「進而、接著」表示連鎖反應：A 造成 B，B 又進而造成 C。判斷方法：兩句之間能不能放入「所以（so）」？可以的話就選因果轉折詞。陷阱：注意方向！如果第二句是第一句的原因而不是結果，就不能用表示結果的字。
examples: As a result, Parliament appointed Richard, Third Duke of York, who had a strong claim to the English throne, to rule as Lord Protector. [Digital SAT 1, Module 1, Q28] (Henry VI became unfit to rule → as a result, a Lord Protector was appointed)

Therefore, the researchers, knowing that dishes were sometimes named after their intended effects, theorized that the dish’s name, “unwinding,” referred to its function: to help ancient diners relax. [Digital SAT 4, Module 1, Q30] (the stew inspired calm → therefore, the researchers drew their theory)

notes.title: Conclusion and Inference: hence, thus, accordingly, as such, then, in conclusion
notes.en: A conclusion transition introduces an idea that the writer reasons out (infers) from the evidence before it. It is close to cause and effect, but the second sentence is often a claim, theory, or judgment rather than a physical result: siderophiles are more abundant than predicted → hence, material from asteroids almost certainly arrived later. Hence and thus mean “from this we can conclude.” Accordingly means “in response to this, people acted in a matching way.” As such means “because it is this kind of thing, …” (her work proves shared resources can be managed → as such, it rejects the “tragedy of the commons”). Then, placed mid-sentence between commas, means “in that case / so”, not time. In conclusion sums up a whole passage. Test: can you insert “so we can say that…”? If yes, use a conclusion word.
notes.zh: 結論／推論轉折詞（conclusion / inference）引出作者根據前面的證據推理出來的想法。它和因果很接近，但第二句常常是一個主張、理論或判斷，而不是實際發生的結果：親鐵元素比預測的多 → 因此（hence）可推論小行星物質幾乎一定是後來才到達地球的。Hence、thus「因此、由此可知」；accordingly「據此、相應地」表示人們針對這個情況做出相應的行動；as such「既然如此、就此而言」表示「因為它是這樣的東西，所以…」；then 放在句中、前後有逗號時，意思是「那麼、這樣看來」，不是表示時間；in conclusion「總之」用來總結整段內容。判斷方法：兩句之間能不能放入「所以我們可以說…」？可以的話就選結論轉折詞。
examples: As such, Ostrom’s work is a repudiation of the “tragedy of the commons,” the view that individuals will inevitably overexploit a finite shared resource if given unfettered access to it. [Digital SAT 8, Module 2, Q31] (her studies show shared resources can be managed → as such, her work rejects the old view)

Some members of the US Supreme Court have resisted calls to televise the court’s oral arguments, concerned that the participants would be tempted to perform for the cameras (and thus lower the quality of the discourse). [Digital SAT 9, Module 1, Q28] (“thus” = as a logical consequence)

notes.title: Sequence and Enumeration: first, second, next, then, finally, lastly, afterward, later
notes.en: A sequence transition puts steps or events in order. Look for order clues already in the passage: first, began, then, lastly, dates (1968… fifteen years… 1983). If the passage says first, the next step is second or next; if a step comes after then, the last step is finally. Enumeration words (first, second, third) count reasons or points in an argument (“First, the gold artifacts… Second, the massive effort…”). Finally can also mean “at last, after a long time” (they resubmitted the bill for fifteen years → finally, in 1983, it passed). Afterward and later say that one event happened after another. Test: are the sentences steps in a process or events on a timeline? Then choose the word that matches the position of the step: beginning, middle, or end.
notes.zh: 順序轉折詞（sequence）把步驟或事件按先後排列。先找文章中已有的順序線索：first（首先）、began（開始）、then（接著）、lastly（最後）、年份（1968…十五年…1983）。如果文章已經寫了 first，下一步就是 second 或 next；如果前面已經有 then，最後一步就用 finally。列舉（enumeration）的字（first, second, third）用來依序列出理由或論點（「第一，黃金文物…第二，巨大的工程…」）。Finally 也可以表示「經過很長時間，終於」（連續十五年重新提案 → 終於在 1983 年通過）。Afterward、later 表示一件事發生在另一件事之後。判斷方法：這幾句是不是一個過程的步驟，或時間軸上的事件？如果是，就依照該步驟的位置（開頭、中間、結尾）選字。
examples: Afterward, instead of downplaying the incident, Rocket Labs’ CEO publicly acknowledged what happened and apologized for the loss of the rocket’s payload, which had consisted of two satellites. [Digital SAT 4, Module 2, Q27] (first the rocket failed; afterward the CEO responded)
