Later, in 2017, Gomez created the show 80 Minutes Around the World as a platform for others to share stories about their immigration experiences. [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q27] (2014 → later, in 2017)

notes.title: Time: Simultaneity, Earlier Events, Past vs. Present, and Change over Time: meanwhile, previously, currently, today, increasingly
notes.en: Time transitions place an event on a timeline relative to another event. Check the verb tenses and dates around the blank. Meanwhile means “at the same time”: two different people or places, simultaneous actions (Ifemelu moves to the US; meanwhile, Obinze travels to London). Previously points to an earlier event; look for the past perfect had + V-pp (had been named). Today, currently, and now switch from the past to the present (before 2009… 5% → today… 30%; since the 1920s → currently… are aided). Increasingly shows a trend that grows over time; look for words like shift, trend, rise. Test: ask “When does the second sentence happen compared with the first?” Same time → meanwhile; earlier → previously; now → today / currently; more and more → increasingly.
notes.zh: 時間轉折詞把一個事件放在時間軸上，說明它和另一事件的時間關係。請看空格前後的動詞時態和年份。Meanwhile「同時、與此同時」：兩個不同的人或地點，同時發生的動作（Ifemelu 去美國；同時，Obinze 去倫敦）。Previously「先前、之前」指更早的事件，常搭配過去完成式 had + 過去分詞（had been named）。Today、currently、now「現今、目前」把時間從過去轉到現在（2009 年以前 5% → 今天 30%；從 1920 年代起 → 目前…are aided）。Increasingly「越來越多地」表示隨時間增長的趨勢，常見線索有 shift（轉變）、trend（趨勢）、rise（上升）。判斷方法：問自己「第二句發生的時間和第一句相比如何？」同時 → meanwhile；更早 → previously；現在 → today / currently；越來越 → increasingly。
examples: Today, Paik is considered the first video artist. [Digital SAT 1, Module 2, Q23] (1963 exhibition → today’s reputation)

Recently, engineer Erkka Frankberg of Tampere University in Finland used the chemical compound aluminum oxide to make a glassy solid that can withstand higher strain than silicate glass can before fracturing. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q27] (a recent development after a long-known problem)

notes.title: Similarity and Comparison: similarly, likewise, in the same way
notes.en: A similarity transition says that the second sentence describes the same kind of action or pattern as the first, but for a different person, place, or thing. The two sentences are parallel: activists in San Francisco sold tea → similarly, an activist in Los Angeles sold tea. Similarly, likewise, and in the same way all mean “the same is true of this second case.” Compare addition (Part 1): in addition adds another point about the same subject, while similarly shows a second subject doing the same thing. Compare example: for example gives one case of a group, but a similarity word links two equal cases. Test: can you say “the same thing happens with…”? If yes, use a similarity word. Trap: by contrast is its opposite (two subjects that differ).
notes.zh: 相似轉折詞（similarity）表示第二句描述的是同一類的行為或模式，只是主角換成不同的人、地點或事物。兩句是平行的：舊金山的社運人士賣茶 → 同樣地，洛杉磯的社運人士也賣茶。Similarly、likewise、in the same way 都是「同樣地；同理」。和附加（Part 1）比較：in addition 是就同一主題再加一點；similarly 是另一個主題做同樣的事。和舉例比較：for example 是從一個群體中舉出一例；相似轉折詞連接的是兩個對等的情況。判斷方法：能不能說成「同樣的事也發生在…」？可以就選相似轉折詞。陷阱：by contrast 正好相反，表示兩個主題不同。
examples: Like other amphibians, the wood frog (Rana sylvatica) is unable to generate its own heat, so during periods of subfreezing temperatures, it survives by producing large amounts of glucose, a sugar that helps prevent damaging ice from forming inside its cells. [Digital SAT 4, Module 1, Q20] (“Like other amphibians” shows similarity inside one sentence)

The Hawaiian sea slug, for example, not only tolerates Byropsis toxins but actually uses them for protection in the same way the algae does. [Digital SAT 6, Module 2, Q26] (“in the same way” links two subjects doing the same thing)

notes.title: Alternative, Replacement, Purpose, and Comment: alternatively, instead, more often, to that end, fittingly
notes.en: These transitions each do a special job. Alternative: alternatively offers another possible option for the same goal; both options are acceptable (remove the soil to a landfill; alternatively, clean it with plants). Replacement: instead and rather mean “not that — this”; the first idea is rejected or avoided. A related pattern is frequency: “X is rarely true. More often, Y.” Here more often tells what usually happens instead. Purpose: to that end (for that purpose) links a goal in the first sentence to the action taken to reach it (their goal was good parts for female friends → to that end, they created Six). Comment: fittingly (appropriately) gives the writer’s judgment that something is suitable (the event was named after its discoverer). Test: look for clue words before the blank: can be (option), avoid / rarely / not (replacement), goal / wanted (purpose), discoverer / named for (comment).
notes.zh: 這幾類轉折詞各有特別的功能。替代選項：alternatively「或者、另一種方式」提出達成同一目的的另一個可行選項，兩種方式都可以（把土壤運到掩埋場；或者用植物淨化）。取代：instead、rather「反而、而是」表示「不是那樣，而是這樣」，前面的做法被否定或避免。相關的句型是頻率對比：「X 很少是這樣。更常見的是 Y。」more often 說明通常的情況。目的：to that end「為此、為了達到這個目的」把前一句的目標和為達成目標所採取的行動連起來（她們的目標是讓女演員朋友有好角色 → 為此創作了音樂劇 Six）。評論：fittingly「恰如其分地、很合適地」表達作者認為某件事很恰當（以發現者的名字為這個事件命名）。判斷方法：找空格前的線索字：can be（選項）→ alternatively；avoid / rarely / not（避免／很少／不）→ instead / more often；goal / wanted（目標／想要）→ to that end；discoverer / named（發現者／命名）→ fittingly。
examples: Instead, researchers should use another word: “lyfe.” [Digital SAT 6, Module 1, Q26] (replacement: avoid “life” — use “lyfe” instead)

In order to prevent nonnative fish species from moving freely between the Mediterranean and Red Seas, marine biologist Bella Galil has proposed that a saline lock system be installed along the Suez Canal in Egypt’s Great Bitter Lakes. [Digital SAT 1, Module 2, Q25] (purpose: “in order to” states the goal of the action)

notes.title: Nonfinite Verbs Used Correctly (Participles, Infinitives, Absolute Phrases, Parallel Verbs)
notes.en: When a sentence already has its main verb, additional verb forms must be nonfinite. The SAT tests six patterns:
examples: Describes the subject or shows a result
…snow and ice cover, forcing the monkeys to hunt for marine animals.

notes.title: Verb Tense
notes.en: Tense questions are solved with time clues in the passage—dates, words like today, since, by the end of, now, and the tense of nearby verbs.
examples: General facts, repeated processes, current states; describing books, art, documents (literary present)
"Atoms...travel faster until they reach..."; "Today, Paik is considered..."; "Linda experiences..." (novel)

notes.title: Subject–Verb Agreement
notes.en: A verb must agree in number with its true subject—not with the noun closest to it. The SAT hides the subject in several ways:
examples: Long interrupter between subject and verb
Such objects, depicted in exquisite detail by Vermeer, a painter celebrated for his naturalism, [blank]

notes.title: Pronoun and Determiner Agreement
notes.en: A pronoun (it, they, them, this, these, its, their) must match the number of the noun it refers to (its antecedent), and the reference must be clear.
examples: a given industry… it often consists; became secretary-general, making this the first time
two woodcuts… they were exhibited; eighteen letters… These letters

notes.title: Modifiers: Dangling Modifiers and Logical Comparisons
notes.en: An introductory modifier (a phrase before the comma with no subject of its own) must be followed IMMEDIATELY by the noun it describes—the one doing (or receiving) the action.
examples: ✘ Dangling
✔ Correct

notes.title: Transitions: Choosing the Logical Connector
notes.en: Transition questions ("Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?") are logic questions, not grammar questions. Read the sentence BEFORE the blank and the sentence AFTER it, decide the relationship in your own words, then match a category.
examples: Additionally, In addition, Moreover, Furthermore, Also
Is this another point of the same kind?

notes.title: IC; however, IC.  /  IC. However, IC.
notes.en: however belongs to the second clause: the second clause contrasts with the first. Strong stop (; or .) BEFORE however, comma AFTER it.
notes.zh: however 開啟第二句

notes.title: IC, however; IC.
notes.en: however belongs to the first clause: that clause contrasts with the sentence before it, and the second clause explains or supports it. Ask: which clause is the contrast?
notes.zh: however 結束第一句（與前一句對比）

notes.title: Subject, however, verb.
notes.en: Only one independent clause. however just interrupts it, so it takes a pair of commas. A semicolon would cut the subject off from its verb.
notes.zh: however 插入同一句（成對逗號）

notes.title: IC, though.  /  IC, though; IC.  /  Subject, though, verb.
notes.en: As an adverb, though works exactly like however. Its favorite SAT position is the end of a clause: , though; or , though.
notes.zh: though = however（副詞）

notes.title: Though DC, IC.  /  IC, though DC.
notes.en: As a conjunction, though starts a dependent clause. Join it to the main clause with a comma (or nothing). Never put ; . : right before it: the though-clause becomes a fragment.
notes.zh: though = although（連接詞，不可接在分號/句號後）

notes.title: ✗ IC, however, IC.     ✗ Although X; however, Y.
notes.en: A comma cannot join two independent clauses, even with however/though in between (comma splice). And although/though already show contrast, so adding however is redundant.
notes.zh: 常見錯誤：逗號拼接、重複轉折

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 1 · Q19 (also SAT 10 M2 Q18)
items.passage: Public-awareness campaigns about the need to reduce single-use plastics can be successful, says researcher Kim Borg of Monash University in Australia, when these campaigns give consumers a choice: for example, Japan achieved a 40 percent reduction in plastic-bag use after cashiers were instructed to ask customers whether _______ wanted a bag.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun refers to the plural "customers," so "they" is required.

items.skill: Comma before participial phrase + quotation marks
items.passage: In ancient Greece, an Epicurean was a follower of Epicurus, a philosopher whose beliefs revolved around the pursuit of pleasure. Epicurus defined pleasure as “the absence of pain in the body and of trouble in the _______ that all life’s virtues derived from this absence.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Positing that all life’s virtues derived..." is a participial phrase (no subject, no finite verb) describing Epicurus, so it attaches to the main clause with a comma, placed inside the closing quotation mark. A semicolon or period (C, D) would leave the phrase as a fragment; a colon (B) is not used before a participial phrase.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 1 · Q21 (also SAT 9 M2 Q19)
items.passage: British scientists James Watson and Francis Crick won the Nobel Prize in part for their 1953 paper announcing the double helix structure of DNA, but it is misleading to say that Watson and Crick discovered the double helix. _______ findings were based on a famous X-ray image of DNA fibers, “Photo 51,” developed by X-ray crystallographer Rosalind Franklin and her graduate student Raymond Gosling.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: A plural possessive determiner is needed to show the findings belong to Watson and Crick: "Their." "They’re" and "It’s" are contractions; "Its" is singular.

items.passage: In 1937, Chinese American screen actor Anna May Wong, who had portrayed numerous villains and secondary characters but never a heroine, finally got a starring role in Paramount Pictures’ Daughter of Shanghai, a film that _______ “expanded the range of possibilities for Asian images on screen.”
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Critic Stina Chyn" is a title + name (restrictive appositive), so no commas around the name. No comma belongs between the subject and the verb "claims" or between "claims" and the quotation that serves as its content.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: In 1637, the price of tulips skyrocketed in Amsterdam, with single bulbs of rare varieties selling for up to the equivalent of $200,000 in today’s US dollars. Some historians _______ that this “tulip mania” was the first historical instance of an asset bubble, which occurs when investors drive prices to highs not supported by actual demand.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject "Some historians" needs a finite main verb. "Claim" is finite and plural; the other choices are nonfinite and leave the sentence without a main verb.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 1 · Q24 (also SAT 10 M2 Q25)
items.passage: Researchers studying magnetosensation have determined why some soil-dwelling roundworms in the Southern Hemisphere move in the opposite direction of Earth’s magnetic field when searching for _______ in the Northern Hemisphere, the magnetic field points down, into the ground, but in the Southern Hemisphere, it points up, toward the surface and away from worms’ food sources.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The second independent clause explains why the worms behave this way, so a colon is appropriate. B is a comma splice, D a run-on, C creates a confusing structure.

items.passage: Scientists believe that, unlike most other species of barnacle, turtle barnacles (Chelonibia testudinari) can dissolve the cement-like secretions they use to attach _______ to a sea turtle shell, enabling the barnacles to move short distances across the shell’s surface.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The barnacles ("they") attach their own bodies to the shell, so the object refers back to the subject and must be reflexive and plural: "themselves." "Them" would refer to some other group; "it/itself" are singular.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 1 · Q26 (also SAT 9 M1 Q20)
items.passage: The classic children’s board game Chutes and Ladders is a version of an ancient Nepalese game, Paramapada Sopanapata. In both games, players encounter “good” or “bad” spaces while traveling along a path; landing on one of the good spaces _______ a player to skip ahead and arrive closer to the end goal.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the gerund phrase "landing on one of the good spaces," which is singular (not "spaces"), so the singular "allows" is correct.

items.skill: Colon between independent clauses + adverb placement
items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 1 · Q27 (also SAT 8 M1 Q22)
items.passage: In 1943, in the midst of World War II, mathematics professor Grace Hopper was recruited by the US military to help the war effort by solving complex equations. Hopper’s subsequent career would involve more than just _______ as a pioneering computer programmer, Hopper would help usher in the digital age.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" is an adverb ending the first clause (set off by a comma). The second independent clause explains what "more than just equations" means, so a colon is appropriate. B is a comma splice; C makes "Though," start a fragment; D is a run-on.

items.passage: In 1453, English King Henry VI became unfit to rule after falling gravely ill. As a result, Parliament appointed Richard, Third Duke of York, who had a strong claim to the English throne, to rule as Lord Protector. Upon recovering two years later, _______ forcing an angered Richard from the royal court and precipitating a series of battles later known as the Wars of the Roses.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.D: it was Henry who resumed his reign,

items.explanation: The modifier "Upon recovering two years later" describes the person who recovered—Henry—so "Henry" must be the subject right after the comma. The reign didn't recover, and "it" is not Henry (dangling modifier).

items.passage: Although novels and poems are considered distinct literary forms, many authors have created hybrid works that incorporate elements of both. Bernardine Evaristo’s The Emperor’s Babe, _______ is a verse novel, a book-length narrative complete with characters and a plot but conveyed in short, crisp lines of poetry rather than prose.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The Emperor’s Babe is a specific instance of the "hybrid works" described in the previous sentence, so "for example" is logical.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 1 · Q30 (also SAT 8 M2 Q29)
items.passage: At two weeks old, the time their critical socialization period begins, wolves can smell but cannot yet see or hear. Domesticated dogs, _______ can see, hear, and smell by the end of two weeks. This relative lack of sensory input may help explain why wolves behave so differently around humans than dogs do: from a very young age, wolves are more wary and less exploratory.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Dogs differ from wolves in sensory development at two weeks, so "by contrast" is logical.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 1 · Q31 (also SAT 10 M2 Q30)
items.passage: Researchers Helena Mihaljević-Brandt, Lucía Santamaría, and Marco Tullney report that while mathematicians may have traditionally worked alone, evidence points to a shift in the opposite direction. _______ mathematicians are choosing to collaborate with their peers—a trend illustrated by a rise in the number of mathematics publications credited to multiple authors.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence describes a growing trend ("a shift"), so "Increasingly" is logical.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 2 · Q19 (also SAT 8 M1 Q19)
items.passage: When writing The Other Black Girl (2021), novelist Zakiya Dalila Harris drew on her own experiences working at a publishing office. The award-winning book is Harris’s first novel, but her writing _______ honored before. At the age of twelve, she entered a contest to have a story published in American Girl magazine—and won.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject "her writing" is singular, and "before" signals an experience up to now, so the singular present perfect "has been" is correct.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 2 · Q20 (also SAT 10 M1 Q20)
items.passage: The Alvarez theory, developed in 1980 by physicist Luis Walter Alvarez and his geologist son Walter Alvarez, maintained that the secondary effects of an asteroid impact caused many dinosaurs and other animals to die _______ it left unexplored the question of whether unrelated volcanic activity might have also contributed to the mass extinctions.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined with a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but." A lacks the comma, C is a run-on, D is a comma splice.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 2 · Q21 (also SAT 10 M1 Q22)
items.passage: In winter, the diets of Japanese macaques, also known as snow monkeys, are influenced more by food availability than by food preference. Although the monkeys prefer to eat vegetation and land-dwelling invertebrates, those food sources may become unavailable because of extensive snow and ice cover, _______ the monkeys to hunt for marine animals in any streams that have not frozen over.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Forcing the monkeys to hunt..." is a participial phrase describing the result of the snow cover; it attaches with a comma. A finite verb (A, D) would create a comma splice; "to force" suggests purpose, which is illogical.

items.skill: Direct question – word order & question mark
items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 2 · Q22 (also SAT 10 M2 Q19)
items.passage: Lucía Michel of the University of Chile observed that alkaline soils contain an insoluble form of iron that blueberry plants cannot absorb, thus inhibiting blueberry growth. If these plants were grown in alkaline soil alongside grasses that aid in iron solubilization, _______ Michel was determined to find out.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: This is a direct question that Michel wanted answered ("...could the blueberries thrive? Michel was determined to find out."). A direct question uses inverted word order and a question mark.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 2 · Q23 (also SAT 10 M2 Q21)
items.passage: In his 1963 exhibition Exposition of Music—Electronic Television, Korean American artist Nam June Paik showed how television images could be manipulated to express an artist’s perspective. Today, Paik _______ considered the first video artist.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Today" signals the present, so the simple present "is" is correct.

items.passage: The first computerized spreadsheet, Dan Bricklin’s VisiCalc, improved financial recordkeeping not only by providing users with an easy means of adjusting data in spreadsheets but also by automatically updating all calculations that were dependent on these _______ to VisiCalc’s release, changing a paper spreadsheet often required redoing the entire sheet by hand, a process that could take days.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Prior to VisiCalc’s release, changing a paper spreadsheet often required..." is a new independent clause, so a period is needed after "adjustments." B is a comma splice; A and D fuse the sentences and make "prior to" illogically modify "adjustments."

items.skill: Parallel verbs after a modal (would + base form)
items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 2 · Q25 (also SAT 8 M1 Q20)
items.passage: In order to prevent nonnative fish species from moving freely between the Mediterranean and Red Seas, marine biologist Bella Galil has proposed that a saline lock system be installed along the Suez Canal in Egypt’s Great Bitter Lakes. The lock would increase the salinity of the lakes and _______ a natural barrier of water most marine creatures would be unable to cross.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The verb is parallel with "increase" after the modal "would" (would increase...and create), so the base form "create" is required.

items.passage: Despite being cheap, versatile, and easy to produce, _______ they are made from nonrenewable petroleum, and most do not biodegrade in landfills.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: there are two problems associated with commercial plastics:
options.B: two problems are associated with commercial plastics:
options.C: commercial plastics’ two associated problems are that
options.D: commercial plastics have two associated problems:

items.explanation: The modifier "Despite being cheap, versatile, and easy to produce" describes the plastics, so "commercial plastics" must be the subject right after the comma. A starts with "there," B with "two problems," and C with "problems" (dangling modifier).

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 2 · Q27 (also SAT 9 M1 Q23)
items.passage: Stomata, tiny pore structures in a leaf that absorb gases needed for plant growth, open when guard cells surrounding each pore swell with water. In a pivotal 2007 article, plant cell _______ showed that lipid molecules called phosphatidylinositol phosphates are responsible for signaling guard cells to open stomata.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Plant cell biologist Yuree Lee" is a title + name (restrictive), so no commas. No punctuation belongs between the subject and the verb "showed."

items.passage: Small, flat structures called spatulae are found at the tips of the hairs on a spider’s leg. These spatulae temporarily bond with the atoms of whatever they touch. _______ spiders are able to cling to and climb almost any surface.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Spiders can cling to surfaces because the spatulae bond with atoms—a cause-and-effect relationship, so "As a result" is logical.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 2 · Q29 (also SAT 8 M1 Q27)
items.passage: In November 1934, Amrita Sher-Gil was living in what must have seemed like the ideal city for a young artist: Paris. She was studying firsthand the color-saturated style of France’s modernist masters and beginning to make a name for herself as a painter. _______ Sher-Gil longed to return to her childhood home of India; only there, she believed, could her art truly flourish.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Despite ideal conditions in Paris, she wanted to leave. "Still" signals this unexpected contrast.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 1 – Module 2 · Q30 (also SAT 9 M2 Q27)
items.passage: Before California’s 1911 election to approve a proposition granting women the right to vote, activists across the state sold tea to promote the cause of suffrage. In San Francisco, the Woman’s Suffrage Party sold Equality Tea at local fairs. _______ in Los Angeles, activist Nancy Tuttle Craig, who ran one of California’s largest grocery store firms, distributed Votes for Women Tea.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The Los Angeles activity is parallel to the San Francisco one (both sold tea for suffrage), so "Similarly" is logical.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 2 – Module 1 · Q20 (also SAT 8 M2 Q19)
items.passage: To survive when water is scarce, embryos inside African turquoise killifish eggs _______ a dormant state known as diapause. In this state, embryonic development is paused for as long as two years—longer than the life span of an adult killifish.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject "embryos" needs a main (finite) verb. "Enter" is a finite plural present-tense verb. The infinitive (B) and participles (C, D) cannot serve as the main verb, leaving the sentence incomplete.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 2 – Module 1 · Q21 (also SAT 8 M2 Q20)
items.passage: Formed in 1967 to foster political and economic stability within the Asia-Pacific region, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations was originally made up of five members: Thailand, the Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. By the end of the 1990s, the organization _______ its initial membership.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "By the end of the 1990s" marks an action completed before a specific past point, which requires the past perfect "had doubled."

items.passage: The intense pressure found in the deep ocean can affect the structure of proteins in fish’s cells, distorting the proteins’ shape. The chemical trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) counters this effect, ensuring that proteins retain their original _______ is found in high concentrations in the cells of the deepest-dwelling fish.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses ("The chemical TMAO counters..." and "TMAO is found...") must be separated. A period does this correctly. B is a run-on, C a comma splice, and D joins them with "and" but no comma and creates confusion with "configurations and TMAO" as a compound object.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 2 – Module 1 · Q23 (also SAT 10 M1 Q24)
items.passage: Food and the sensation of taste are central to Monique Truong’s novels. In The Book of Salt, for example, the exiled character of Bình connects to his native Saigon through the food he prepares, while in Bitter in the Mouth, the character of Linda _______ a form of synesthesia whereby the words she hears evoke tastes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The sentence uses the literary present ("connects") to describe events in novels. The parallel verb for Linda must also be simple present: "experiences."

items.passage: Inventor John Friedman created a prototype of the first flexible straw by inserting a screw into a paper straw and, using dental floss, binding the straw tightly around the _______ When the floss and screw were removed, the resulting corrugations in the paper allowed the straw to bend easily over the edge of a glass.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: There is one screw ("a screw"), so the singular possessive "screw’s" is needed. The threads belong to the screw and are plural but do not possess anything, so "threads" takes no apostrophe.

items.skill: Comma before supplementary noun phrase (appositive) + quotation marks
items.passage: In her analysis of Edith Wharton’s The House of Mirth (1905), scholar Candace Waid observes that the novel depicts the upper classes of New York society as “consumed by the appetite of a soulless _______ an apt assessment given that The House of Mirth is set during the Gilded Age, a period marked by rapid industrialization, economic greed, and widening wealth disparities.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "An apt assessment..." is a noun phrase that renames/comments on the preceding clause, so it is set off with a comma. In American style, the comma goes inside the closing quotation mark. A and B wrongly add "and" to a phrase that isn't a clause; D has no punctuation.

items.skill: Semicolon + conjunctive adverb between independent clauses
items.passage: To humans, it does not appear that the golden orb-weaver spider uses camouflage to capture its _______ the brightly colored arachnid seems to wait conspicuously in the center of its large circular web for insects to approach. Researcher Po Peng of the University of Melbourne has explained that the spider’s distinctive coloration may in fact be part of its appeal.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined here. "Rather" is a conjunctive adverb that begins the second clause, so a semicolon goes before it and a comma after it. A is a comma splice; B is a run-on; C puts the semicolon in the wrong place.

items.passage: In Death Valley National Park’s Racetrack Playa, a flat, dry lakebed, are 162 rocks—some weighing less than a pound but others almost 700 pounds—that move periodically from place to place, seemingly of their own volition. Racetrack-like trails in the _______ mysterious migration.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: There is one playa, so "playa’s" (singular possessive) is correct. The migration belongs to the 162 rocks, so the plural possessive "rocks’" is required.

items.skill: No punctuation between subject and verb / restrictive appositive
items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 2 – Module 1 · Q28 (also SAT 9 M2 Q22)
items.passage: In crafting her fantasy fiction, Nigerian-born British author Helen Oyeyemi has drawn inspiration from the classic nineteenth-century fairy tales of the Brothers Grimm. Her 2014 novel Boy, Snow, Bird, for instance, is a complex retelling of the story of Snow White, while her 2019 novel _______ offers a delicious twist on the classic tale of Hansel and Gretel.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Her 2019 novel Gingerbread" is the subject of the clause and "offers" is its verb. No punctuation should separate a subject from its verb, and the title is an essential (restrictive) identifier.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: For thousands of years, people in the Americas _______ the bottle gourd, a large bitter fruit with a thick rind, to make bottles, other types of containers, and even musical instruments. Oddly, there is no evidence that any type of bottle gourd is native to the Western Hemisphere; either the fruit or its seeds must have somehow been carried from Asia or Africa.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject "people" needs a finite main verb. "Have used" is finite, and the present perfect fits an action continuing "for thousands of years." A, C, and D are nonfinite and leave the sentence without a main verb.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 2 – Module 2 · Q19 (also SAT 10 M1 Q23)
items.passage: While many video game creators strive to make their graphics ever more _______ others look to the past, developing titles with visuals inspired by the “8-bit” games of the 1980s and 1990s. (The term “8-bit” refers to a console whose processor could only handle eight bits of data at once.)
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "While…lifelike" is an introductory dependent clause, so a comma separates it from the main clause "others look to the past." Adding "but" (A, D) is wrong because "while" already links the clauses; B lacks the needed comma.

items.passage: In the 1950s, a man named Joseph McVicker was struggling to keep his business afloat when his sister-in-law Kay Zufall advised him to repurpose the company’s product, a nontoxic, clay-like substance for removing soot from wallpaper, as a modeling putty for kids. In addition, Zufall _______ selling the product under a child-friendly name: Play-Doh.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The story is told in the simple past ("advised"). Zufall's suggestion is another completed past action in sequence, so the simple past "suggested" is consistent.

items.passage: Beatrix Potter is perhaps best known for writing and illustrating children’s books such as The Tale of Peter Rabbit (1902), but she also dedicated herself to mycology, the study of _______ more than 350 paintings of the fungal species she observed in nature and submitting her research on spore germination to the Linnean Society of London.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Producing...and submitting..." is a participial phrase describing how Potter dedicated herself, so it is joined to the main clause with a comma. A semicolon (A) or period (B) would leave the phrase as an incomplete sentence; C makes it seem the fungi are producing paintings.

items.passage: In assessing the films of Japanese director Akira Kurosawa, _______ have missed his equally deep engagement with Japanese artistic traditions such as Noh theater.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: many critics have focused on Kurosawa’s use of Western literary sources but
options.B: Kurosawa’s use of Western literary sources has been the focus of many critics, who
options.C: there are many critics who have focused on Kurosawa’s use of Western literary sources, but they
options.D: the focus of many critics has been on Kurosawa’s use of Western literary sources; they

items.explanation: The introductory modifier "In assessing the films..." must be followed immediately by the people doing the assessing: "many critics." Only A places "many critics" right after the modifier; the others make "Kurosawa’s use," "there," or "the focus" do the assessing (dangling modifier).

items.passage: Joshua Hinson, director of the language revitalization program of the Chickasaw Nation in Oklahoma, helped produce the world’s first Indigenous-language instructional app, Chickasaw _______ Chickasaw TV, in 2010; and a Rosetta Stone language course in Chickasaw, in 2015.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: Basic; in 2009, an online television network;
options.B: Basic; in 2009, an online television network,
options.C: Basic, in 2009; an online television network,
options.D: Basic, in 2009, an online television network,

items.explanation: This is a list of three items that contain internal commas, so the items are separated by semicolons. Item 1 is "the...app, Chickasaw Basic, in 2009"; the semicolon comes after "2009," and item 2 begins "an online television network, Chickasaw TV, in 2010."

items.skill: Paired dashes around a supplementary element
items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 2 – Module 2 · Q24 (also SAT 8 M2 Q23)
items.passage: The forty-seven geothermal springs of Arkansas’ Hot Springs National Park are sourced via a process known as natural groundwater recharge, in which rainwater percolates downward through the earth—in this case, the porous rocks of the hills around Hot _______ collect in a subterranean basin.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The supplementary phrase "in this case, the porous rocks...Hot Springs" opens with a dash, so it must close with a matching dash before the sentence resumes ("percolates downward through the earth...to collect").

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 2 – Module 2 · Q25 (also SAT 8 M2 Q24)
items.passage: Over twenty years ago, in a landmark experiment in the psychology of choice, professor Sheena Iyengar set up a jam-tasting booth at a grocery store. The number of jams available for tasting _______ some shoppers had twenty-four different options, others only six. Interestingly, the shoppers with fewer jams to choose from purchased more jam.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The second part explains how the number varied, so a colon (which introduces an explanation after an independent clause) is correct. B is a comma splice; C and D create an illogical/garbled structure with "while" followed by another comma-joined clause.

items.skill: Semicolons in a complex series + appositive comma
items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 2 – Module 2 · Q26 (also SAT 8 M2 Q25)
items.passage: Nigerian author Buchi Emecheta’s celebrated literary oeuvre includes The Joys of Motherhood, a novel about the changing roles of women in 1950s _______ a television play about the private struggles of a newlywed couple in Nigeria; and Head Above Water, her autobiography.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The list items contain internal commas, so semicolons separate them (matching the later "; and Head Above Water"). Within item 2, a comma sets off the appositive "a television play..." after the title.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 2 – Module 2 · Q27 (also SAT 9 M1 Q27)
items.passage: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie’s 2013 novel Americanah chronicles the divergent experiences of Ifemelu and Obinze, a young Nigerian couple, after high school. Ifemelu moves to the United States to attend a prestigious university. _______ Obinze travels to London, hoping to start a career there. However, frustrated with the lack of opportunities, he soon returns to Nigeria.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The two events happen at the same time to two different characters. "Meanwhile" signals simultaneous action.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 2 – Module 2 · Q28 (also SAT 10 M1 Q28)
items.passage: Organisms have evolved a number of surprising adaptations to ensure their survival in adverse conditions. Tadpole shrimp (Triops longicaudatus) embryos, _______ can pause development for over ten years during extended periods of drought.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Tadpole shrimp embryos are a specific instance of the "surprising adaptations" mentioned in the first sentence, so "for example" is logical.

items.passage: In 1933, the Twentieth Amendment to the US Constitution was ratified. The amendment mandates that presidential inaugurations be held on January 20, approximately ten weeks after the November election. _______ this amendment requires newly elected US senators and representatives to be sworn into their respective offices on January 3.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence adds a second, separate requirement of the amendment, so "In addition" (addition) is correct.

items.passage: In her poetry collection Thomas and Beulah, Rita Dove interweaves the titular characters’ personal stories with broader historical narratives. She places Thomas’s journey from the American South to the Midwest in the early 1900s within the larger context of the Great Migration. _______ Dove sets events from Beulah’s personal life against the backdrop of the US Civil Rights Movement.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Dove does the same thing for Beulah that she did for Thomas (placing a personal story in a historical context). "Similarly" signals this parallel.

items.skill: Finite verb in a relative clause
items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 1 · Q20 (also SAT 9 M1 Q19)
items.passage: A member of the Cherokee Nation, Mary Golda Ross is renowned for her contributions to NASA’s Planetary Flight Handbook, which _______ detailed mathematical guidance for missions to Mars and Venus.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The relative clause "which ___ detailed mathematical guidance" needs a finite verb. "Provided" is finite; the other choices are nonfinite and leave the clause without a verb.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 1 · Q21 (also SAT 10 M1 Q21)
items.passage: Typically, underlines, scribbles, and notes left in the margins by a former owner lower a book’s _______ when the former owner is a famous poet like Walt Whitman, such markings, known as marginalia, can be a gold mine to literary scholars.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses with contrasting ideas are joined; a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but" is correct. B is a run-on, C a comma splice, D lacks the comma before "but."

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 1 · Q22 (also SAT 8 M2 Q21)
items.passage: After the United Kingdom began rolling out taxes equivalent to a few cents on single-use plastic grocery bags in 2011, plastic-bag consumption decreased by up to ninety _______ taxes are subject to what economists call the “rebound effect”: as the change became normalized, plastic-bag use started to creep back up.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses must be separated; a period does this. A is a comma splice, D is a run-on, and B needs a comma before "and."

items.skill: No punctuation before essential dependent clause
items.passage: As British scientist Peter Whibberley has observed, “the Earth is not a very good timekeeper.” Earth’s slightly irregular rotation rate means that measurements of time must be periodically adjusted. Specifically, an extra “leap second” (the 86,401st second of the day) is _______ time based on the planet’s rotation lags a full nine-tenths of a second behind time kept by precise atomic clocks.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Whenever time...lags" is an essential dependent clause telling when the second is added, so no punctuation is needed. B and C would leave the dependent clause as a fragment; A inserts an unnecessary comma.

items.passage: Bengali author Toru Dutt’s A Sheaf Gleaned in French Fields (1876), a volume of English translations of French poems, _______ scholars’ understanding of the transnational and multilingual contexts in which Dutt lived and worked.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the singular book title "A Sheaf Gleaned in French Fields" (ignore the appositive and "poems"). It takes the singular verb "has enhanced."

items.skill: Commas around an interrupting conjunctive adverb
items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 1 · Q25 (also SAT 9 M1 Q22)
items.passage: Journalists have dubbed Gil Scott-Heron the “godfather of rap,” a title that has appeared in hundreds of articles about him since the 1990s. Scott-Heron himself resisted the godfather _______ feeling that it didn’t encapsulate his devotion to the broader African American blues music tradition as well as “bluesologist,” the moniker he preferred.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "However" interrupts one sentence (the participial phrase "feeling that..." is not an independent clause), so it is set off by a pair of commas. D uses a semicolon, which would require an independent clause after it.
items.mk: [1|Scott-Heron himself resisted the godfather nickname]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [p|feeling that it didn’t encapsulate his devotion to the broader African American blues music tradition as well as “bluesologist,” the moniker he preferred].

why.C: What follows is a participial phrase (feeling…), not a clause. Still one sentence → paired commas.
why.B: A semicolon needs an IC after it; “feeling…” is not one.
why.D: Same problem: no IC after the semicolon.

items.passage: From afar, African American fiber artist Bisa Butler’s portraits look like paintings, their depictions of human faces, bodies, and clothing so intricate that it seems only a fine brush could have rendered them. When viewed up close, however, the portraits reveal themselves to be _______ stitching barely visible among the thousands of pieces of printed, microcut fabric.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "The stitching barely visible..." is an absolute phrase (no finite verb), so it attaches to the main clause with a comma. A, C, and D treat it as an independent clause, which it is not.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 1 · Q27 (also SAT 10 M2 Q26)
items.passage: Most conifers (trees belonging to the phylum Coniferophyta) are evergreen. That is, they keep their green leaves or needles year-round. However, not all conifer species are evergreen. Larch trees, _______ lose their needles every fall.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Larch trees are an example of a conifer that is not evergreen, so "for instance" is logical.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 2 · Q18 (also SAT 10 M2 Q20)
items.passage: Atoms in a synchrotron, a type of circular particle accelerator, travel faster and faster until they _______ a desired energy level, at which point they are diverted to collide with a target, smashing the atoms.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The text describes a general, repeated process in the simple present ("travel," "are diverted"), so the simple present "reach" is consistent.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: Even though bats prefer very sweet nectar, the plants that attract them have evolved to produce nectar that is only moderately sweet. A recent study _______ why: making sugar is energy-intensive, and it is more advantageous for plants to make a large amount of low-sugar nectar than a small amount of high-sugar nectar.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject "A recent study" needs a finite main verb: "explains." The other choices are nonfinite.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 2 · Q20 (also SAT 10 M2 Q22)
items.passage: Former First Lady of the United States Eleanor Roosevelt and Indian activist and educator Hansa Mehta were instrumental in drafting the United Nations’ Universal Declaration of Human Rights, a document that _______ the basic freedoms to which all people are entitled.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The relative pronoun "that" refers to the singular "a document," so the singular verb "outlines" is required. The present tense suits a document that still exists.

items.passage: The life spans of rockfish vary greatly by species. For instance, the colorful calico rockfish (Sebastes dalli) can survive for a little over a _______ the rougheye rockfish (Sebastes aleutianus) boasts a maximum life span of about two centuries.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "While the rougheye rockfish boasts..." is a dependent clause showing contrast, so it is joined to the main clause with a comma. A period or semicolon (B, C) would leave it as a fragment; a colon (A) is not used before a dependent clause here.

items.skill: Comma after introductory phrase; no commas in essential phrase
items.passage: The Lion Light system, developed by Kenyan inventor Richard Turere, consists of LED lights installed around the perimeter of livestock pastures. Powered with _______ the blinking LEDs keep lions away at night, thus protecting the livestock without risking harm to the endangered lions.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: energy collected, by solar panels, during the day
options.B: energy collected by solar panels during the day
options.C: energy collected by solar panels during the day,
options.D: energy, collected by solar panels during the day,

items.explanation: The introductory phrase "Powered with energy collected by solar panels during the day" must be followed by a comma before the main clause. Its internal parts are essential, so no internal commas are needed.

items.passage: Materials scientist Marie-Agathe Charpagne and her colleagues believed they could improve on the multicomponent alloy NiCoCr, an equal-proportions mixture of nickel (Ni), cobalt (Co), and chromium (Cr), by replacing chromium with ruthenium _______ the alloy that resulted, NiCoRu, turned out to be an unsuitable replacement for NiCoCr.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two contrasting independent clauses are joined with a comma plus "but." A is a run-on, B lacks the comma, C is a comma splice.

items.passage: The Progressive Era in the United States witnessed the rise of numerous Black women’s clubs, local organizations that advocated for racial and gender equality. Among the clubs’ leaders _______ Josephine St. Pierre Ruffin, founder of the Women’s Era Club of Boston.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The sentence is inverted; the true subject is the singular "Josephine St. Pierre Ruffin" (not "leaders"). The historical context calls for past tense, so "was."

items.passage: Based on genetic evidence, archaeologists have generally agreed that reindeer domestication began in the eleventh century CE. However, since uncovering fragments of a 2,000-year-old reindeer training harness in northern Siberia, _______ may have begun much earlier.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: researcher Robert Losey has argued that domestication
options.B: researcher Robert Losey’s argument is that domestication
options.C: domestication, researcher Robert Losey has argued,
options.D: the argument researcher Robert Losey has made is that domestication

items.explanation: The modifier "since uncovering fragments..." describes a person who uncovered them, so the subject right after the comma must be "researcher Robert Losey." The other choices create dangling modifiers (an argument or domestication did not uncover anything).

items.passage: Hegra is an archaeological site in present-day Saudi Arabia and was the second largest city of the Nabataean Kingdom (fourth century BCE to first century CE). Archaeologist Laila Nehmé recently traveled to Hegra to study its ancient _______ into the rocky outcrops of a vast desert, these burial chambers seem to blend seamlessly with nature.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Built into the rocky outcrops..." introduces the second independent clause ("these burial chambers seem..."). A period separates the two sentences. B–D create a run-on/comma splice or misattach the modifier.

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 2 · Q27 (also SAT 9 M2 Q24)
items.passage: When external forces are applied to common glass made from silicates, energy builds up around minuscule defects in the material, resulting in fractures. Recently, engineer Erkka Frankberg of Tampere University in Finland used the chemical _______ to make a glassy solid that can withstand higher strain than silicate glass can before fracturing.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Aluminum oxide" is an essential (restrictive) appositive identifying which compound; it takes no commas. Nothing should separate the object from "to make."

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 2 · Q28 (also SAT 8 M2 Q28)
items.passage: Etched into Peru’s Nazca Desert are line drawings so large that they can only be fully seen from high above. Archaeologists have known of the lines since the 1920s, when a researcher spotted some from a nearby foothill, and they have been studying the markings ever since. _______ archaeologists’ efforts are aided by drones that capture high-resolution aerial photographs of the lines.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text moves from past study (since the 1920s) to present practice ("are aided"). "Currently" marks this time shift.

items.passage: Archaeologist Sue Brunning explains why the seventh-century ship burial site at Sutton Hoo in England was likely the tomb of a king. First, the gold artifacts inside the ship suggest that the person buried with them was a wealthy and respected leader. _______ the massive effort required to bury the ship would likely only have been undertaken for a king.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text lists reasons beginning with "First"; the next reason is introduced by "Second."

items.origin: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 2 · Q30 (also SAT 9 M1 Q29)
items.passage: The more diverse and wide ranging an animal’s behaviors, the larger and more energy demanding the animal’s brain tends to be. _______ from an evolutionary perspective, animals that perform only basic actions should allocate fewer resources to growing and maintaining brain tissue. The specialized subtypes of ants within colonies provide an opportunity to explore this hypothesis.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence is a logical conclusion drawn from the first, so "Thus" (cause–effect) fits.

items.passage: When designing costumes for film, American artist Suttirat Larlarb typically custom fits the garments to each actor. _______ for the film Sunshine, in which astronauts must reignite a dying Sun, she designed a golden spacesuit and had a factory reproduce it in a few standard sizes; lacking a tailor-made quality, the final creations reflected the ungainliness of actual spacesuits.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Standard-size spacesuits contrast with her usual custom-fitting practice. "Nevertheless" signals this exception/contrast.

items.skill: Possessive of irregular plural + plural noun
items.passage: Literary agents estimate that more than half of all nonfiction books credited to a celebrity or other public figure are in fact written by ghostwriters, professional authors who are paid to write other _______ but whose names never appear on book covers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "People" is already plural, so its possessive is "people’s." "Stories" is a plural noun that owns nothing, so it takes no apostrophe.

items.passage: Like other amphibians, the wood frog (Rana sylvatica) is unable to generate its own heat, so during periods of subfreezing temperatures, it _______ by producing large amounts of glucose, a sugar that helps prevent damaging ice from forming inside its cells.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The text states a general scientific fact in the present tense ("is unable"), so the simple present "survives" is consistent.

items.passage: After a spate of illnesses as a child, Wilma Rudolph was told she might never walk again. Defying all odds, Rudolph didn’t just walk, she _______ the 1960 Summer Olympics in Rome, she won both the 100- and 200-meter dashes and clinched first place for her team in the 4 ×100-meter relay, becoming the first US woman to win three gold medals in a single Olympics.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "During the 1960 Summer Olympics in Rome, she won..." is a new independent clause, so a period is needed after "fast." The other choices fuse the two sentences.

items.passage: In many of her landscape paintings from the 1970s and 1980s, Lebanese American artist Etel Adnan worked to capture the essence of California’s fog-shrouded Mount Tamalpais region through abstraction, using splotches of color to represent the area’s features. Interestingly, the triangle representing the mountain itself _______ among the few defined figures in her paintings.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the singular "the triangle" (ignore "representing the mountain itself"), so the singular "is" is needed. Present tense suits describing existing paintings.

items.passage: Seneca sculptor Marie Watt’s blanket art comes in a range of shapes and sizes. In 2004, Watt sewed strips of blankets together to craft a 10-by-13-inch _______ in 2014, she arranged folded blankets into two large stacks and then cast them in bronze, creating two curving 18-foot-tall blue-bronze pillars.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses ("In 2004, Watt sewed..." / "in 2014, she arranged...") are joined without a conjunction, so a semicolon is required. C and D are comma splices; A is a run-on.

items.passage: African American Percy Julian was a scientist and entrepreneur whose work helped people around the world to see. Named in 1999 as one of the greatest achievements by a US chemist in the past hundred years, _______ led to the first mass-produced treatment for glaucoma.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: Julian synthesized the alkaloid physostigmine in 1935; it
options.B: in 1935 Julian synthesized the alkaloid physostigmine, which
options.C: Julian’s 1935 synthesis of the alkaloid physostigmine
options.D: the alkaloid physostigmine was synthesized by Julian in 1935 and

items.explanation: The introductory modifier says something was "named...as one of the greatest achievements." The achievement is Julian’s synthesis, so "Julian’s 1935 synthesis..." must come right after the comma. The other choices make Julian or the alkaloid the "achievement" (dangling modifier).

items.passage: The Arctic-Alpine Botanic Garden in Norway and the Jardim Botânico of Rio de Janeiro in Brazil are two of many botanical gardens around the world dedicated to growing diverse plant _______ fostering scientific research; and educating the public about plant conservation.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: This is a series of three items separated by semicolons ("; and educating..."). Item 1 contains an internal comma ("species, both native and nonnative"), so it ends with a semicolon.

items.passage: Sociologist Alton Okinaka sits on the review board tasked with adding new sites to the Hawai‘i Register of Historic Places, which includes Pi‘ilanihale Heiau and the ‘Ōpaeka‘a Road Bridge. Okinaka doesn’t make such decisions _______ all historical designations must be approved by a group of nine other experts from the fields of architecture, archaeology, history, and Hawaiian culture.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "However" belongs to the first clause (it contrasts with the previous sentence), so it is set off with a comma and followed by a semicolon that separates the two independent clauses. B would link "however" illogically to the second clause.
items.mk: [1|Okinaka doesn’t make such decisions single-handedly]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨;⟩ [2|all historical designations must be approved by a group of nine other experts]…

why.A: The contrast is sentence 1 vs IC1 (he sits on the board ↔ but doesn't decide alone). IC2 explains IC1, so however stays with IC1.
why.B: Puts however with IC2, but IC2 agrees with IC1 — no contrast there.
why.D: Run-on; no punctuation between the ICs.

items.passage: In 1968, US Congressman John Conyers introduced a bill to establish a national holiday in honor of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. The bill didn’t make it to a vote, but Conyers was determined. He teamed up with Shirley Chisholm, the first Black woman to be elected to Congress, and they resubmitted the bill every session for the next fifteen years. _______ in 1983, the bill passed.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: After fifteen years of effort, the bill passed at last. "Finally" signals the end of a long sequence.

items.passage: Geoscientists have long considered Hawaii’s Mauna Loa volcano to be Earth’s largest shield volcano by volume, measuring approximately 74,000 cubic kilometers. _______ according to a 2020 study by local geoscientist Michael Garcia, Hawaii’s Pūhāhonu shield volcano is significantly larger, boasting a volume of about 148,000 cubic kilometers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The new study contradicts the long-held view, so the contrast word "However" is needed.
items.mk: [1|Geoscientists have long considered Hawaii’s Mauna Loa volcano to be Earth’s largest shield volcano by volume][p|, measuring approximately 74,000 cubic kilometers]⟨.⟩ {However}⟨,⟩ [p|according to a 2020 study by local geoscientist Michael Garcia,] [2|Hawaii’s Pūhāhonu shield volcano is significantly larger][p|, boasting a volume of about 148,000 cubic kilometers].

why.D: The new study contradicts the long-held view → contrast. Punctuation already fixed: . However,
why.B: The study is not a result of the old belief.
why.C: Moreover adds a similar point; this is the opposite.

items.passage: Samuel Coleridge-Taylor was a prominent classical music composer from England who toured the US three times in the early 1900s. The child of a West African father and an English mother, Coleridge-Taylor emphasized his mixed-race ancestry. For example, he referred to himself as Anglo-African. _______ he incorporated the sounds of traditional African music into his classical music compositions.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence gives a second example of how he emphasized his ancestry, so "In addition" is logical.

items.passage: In 2019, researcher Patricia Jurado Gonzalez and food historian Nawal Nasrallah prepared a stew from a 4,000-year-old recipe found on a Mesopotamian clay tablet. When they tasted the dish, known as pašrūtum (“unwinding”), they found that it had a mild taste and inspired a sense of calm. _______ the researchers, knowing that dishes were sometimes named after their intended effects, theorized that the dish’s name, “unwinding,” referred to its function: to help ancient diners relax.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The researchers' theory is a conclusion drawn from their experience of the dish's calming effect. "Therefore" signals this result.

items.passage: In his groundbreaking book Bengali Harlem and the Lost Histories of South Asian America, Vivek Bald uses newspaper articles, census records, ships’ logs, and memoirs to tell the _______ who made New York City their home in the early twentieth century.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: story’s of the South Asian immigrants
options.B: story’s of the South Asian immigrants’
options.C: stories of the South Asian immigrants
options.D: stories’ of the South Asian immigrant’s

items.explanation: Neither "stories" nor "immigrants" possesses anything here, so both are simple plurals without apostrophes.

items.skill: No punctuation between preposition and object
items.passage: In her two major series “Memory Test” and “Autobiography,” painter Howardena Pindell explored themes _______ healing, self-discovery, and memory by cutting and sewing back together pieces of canvas and inserting personal artifacts, such as postcards, into some of the paintings.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: No punctuation belongs between a preposition ("of") and its object ("healing, self-discovery, and memory").

items.passage: Both Sona Charaipotra, an Indian American, and Dhonielle Clayton, an African American, grew up frustrated by the lack of diverse characters in books for young people. In 2011, these two writers joined forces to found CAKE Literary, a book packaging _______ specializes in the creation and promotion of stories told from diverse perspectives for children and young adults.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "That specializes in..." is an essential relative clause describing the company; it needs the relative pronoun "that" and no comma. A and C lack a connecting word; D wrongly uses a comma before "that."

items.passage: A study led by scientist Rebecca Kirby at the University of Wisconsin–Madison found that black bears that eat human food before hibernation have increased levels of a rare carbon isotope, _______ due to the higher 13C levels in corn and cane sugar. Bears with these elevated levels were also found to have much shorter hibernation periods on average.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Carbon-13 (13C)" is a nonessential appositive opened by the comma after "isotope," so it must close with a comma. The parenthetical abbreviation stays attached to "carbon-13" with no comma in between.

items.passage: In 2010, archaeologist Noel Hidalgo Tan was visiting the twelfth-century temple of Angkor Wat in Cambodia when he noticed markings of red paint on the temple _______ the help of digital imaging techniques, he discovered the markings to be part of an elaborate mural containing over 200 paintings.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "With the help of digital imaging techniques, he discovered..." is a new independent clause, so a period is needed. A is a comma splice, B a run-on, C illogical.

items.passage: Working from an earlier discovery of Charpentier’s, chemists Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna—winners of the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry—re-created and then reprogrammed the so-called “genetic scissors” of a species of DNA-cleaving bacteria _______ a tool that is revolutionizing the field of gene technology.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The infinitive "to forge" expresses purpose (they reprogrammed the scissors in order to forge a tool). "Forging" (B) would illogically modify "bacteria," and C/D create faulty structure.

items.passage: In 2016, engineer Vanessa Galvez oversaw the installation of 164 bioswales, vegetated channels designed to absorb and divert stormwater, along the streets of Queens, New York. By reducing the runoff flowing into city sewers, _______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: the mitigation of both street flooding and the resulting pollution of nearby waterways has been achieved by bioswales.
options.B: the bioswales have mitigated both street flooding and the resulting pollution of nearby waterways.
options.C: the bioswales’ mitigation of both street flooding and the resulting pollution of nearby waterways has been achieved.
options.D: both street flooding and the resulting pollution of nearby waterways have been mitigated by bioswales.

items.explanation: "By reducing the runoff" describes what the bioswales did, so "the bioswales" must be the subject immediately after the comma. The other choices make "the mitigation," "the bioswales’ mitigation," or "flooding" do the reducing.

items.passage: A study published by Rice University geoscientist Ming Tang in 2019 offers a new explanation for the origin of Earth’s _______ structures called arcs, towering ridges that form when a dense oceanic plate subducts under a less dense continental plate, melts in the mantle below, and then rises and bursts through the continental crust above.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The first part is an independent clause, and what follows ("geological structures called arcs...") is a noun phrase that specifies the explanation. A colon correctly introduces it. C and D would leave a fragment; A runs the two together.

items.passage: During a 2021 launch, Rocket Labs’ Electron rocket experienced an unexpected failure: its second-stage booster shut down suddenly after ignition. _______ instead of downplaying the incident, Rocket Labs’ CEO publicly acknowledged what happened and apologized for the loss of the rocket’s payload, which had consisted of two satellites.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The CEO’s response came after the failure, so the time-sequence transition "Afterward" is logical.

items.passage: When soil becomes contaminated by toxic metals, it can be removed from the ground and disposed of in a landfill. _______ contaminated soil can be detoxified via phytoremediation: plants that can withstand high concentrations of metals absorb the pollutants and store them in their shoots, which are then cut off and safely disposed of, preserving the health of the plants.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Phytoremediation is a different option from removing the soil to a landfill. "Alternatively" introduces another possible method.

items.passage: Lê Lương Minh became the thirteenth secretary-general of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in January 2013, making _______ the first time the organization would appoint a Vietnamese leader.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun refers to a single event—Minh becoming secretary-general—so the singular "this" is required.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: In 1929, Edwin Herbert Land invented a polarizing filter that was featured in a number of products, from sunglasses to 3D movies. A decade later, Land _______ his technology to invent the world’s first instant camera, the Polaroid Land camera.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject "Land" needs a finite main verb. "Used" is finite and in the past tense, matching "invented" and "a decade later."

items.passage: An online content creator who uses copyrighted songs without permission risks being demonetized (prohibited from including paid advertisements in content). The best way to avoid demonetization is to choose music from the public domain. Using one of these noncopyrighted songs _______ a creator won’t lose advertising revenue.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the gerund phrase "Using one of these noncopyrighted songs," which is singular, so it takes the singular verb "ensures."

items.passage: What makes the theremin a unique musical instrument? You play it without touching it. When you place your _______ the pitch will shift as your hands move through the air.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Hands" and "antennas" are simple plurals that do not possess anything, so neither takes an apostrophe. (Note: the source prints the transition stem for this item, but it tests Standard English conventions.)

items.passage: In the music video for the song “We Didn’t Start the Fire” by Billy Joel, the singer lists 118 political and cultural references. Such iconic references, cited in rapid and frenetic procession by the musician, who is seated impassively at a dinner table, _______ key moments and personalities of the twentieth century.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the plural "Such iconic references" (the long interrupter doesn't change it), so the plural verb "represent" is needed.

items.passage: Long attributed to Jacques-Louis David, the preeminent Neoclassical painter of his day, the 1801 painting Marie Joséphine Charlotte du Val d’Ognes gained fresh attention in the 1990s when art historians discovered that the painting—which depicts a solitary young woman sketching—was actually the work of little-known French portrait _______ Marie-Denise Villers (1774–1821).
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Marie-Denise Villers" is an essential (restrictive) appositive identifying which portrait artist, so no punctuation separates it from "artist."

items.skill: Paired dashes around a supplementary element
items.passage: In 1986, conceptual artist Sophie Calle asked twenty-three people, all of whom had been born without sight, to describe “their image of beauty” in rich detail. Calle paired excerpts of these conversations with photographs—both of interviewees and the items they _______ to powerful effect in her exhibition The Blind.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: described, from hair to grass to sculptures
options.B: described, from hair to grass to sculptures—
options.C: described—from hair to grass to sculptures,
options.D: described: from hair to grass to sculptures

items.explanation: The supplementary element begins with a dash after "photographs," so it must close with a dash before "to powerful effect." Inside it, a comma sets off the examples "from hair to grass to sculptures."

items.passage: Celebrated Tewa potter Maria Martinez (1887–1980) made her signature all-black ceramic vessels using a heating technique called reduction firing. This technique involves smothering the flame surrounding the clay vessel. _______ the vessel takes on a shiny, black hue.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The black hue is the effect of smothering the flame, so "As a result" (cause–effect) is correct.

items.passage: Historians agree that the jazz pianist Jelly Roll Morton was exaggerating when he claimed to have invented jazz music. No one can deny, _______ that Morton’s innovative compositions and remarkable improvisational skills helped shape jazz as a genre during its early years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence concedes Morton's real importance in contrast to his exaggeration. "Though" signals this contrast.

items.passage: According to Duverger’s law, countries with single-ballot majoritarian elections for single-member districts tend to polarize into two-party systems, wherein dueling political parties consistently dominate the political system. _______ countries with proportional-representation electoral systems tend to support multi-partyism, under which power gets distributed among many political parties.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence describes the opposite situation (multi-party vs. two-party), so "Conversely" is logical.
