items.passage: A turtle shell appears external to the animal, protecting its body like armor. _______ the shell is often incorrectly assumed to be an exoskeleton, a rigid outer casing like that of a crustacean or an insect, when in fact it is an endoskeleton, a part of the turtle’s internal bone structure, more akin to a spine or a pair of ribs.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Because the shell looks external, people assume it is an exoskeleton. "Hence" shows that this assumption follows from the previous sentence.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: How did whales, once no bigger than seals, evolve to become the largest animals on Earth? Brazilian biologist Mariana Nery believes the answer might be found in whales’ DNA. In January 2023, Nery and her colleagues _______ a study showing changes over time in four whale genes associated with body size.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject "Nery and her colleagues" needs a finite main verb; "published" is finite and past tense (January 2023).

items.skill: No punctuation between subject and verb
items.passage: A harpsichord may look just like a piano, but the difference between the two instruments is easy to hear. When a harpsichord’s keys are pressed, the strings inside the _______ are plucked, not struck.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "The strings inside the instrument" is the subject and "are plucked" is the verb. No punctuation belongs between a subject and its verb.

items.passage: When they were first introduced to western Europe from Byzantium in the eleventh century, table forks were met with much resistance. The Bishop of Ostia, St. Peter Damian, condemned the eating utensils because he considered _______ dangerous and unnecessary luxury items.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun refers to the plural "the eating utensils" (table forks) and must match "items," so the plural "them" is correct.

items.skill: Paired commas around a nonessential appositive
items.passage: Julia Alvarez’s 1994 novel In the Time of the Butterflies, a fictionalized account of the lives of the Mirabal _______ can serve as a starting point for those wanting to explore how the rule of dictator Rafael Trujillo has been represented in Dominican American literature.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The appositive "a fictionalized account...Mirabal sisters" is opened with a comma, so it must close with a comma before the verb "can serve." Adding "and" would create a compound subject with no verb logic.

items.passage: On March 23, 2021, a gust of wind wreaked havoc on global trade. Ever Given, an international shipping container vessel, became lodged in Egypt’s Suez Canal, a major shipping route between Europe and Asia. The vessel took six days to _______ it’s as heavy as two thousand blue whales when fully loaded.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: dislodge in part due to its sheer size,
options.B: dislodge, in part due to its sheer size:
options.C: dislodge, in part due to its sheer size,
options.D: dislodge, in part, due to its sheer size

items.explanation: "In part due to its sheer size" is a supplementary phrase set off with a comma. The next part ("it’s as heavy as...") is an independent clause that explains the size, so a colon is appropriate. A and C create comma splices; D is a run-on.

items.skill: Restrictive appositive; no comma before verb
items.passage: Fans of the film Moana (2016) may not know that the deep and humorous voice behind the _______ belongs to comedian, actor, and musician Jemaine Clement. The versatile performer has appeared in everything from television commercials to action movies, but voice acting, specifically, has become a notable part of his career.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Tamatoa the crab" is a restrictive appositive identifying which character, so no commas are used. Also, no punctuation belongs between the subject ("the...voice behind the character Tamatoa the crab") and the verb "belongs."

items.passage: In her 1983 book The Managed Heart: Commercialization of Human Feeling, sociologist Arlie Russell Hochschild first explored at length her conception of a “sociology of emotions”—the idea that the various cultural and ideological frameworks a person has internalized (class, gender, political affiliation, etc.) _______ each emotional reaction that person has within a situation.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the plural "the various cultural and ideological frameworks," so the plural verb "underlie" is required. Present tense fits a general idea.

items.skill: Participial phrase as supplement (nonfinite) + paired commas
items.passage: American abstract artist Richard _______ his installations to make passersby keenly aware of how one’s movements are affected by the physical features of one’s environment, assembles large-scale steel plates into sculptures that dominate the outdoor spaces they occupy.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The main verb is "assembles." The words between the commas must be a nonessential participial phrase ("intending his installations to..."), so "Serra, intending" is correct. A finite verb (A, B, D) would create two main verbs.

items.passage: In 1949, Frank Zamboni developed an ice rink resurfacing machine. As Zamboni’s machine moved along the rink’s surface, it first scraped off the top layer of ice. _______ it sprayed water into the deep grooves left behind by customers’ skates. Lastly, it smoothed over the newly formed ice.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The steps are in order: "first," ___, "Lastly." "Next" fits the middle step.

items.passage: In 2014, Nestor Gomez won his first-ever storytelling competition, relating a tale about his life as a Guatemalan immigrant living in Chicago. _______ in 2017, Gomez created the show 80 Minutes Around the World as a platform for others to share stories about their immigration experiences.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The 2017 event came after the 2014 event, so the time transition "Later" is logical.

items.passage: To guarantee the validity of experimental results, scientists rely on precise, unchanging standards of measurement. _______ metrologists (scientists who study measurement) developed the SI, or International System of Units. The SI’s units of measurement are based on unchanging values in nature, such as the mass of an electron or the speed of light.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Metrologists developed the SI because scientists need unchanging standards. "For this reason" signals cause–effect.

items.passage: In retrospect, one of the lessons of the 2003 Human Genome Project is that a gene is affected by many factors, not the least of which is its interactions with the protein products of other genes. _______ rather than just focusing on the human genome, efforts to better understand gene mutations related to disease have begun to consider the human proteome, the complete set of proteins expressed by human genes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The shift in research focus is a consequence of the lesson learned. "Accordingly" signals a response that follows logically.

items.passage: The Boston Saloon was one of the most popular African American–owned establishments in nineteenth-century Nevada. _______ by businessman William A.G. Brown, the saloon was known to offer elegant accommodations and an inclusive environment.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The introductory phrase modifies "the saloon," which was created (passive meaning) by Brown. The past participle "Created" expresses this. "Creating" would mean the saloon did the creating; B and D are finite verbs that don't fit an introductory modifier.

items.skill: No punctuation between verb and object
items.passage: Louise Bennett (1919–2006), also known as “Miss Lou,” was an influential Jamaican poet and folklorist. Her innovative poems _______ the use of Jamaican Creole (a spoken language) in literature.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "The use of Jamaican Creole" is the direct object of "popularized." No punctuation belongs between a verb and its object.

items.passage: “He was just the man for such a place, and it was just the place for such a man.” This line is from Frederick Douglass’s autobiography Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass (1845). It’s an example of antimetabole, a writing technique that _______ emphasis by repeating a statement in a reversed order.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "That" refers to the singular "a writing technique," so the singular present-tense "creates" is correct (general definition).

items.skill: Indirect question – word order & end punctuation
items.passage: Researchers Amit Kumar and Nicholas Epley investigated how _______ In a series of experiments conducted in 2022, they found that people performing small acts of kindness underestimated the positive effect their actions had on others.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: do people perceive acts of kindness.
options.B: do people perceive acts of kindness?

items.explanation: This is an indirect (embedded) question inside a statement, so it uses statement word order (subject + verb: "people perceive") and ends with a period, not a question mark.

items.passage: In a painting titled “The Milkmaid” by Johannes Vermeer, the artist prominently features a bread basket, milk pitcher, and bowl. Such quotidian objects, depicted in exquisite detail by Vermeer, a painter celebrated for his naturalism, _______ the daily minutiae of a seventeenth-century Dutch household.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the plural "Such quotidian objects" (ignore the long interrupter), so the plural verb "reveal" is needed.

items.passage: Jamaican British artist Willard Wigan is known for his remarkable _______ so small that they are best viewed through a microscope, Wigan’s sculptures are made from tiny natural materials, such as spiderweb strands.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Creations so small that...microscope" is an introductory appositive for the second sentence's subject "Wigan’s sculptures." A period ends the first sentence; the other options fuse two independent clauses.

items.skill: Sentence boundary (dependent clause starts new sentence)
items.passage: Consider the mechanics of the pinhole camera: light passes through a small hole, resulting in a focused projected image. A ray diagram reveals how this _______ the hole’s small size restricts light to a single ray, all light passing through the hole can only arrive at a single destination, eliminating diffraction and ensuring a clear image.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Because the hole’s small size restricts light..., all light...can only arrive..." is a complete sentence (dependent clause + main clause). A period ends the previous sentence. C and D create a comma splice after "ray"; A fuses the sentences.

items.passage: In the search for extraterrestrial life, astrobiologists Stuart Bartlett and Michael L. Wong propose that scientists avoid using the term “life.” _______ researchers should use another word: “lyfe.” This new term, they argue, could be used to draw distinctions between the known characteristics of life on Earth and the potentially differing characteristics of lyfe on other planets.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Using "lyfe" is proposed as a replacement for "life," so "Instead" is logical.

items.passage: Before it unveiled a massive new gallery in 2009, the Art Institute of Chicago was only able to display about 5% of its art collection. _______ the museum is able to display close to 30% of its collection.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text contrasts the past (before 2009) with the present ("is able"), so "Today" is the logical time transition.

items.passage: Working together with the Navajo Nation Department of Water Resources, Dr. Lani Tsinnajinnie analyzed data about snowpack levels in the Chuska Mountains. She found that the snowpack (the amount of snow on the ground) was deepest in early March at lower elevations. At higher elevations, _______ the snowpack was deepest in mid-March.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Higher elevations show a different result than lower elevations. "On the other hand" signals this contrast.

items.passage: The Inca of South America used intricately knotted string devices called quipus to record countable information, like population data and payments. _______ they may have used quipus to record more complex information, like stories and myths, according to researchers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Recording stories is an additional possible use of quipus, so "In addition" is logical.

items.passage: In hindsight, given the ideas about the natural world circulating among British scientists in the 1800s, the theory of natural selection was an obvious next step. It may not have been a coincidence, _______ that Charles Darwin and Alfred Wallace arrived at the concept independently. Indeed, contrary to the popular myth of the lone genius, theirs is not the first paradigm-shifting theory to have emerged from multiple scholars working in parallel.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence draws a conclusion from the previous one (since the theory was an obvious next step, simultaneous discovery was likely no coincidence). "Then" here means "therefore/in that case."

items.skill: Direct question – word order & question mark
items.passage: In forecasting weather events, meteorologists sometimes discuss the role of atmospheric rivers. What are atmospheric rivers, and how _______ Part of the water cycle, atmospheric rivers are narrow channels of moisture moving through the atmosphere. In certain conditions, these “rivers” can release some of their moisture as precipitation.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: This is a direct question ("What are atmospheric rivers, and how..."), so it needs question word order ("do they affect") and a question mark.

items.passage: One of the few African American global explorers during the turn of the 20th century, _______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: Matthew Henson made several treks across Greenland between 1891 and 1909.
options.B: 1891 and 1909 were the years between which Matthew Henson made several treks across Greenland.
options.C: Greenland was where Matthew Henson made several treks between 1891 and 1909.
options.D: several treks across Greenland were made by Matthew Henson between 1891 and 1909.

items.explanation: The introductory phrase describes a person (an explorer), so the subject right after the comma must be "Matthew Henson." The other choices make years, Greenland, or treks the explorer (dangling modifier).

items.passage: Woven from recycled yarn and hand tufted using a carpet weaving technique passed down by the artist’s Turkish grandmother, _______ so lush and tactilely inviting that you are tempted to reach out and touch them.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: the topological tapestries of Argentine textile artist Alexandra Kehayoglou are
options.B: the Argentine textile artist Alexandra Kehayoglou creates topological tapestries that are
options.C: when she creates her topological tapestries, Argentine textile artist Alexandra Kehayoglou makes them
options.D: Alexandra Kehayoglou is an Argentine textile artist whose topological tapestries are

items.explanation: Things "woven from recycled yarn" are the tapestries, so "the topological tapestries" must immediately follow the modifier. The other choices put the artist (or a clause) there, creating a dangling modifier.

items.passage: Physical materials can be classified by how much light passes through them. Clear glass, which is classified as transparent, allows all (or almost all) light to pass _______ wax paper, which is classified as translucent, allows only some light to pass through.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined with no conjunction, so a semicolon is required. A is a comma splice; B is a run-on; D lacks the needed comma before "and."

items.passage: Using natural debris, such as dried _______ such as plastic bags; and more traditional art supplies, such as tree glue, Ghanaian artist Ed Franklin Gavua creates his striking Yiiiiikakaii African masks, which he hopes can help viewers rethink how waste is used in their communities.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The list items contain internal commas, so items are separated with semicolons ("...leaves; man-made trash, such as plastic bags; and..."). Within item 2, a comma precedes "such as."

items.skill: Colon introducing a list + conjunctive adverb
items.passage: Latin America is known to have dozens, if not hundreds, of popular dance forms. Only five of these dances are included in international ballroom dance _______ rumba, samba, cha-cha-cha, paso doble, and jive—the last of which is grouped with the other Latin dances despite not having Latin roots.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "However" ends the first independent clause (contrasting it with the previous sentence) and is set off by a comma. A colon then introduces the list of the five dances.

items.passage: For thousands of years, humans have used domesticated goats (Capra hircus) to clear land of unwanted vegetation. When it comes to their diets, goats are notoriously _______ they will devour all kinds of shrubs and weeds, leaving virtually no part of any plant unconsumed.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The second clause explains what "indiscriminate" means, so a colon (after an independent clause) is correct. B is a comma splice, C a run-on, A lacks a comma before "and."

items.passage: A species of Byropsis algae produces toxins to avoid being eaten by predators. However, in some cases, the toxins the organism uses to protect itself from predation actually _______ its attractiveness to predators. The Hawaiian sea slug, for example, not only tolerates Byropsis toxins but actually uses them for protection in the same way the algae does.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the plural "the toxins" (not "the organism" in the relative clause), so the plural verb "increase" is needed.

items.passage: After appropriate permissions are granted, a typical archaeological dig begins with a surveyor making a detailed grid of the excavation site. Then, the site is carefully dug, and any artifacts found are recorded and mapped onto the site grid. _______ the artifacts are removed, cataloged, and analyzed in a laboratory.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text describes steps in order ("begins," "Then"); the last step is introduced by "Finally."

items.passage: The liquid metals in Earth’s core circulate constantly, and this circulation generates electrical currents that flow between Earth’s North and South magnetic poles. These electrical currents, _______ create a barrier around Earth that protects us from radiation and charged particles coming from space.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Circulation creates currents, and the currents then create a barrier—a chain of cause and effect. "In turn" signals this next step.

items.passage: Biographer Michael Gorra notes that the novelist Henry James “lived in a world of second thoughts,” frequently tinkering with his novels and stories after their initial publication. However, the differences between the 1881 first edition and the 1908 edition of his novel A Portrait of a Lady are extreme, even by James’s standards; _______ some critics regard the two editions as two different novels altogether.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The final clause intensifies the claim that the differences are extreme. "In fact" introduces this stronger supporting point.

items.passage: One of the earliest known maps is a Babylonian clay tablet thought to be almost 4,500 years old. The map _______ the area of a plot of land, shows a river valley, and includes the cardinal directions.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject "The map" is singular, and the other verbs in the series ("shows," "includes") are singular simple present. "Describes" agrees and keeps the series parallel.

items.passage: Eighteen letters written by Louisa May Alcott, author of the popular novel Little Women (1868), can be found at the New York Historical Society. _______ letters demonstrate Alcott’s keen business sense in her interactions with publishers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The determiner must match the plural noun "letters" (and refer back to the eighteen letters). Only "These" is plural.

items.passage: The Dust Bowl was a period of severe drought that plagued the Great Plains of the US during the 1930s. During this time, dust storms _______ over 100 million acres of land. They even reached as far east as New York City.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The events happened in the 1930s ("was," "plagued," "reached"), so the simple past "affected" is correct.

items.passage: Many mechanical calculators were powered by a notched cylinder mechanism called the Leibniz wheel. Leibniz wheel calculators were popular in the first half of the twentieth _______ these ingenious devices were eventually replaced by electronic calculators.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses with a contrast are joined with a comma + "but." A is a run-on, B a comma splice, D creates an illogical relative clause.

items.passage: Featuring jagged peaks of black ink surrounded by hazy swirls of blue and green paint, Zhang Daqian’s 1983 painting Panorama of Mount Lu is inspired by the tradition of qinglü shanshui, a type of Chinese landscape painting _______ by the use of blue and green hues to depict ethereal, otherworldly landscapes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Characterized by..." is a past-participle phrase modifying "a type of Chinese landscape painting." A finite verb (A, B, D) would create a second main verb inside the appositive.

items.passage: Increasing the heat on an uncovered boiling pot of water does not increase the temperature of the water. What increases is the rate at which the water turns to _______ a pressure cooker pot, though, an airtight seal traps the vapor in the pot, creating pressure that allows the temperature of the water to increase past its boiling point.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "With a pressure cooker pot, though, an airtight seal traps..." is a new independent clause. A period separates the two sentences; B, C, D create a run-on or comma splice or illogical attachment.

items.passage: Wanting to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the Alaska Purchase, _______ up with a motto that best captured the state’s unique character. The commission selected “North to the Future,” submitted by Juneau journalist Richard Peter, as its winning entry.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: a contest sponsored by the Alaska Centennial Commission would award $300 to an individual who came
options.B: an award of $300 would go to an individual in a contest sponsored by the Alaska Centennial Commission for coming
options.C: $300 would be awarded to an individual by the Alaska Centennial Commission in a contest for coming
options.D: the Alaska Centennial Commission sponsored a contest that would award $300 to an individual who came

items.explanation: The modifier "Wanting to celebrate..." must describe the entity that wanted to celebrate—the Alaska Centennial Commission—so it must come right after the comma. The other choices make a contest, an award, or $300 do the "wanting."

items.passage: Recently unearthed Neronian tools in France dating to 54,000 years ago and attributed to Homo sapiens may provide evidence that interactions between Neanderthals and modern humans occurred 10,000 years earlier than was previously _______ finding that, if true, would overturn current theories about H. sapiens migration during the Upper Paleolithic.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "A finding that..." is a noun phrase (appositive) summing up the preceding clause, not an independent clause, so it is attached with a comma. A and B would leave it as a fragment; C omits needed punctuation.

items.passage: Guard cells are specialized cells that are part of a plant’s pores. These cells help regulate the amount of carbon dioxide a plant takes in. _______ they help regulate a plant’s water loss.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence adds another function of guard cells, so "Additionally" is logical.

items.passage: Nowadays, tug-of-war is usually seen as an informal game one might play at a picnic or in gym class. Surprisingly, the Olympic committee once decided _______ tug-of-war as an official Olympic event! Nations competed in the event at the Olympic Games from 1900 to 1920.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The verb "decide" is followed by an infinitive (decide to do something), so "to include" is correct.

items.passage: The Globe Theatre in London is a reconstruction of the famed venue where many of Shakespeare’s plays were first performed. In 1613, a prop cannon _______ during a performance and ignited the Globe’s thatched roof. No one was hurt, but in two hours the original Globe was gone.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The event occurred "in 1613" and is parallel with "ignited," so the simple past "malfunctioned" is correct.

items.skill: No punctuation between subject and verb
items.passage: Nigerian American artist Toyin Ojih Odutola uses black-ink pens to create highly detailed drawings of human figures. Her portrait of novelist Zadie _______ is displayed in the National Portrait Gallery in London.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Her portrait of novelist Zadie Smith" is the subject, and "is displayed" is its verb. No punctuation belongs between a subject and its verb.

items.passage: When a given industry—water and electricity are two well-known examples—carries high infrastructural start-up costs and other barriers that discourage competition, _______ of just one or two suppliers per municipality. Such industries are known as natural monopolies.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun refers to "a given industry," which is singular; the dashed examples are an interrupter. "It often consists" is singular and clearly refers to the industry.

items.passage: As the fourteenth US librarian of Congress, Carla Hayden has many responsibilities. These include overseeing the Library of Congress’s collections, which boast more than 162 million _______ the US Copyright Office, which registers copyright claims and advises Congress on copyright law; and appointing the US poet laureate.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The list of responsibilities (overseeing...; managing...; and appointing...) has items with internal commas, so semicolons separate the items.

items.passage: Digital artist Jung (Lulu) Chen primarily uses a suite of software tools to create illustrations for children’s books. To manifest the warm and welcoming atmospheres that are a signature of her _______ she occasionally relies on more traditional art techniques, such as painting with watercolors.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The introductory infinitive phrase ends at "work," and "though" is an interrupting adverb within the same sentence; it needs commas on both sides before the main clause "she occasionally relies...." Semicolons (C, D) would require independent clauses on both sides.
items.mk: [p|To manifest the warm and welcoming atmospheres] [d|that are a signature of her work]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1|she occasionally relies on more traditional art techniques][p|, such as painting with watercolors].

why.A: Only one IC. though interrupts it (between intro phrase and main clause) → paired commas.
why.C: Semicolon needs ICs on both sides; “To manifest…” is a phrase.

items.passage: Chondrites are stony meteorites that are undifferentiated—that is, their contents have not melted and separated into distinct layers. They are hardly _______ many chondrites experience aqueous alteration as a result of exposure to fluids, as well as fracturing, veining, and localized melting due to collisions with other objects.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "They are hardly pristine, though" is a complete clause (with "though" as an adverb at its end). A semicolon then separates it from the next independent clause "many chondrites experience...".
items.mk: [1|They are hardly pristine]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨;⟩ [2|many chondrites experience aqueous alteration as a result of exposure to fluids, as well as fracturing, veining, and localized melting]…

why.B: IC1 contrasts with sentence 1 (undifferentiated ↔ hardly pristine); IC2 gives the evidence.
why.C: “; though many…” turns IC2 into a fragment.

items.passage: That the geographic center of North America lay in the state of North Dakota was conceded by all _______ establishing its precise coordinates proved more divisive.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined without a conjunction, so a semicolon is required. B is a comma splice, C a run-on; a colon (A) does not fit because the second clause contrasts rather than explains.

items.passage: Famous for its four-degree tilt, the leaning Garisenda Tower is a popular attraction in Bologna’s city center. However, measurements taken in 2023 showed that the tower was rotating in a concerning way. _______ city officials closed the area around the tower so experts could explore solutions to stabilize the historical twelfth-century structure.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Closing the area is a consequence of the concerning rotation, so "As a result" is logical.

items.passage: In 2021, a model developed by astrophysicist Catherine Zucker and her research team revealed that the same supernovas responsible for the creation and ongoing expansion of the Local Bubble—a 14-million-year-old cavity in the Milky Way—are likely responsible for the formation of new stars. _______ this model detailed how the bubble’s expansion trapped interstellar clouds of gas and dust that became stars upon their eventual collapse.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence gives a more detailed explanation of the general claim in the previous sentence, so "Specifically" is correct.

items.passage: Following the American Revolutionary War, North American foodways underwent a radical transformation, fueled in large part by spiking consumer demand for certain grains. The cultivation, trade, and transportation of maize and wheat, _______ reconfigured the continent’s existing regional foodways into a globally oriented food system.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Maize and wheat are the specific "certain grains" mentioned before, so "in particular" is logical.

items.passage: When, in 2017, Cambridge University students Lucy Moss and Toby Marlow decided they wanted to develop a musical together, one of their goals was for their female actor friends to have good parts to play. _______ they created the show Six, a retelling of the history of King Henry VIII’s wives in which each of the six queens has a starring role.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Creating a show with six starring female roles was done to achieve the stated goal. "To that end" signals purpose.

items.passage: Mountain climbing routes that incorporate metal rungs and cables are known as via ferratas, from the Italian phrase for “iron path.” As climbing these routes has shifted from a mode of travel to a sporting activity, modern via ferratas are rarely designed to simply reach a summit. _______ new routes favor recreation over utility, aiming to provide a challenging climb or showcase dramatic scenery.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The previous sentence says routes are "rarely" designed just to reach a summit; the next tells what they are "more often" designed to do. "More often" completes this contrast of frequency.

items.skill: Restrictive appositive; no comma before verb
items.passage: Paintings by the renowned twentieth-century US _______ were featured in Artist to Artist, an exhibition at the Smithsonian Art Museum that paired the works of artists whose career trajectories intersected in meaningful ways.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: artists: Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollock,
options.B: artists Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollock
options.C: artists Thomas Hart Benton, and Jackson Pollock,
options.D: artists, Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollock

items.explanation: The names are a restrictive appositive identifying which artists, so no punctuation is used. Also, no punctuation belongs between the subject and the verb "were featured."

items.passage: Increased gender diversity is revitalizing the field of economics, according to Harvard’s Claudia Goldin. The trailblazing accomplishments of Goldin, winner of the 2023 Nobel Prize in Economics for her work on women in the labor force, _______ to the value of scholars of diverse backgrounds in spurring research into previously unexplored, but vitally important, topics.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the plural "accomplishments" (not "Goldin"), so the plural verb "attest" is required.

items.passage: During the English neoclassical period (1660–1789), many writers imitated the epic poetry and satires of ancient Greece and Rome. They were not the first in England to adopt the literary modes of classical _______ some of the most prominent figures of the earlier Renaissance period were also influenced by ancient Greek and Roman literature.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "However" belongs with the first clause (it contrasts with the previous sentence), and a semicolon separates the two independent clauses. A and B are comma splices; D wrongly attaches "however" to the second clause, where it makes no sense (the second clause supports rather than contrasts with the first).
items.mk: [1|They were not the first in England to adopt the literary modes of classical antiquity]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨;⟩ [2|some of the most prominent figures of the earlier Renaissance period were also influenced by ancient Greek and Roman literature].

why.C: IC1 contrasts with sentence 1 (they imitated ↔ but weren't the first). IC2 supports IC1 (“also”).
why.A: Comma splice (nothing strong between the ICs).
why.D: Links however to IC2, which is not a contrast.

items.skill: Paired commas around a nonessential participial phrase
items.passage: English poet and Shakespeare contemporary John Donne’s _______ much admired during his lifetime (1572–1631) and in the decades that followed, had, at the time of their enthusiastic rediscovery by the early twentieth-century modernists, been essentially gathering dust for the intervening 250 years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The main verb is "had...been gathering." "Much admired during his lifetime..." is a nonessential participial phrase that must be set off by commas; it needs an opening comma after "works." Adding "were" or "had been" creates two main verbs.

items.passage: Compared to that of alumina glass, _______ silica glass atoms are so far apart that they are unable to re-form bonds after being separated.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: silica glass is at a significant disadvantage due to its more dispersed atomic arrangement:
options.B: silica glass has a more dispersed atomic arrangement, resulting in a significant disadvantage:
options.C: a significant disadvantage of silica glass is that its atomic arrangement is more dispersed:
options.D: silica glass’s atomic arrangement is more dispersed, resulting in a significant disadvantage:

items.explanation: "That of alumina glass" means "the atomic arrangement of alumina glass," so it must be compared with another atomic arrangement—"silica glass’s atomic arrangement." The other choices compare an arrangement with silica glass itself or with a disadvantage (illogical comparison/modifier).

items.passage: In 1974, Mexican chemist Mario Molina and US chemist F. Sherwood Rowland discovered that chemicals called CFCs were harmful to the ozone layer. Their research was extremely influential in the fight against CFCs. _______ it laid the foundation for a 1987 treaty that phased out the use of CFCs across the globe.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence gives a specific example of how the research was influential, so "Specifically" is logical.

items.passage: With his room-sized installation Unicorn/My Private Sky, Norwegian artist Børre Sæthre succeeds in creating a whimsical yet perplexing experience. _______ when visitors set foot inside the fantastically blue room and encounter the life-sized stuffed unicorn preening at the far end of it, they are both dazzled and confused—as if stepping into a strange and enchanting new world.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence confirms and reinforces the claim that the experience is whimsical yet perplexing. "Indeed" signals this support.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: In 1966, Emmett Ashford became the first African American to umpire a Major League Baseball game. His energetic gestures announcing when a player had struck out and his habit of barreling after a hit ball to see if it would land out of _______ transform the traditionally solemn umpire role into a dynamic one.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The compound subject ("His energetic gestures...and his habit...") needs a finite main verb: "helped." The other choices are nonfinite or create a relative clause, leaving the sentence without a main verb.

items.passage: Jetties—long, narrow structures that extend from a landmass into the water—are often constructed to protect coastlines from erosion. Jetties can sometimes have the opposite _______ obstructing the natural flow of sand along the shore can lead to increased erosion in some areas.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" is an adverb ending the first clause, set off by a comma. A semicolon then separates the two independent clauses. B and D are comma splices/run-ons; C attaches "though" to the second clause, making it a dependent clause fragment after the semicolon.

items.passage: The Alaska Native Language Archive (ANLA) is known for its impressive audio collection. _______ the ANLA has more than 5,000 audio recordings of Native Alaskan languages dating as far back as 1943.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence gives concrete evidence that strengthens the claim about the "impressive" collection. "In fact" introduces this emphasis.

items.passage: Upon first approaching artist Kurt Wenner’s Dies Irae, a colorful scene painted on the surface of a cobblestone street in Mantua, Italy, one might assume a deep hole filled with life-sized, classically styled sculptures had opened up in the street. _______ by expertly applying the principles of perspective, Wenner created merely the illusion of depth.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence corrects the false assumption in the first (there is no real hole). "On the contrary" signals this correction.

items.passage: Economist Elinor Ostrom’s studies of communities around the world have empirically demonstrated that common pool resources, such as grazing lands, can be sustainably managed by the people who use them (rather than through private entities or centralized governments). _______ Ostrom’s work is a repudiation of the “tragedy of the commons,” the view that individuals will inevitably overexploit a finite shared resource if given unfettered access to it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Because her work demonstrates sustainable shared management, it therefore functions as a repudiation of the "tragedy of the commons." "As such" signals this consequence/characterization.

items.passage: In 1930, Japanese American artist Chiura Obata depicted the natural beauty of Yosemite National Park in two memorable woodcuts: Evening at Carl Inn and Lake Basin in the High Sierra. In 2019, _______ exhibited alongside 150 of Obata’s other works in a single-artist show at the Smithsonian American Art Museum.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun refers to the two woodcuts, a plural antecedent, so "they were" is correct. "Some" is illogical because both woodcuts are meant.

items.passage: As cheesemaking practices spread throughout Europe and Asia during and after the Neolithic, divergent strategies for preserving milk _______ whereas rennet-coagulated cheesemaking became key to milk preservation in Europe and Southwest Asia, acid-heat coagulation methods became common among nomadic herding populations of the northeastern Eurasian steppe.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The first part is a complete sentence; the second part explains what the "divergent strategies" were. A colon introduces this explanation. D creates a comma splice, A a run-on, B an illogical compound.

items.passage: Recent pollen analyses of the Aran Islands have led some researchers to propose that the now treeless islands were once wooded. This hypothesis _______ that certain trees, such as P. sylvestris, survived without interruption or human intervention throughout the Holocene cannot stand, researchers Michael O’Connell and Karen Molloy counter, unless other explanations can first be ruled out.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The main verb of the sentence is "cannot stand." "Suggesting that..." is a participial phrase modifying "This hypothesis." A finite verb (B, C, D) would give the subject two main verbs.

items.passage: Researchers studying the “terra-cotta army,” the thousands of life-size statues of warriors found interred near the tomb of Emperor Qin Shi Huang of China, were shocked to realize that the shape of each statue’s ears, like the shape of each person’s ears, _______ unique.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is "the shape" (singular), not "ears"; the comparison phrase is an interrupter. The fact is permanently true, so the singular present "is" is correct.

items.passage: Some members of the US Supreme Court have resisted calls to televise the court’s oral arguments, concerned that the participants would be tempted to perform for the cameras (and thus lower the quality of the discourse). _______ the justices worry that most viewers would not even watch the full deliberations, only short clips that could be misinterpreted and mischaracterized.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence adds a second concern the justices have, so "Additionally" is logical.

items.passage: A firefly uses specialized muscles to draw oxygen into its lower abdomen through narrow tubes, triggering a chemical reaction whereby the oxygen combines with chemicals in the firefly’s abdomen to produce a glow. _______ when the firefly stops drawing in oxygen, the reaction—and the glow—cease.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Stopping oxygen intake (glow ceases) is the opposite of drawing in oxygen (glow produced). "By contrast" signals this opposite situation.

items.passage: In the historical novel The Surrender Tree, Cuban American author Margarita Engle uses poetry rather than prose _______ the true story of Cuban folk hero Rosa La Bayamesa.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The infinitive "to tell" expresses purpose (she uses poetry in order to tell the story). The sentence already has its main verb, "uses."

items.passage: Interest in mechanotransduction, the mechanism by which cells sense and convert mechanical stimuli into biochemical signals, is expanding because of innovative work by biomedical scientists—many of whom, like neuroscience and biophysics expert Elba Serrano, _______ this mechanism to better understand how the body’s neurological and biomechanical systems interact.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is "many of whom" (many scientists), which is plural; "like...Elba Serrano" is an interrupter. The plural verb "study" is required.

items.passage: Sociologist Todd Gitlin co-opted the term “recombinant,” normally used in reference to genetic engineering, to describe serialized television shows of the 1980s. Gitlin’s use of the term referenced TV studios’ practice of repackaging successful narrative formulas as new _______ even shows that varied only slightly from other shows still attracted sizeable audiences.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined, so a semicolon is needed after "content." "In that era" introduces the second clause and is followed by a comma.

items.passage: In the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, automobiles were commonly referred to as horseless carriages after the older technology they still resembled. Known as the Brass Era, this period in automotive design is remembered for its grandeur and artistry, its vehicles _______ by collectors for their ornate detailing and gleaming brass fittings.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Its vehicles highly prized by collectors..." is an absolute phrase (noun + participle) attached with a comma. A finite verb (A, B, D) would create a comma splice.

items.passage: With the development of new technologies that use natural resources more efficiently, the overall consumption of those resources might be expected to decrease. Economists have observed that improvements in efficiency often correlate negatively with resource _______ efficiency gains, lowering the cost of use, may increase demand to the extent that resource consumption ultimately rises.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" ends the first clause as a contrast adverb (set off with a comma); a semicolon then separates the two independent clauses. A and D create comma splices; B makes the second part a dependent clause after a semicolon.

items.passage: Earth’s auroras—colorful displays of light seen above the northern and southern poles—result, broadly speaking, from the Sun’s activity. _______ the Sun releases charged particles that are captured by Earth’s magnetic field and channeled toward the poles. These particles then collide with atoms in the atmosphere, causing the atoms to emit auroral light.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The following sentences give precise details of the "broadly speaking" explanation. "Specifically" signals this elaboration.

items.passage: Along with carbon dioxide concentration and temperature, light intensity affects the chemical reaction rate of _______ as light intensity increases, so does the rate at which the reactants (water and carbon dioxide) are converted into their products (glucose and oxygen).
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The second independent clause explains how light intensity affects the rate, so a colon is appropriate. B is a comma splice, D a run-on, A lacks the comma before "and."

items.passage: In Marisol’s 1968 sculpture Mi Mama y Yo, gone are the types of pop culture references that made the Parisian-born Venezuelan American artist a star at the height of the pop art movement. In _______ place is a far more personal subject: a sculptural depiction of the artist as a young girl with her mother.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The possessive refers to "the types of pop culture references" (plural), which are gone; the new subject takes their place. So the plural possessive "their" is correct. "It’s" and "they’re" are contractions.

items.passage: The ghazal, a poetic form originating in seventh‑century Arabic poetry, has an intricate structure. The twentieth‑century Kashmiri American poet Agha Shahid Ali explains that each one of a ghazal’s couplets, while adhering to the patterns of rhyme (qafia) and refrain (radif) established in the poem’s opening lines (matla), _______ thematically and logically autonomous, resulting in a poem with “a stringently formal disunity.”
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is "each one" (singular), not "couplets." The present tense matches "explains" and a general description, so "is" is correct.

items.passage: When Chinese director Chloé Zhao accepted the Oscar in 2021 for her film Nomadland, she made Academy Award history. _______ only one other woman, Kathryn Bigelow of the United States, had been named best director at the Oscars, making Zhao the second woman and the first Asian woman to win the award.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence describes what had happened before Zhao's win ("had been named"), so the time transition "Previously" is logical.

items.passage: If the formation of Earth’s mantle had been purely a product of core differentiation—whereby heavier elements sink toward the core and lighter elements rise—the upper mantle would be depleted of heavy siderophile elements. Siderophiles are much more abundant in the mantle than predicted in that model, however. _______ extraterrestrial material containing siderophiles, likely from asteroid or comet impacts, almost certainly accreted to Earth following core differentiation.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The final sentence is a conclusion drawn from the evidence (siderophiles are more abundant than predicted), so "Hence" is logical.

items.passage: In February 1919, following the end of the First World War, women from ten countries around the world convened the Inter-Allied Women’s Conference in Paris. The conference’s goals were _______ ensure women’s participation in the proceedings of the Paris Peace Conference, to secure the right of women to serve in the League of Nations, and to advocate for human rights.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "The conference’s goals were threefold" is complete; a colon introduces the list of the three goals that follows. B and D would leave the list as a fragment; C runs them together.

items.skill: Subject–verb agreement ("in conjunction with" doesn't pluralize)
items.passage: Mathematician Grigori Perelman, sometimes in conjunction with mathematicians Richard S. Hamilton and Shing-Tung Yau, _______ credited with proving the Poincaré conjecture. Having built on Hamilton’s previous work to solve the proof, Perelman has insisted that Hamilton receive credit. Yau later found and closed gaps in Perelman’s proof, persuading some mathematicians that he deserves credit as well.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the singular "Grigori Perelman"; the phrase "sometimes in conjunction with..." is an interrupter and does not make the subject plural. So the singular "is" is required.

items.passage: Neuroscientist Karen Konkoly wanted to determine whether individuals can understand and respond to questions during REM sleep. She first taught volunteers eye movements they would use to respond to basic math problems while asleep (a single left-right eye movement indicated the number one). _______ she attached electrodes to the volunteers’ faces to record their eye movements during sleep.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The procedure is described in order ("first"); the following step is introduced by "Next."

items.passage: In his 1925 book The Morphology of Landscape, US geographer Carl Sauer challenged prevailing views about how natural landscapes influence human cultures. _______ Sauer argued that instead of being shaped entirely by their natural surroundings, cultures play an active role in their own development by virtue of their interactions with the environment.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence explains exactly how Sauer challenged the prevailing views, so "Specifically" is logical.

items.passage: In her 2012 analysis of tree rings from Japan’s Yaku Island, cosmic ray physicist Fusa Miyake noted an anomalous carbon-14 spike dating to 774–775 CE, indicating that a massive burst of radiation reached Earth during that time. _______ this unprecedented radiocarbon surge was dubbed a “Miyake event” in honor of its discoverer.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: It is appropriate that the event is named after the person who discovered it. "Fittingly" expresses this appropriateness.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: In the 1840s, the Irish potato crop was devastated by Phytophthora infestans, a water mold that spreads rapidly in cool, damp conditions. Many agricultural historians _______ that the island’s near-total reliance on a single potato variety, the Lumper, left the crop with almost no genetic defense against the pathogen.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject “Many agricultural historians” has no main verb yet. “Argue” is finite and plural; the participles and the infinitive are nonfinite and would leave the sentence a fragment.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: To conserve energy during the long Arctic winter, when air temperatures can fall below −30°C, Arctic ground squirrels in hibernation _______ their core body temperature to drop below the freezing point of water. No other mammal is known to survive such a low body temperature.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Strip the interrupters: “Arctic ground squirrels [blank] their core body temperature to drop.” The subject needs a finite main verb, and only “allow” is finite.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: For centuries, weavers on the Indonesian island of Sumba _______ ikat, a technique in which bundles of thread are tightly bound and dyed before being woven, to produce textiles that mark births, marriages, and funerals. Remarkably, a single large cloth can take a weaver more than a year to complete.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject “weavers” needs a finite main verb. “Have practiced” is finite, and the present perfect fits an activity that began in the past and continues (“For centuries”). The other choices are nonfinite.

items.skill: Finite verb in a relative clause
items.passage: A largely self-taught mathematician from southern India, Srinivasa Ramanujan is celebrated for the notebooks he filled before his death in 1920, which _______ thousands of formulas that researchers are still working to prove.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The relative clause “which [blank] thousands of formulas” needs its own finite verb. “Contain” is finite and agrees with the plural “notebooks.” The nonfinite forms leave the clause without a verb.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: A honeybee that has located a rich patch of flowers does not simply return to it; she first spends valuable time performing an elaborate “waggle dance” inside the dark hive. Research by Austrian ethologist Karl von Frisch _______ why: the angle and duration of the dance tell nestmates the direction and distance of the food source, allowing the entire colony to exploit it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject “Research” (ignore “by Austrian ethologist Karl von Frisch”) needs a finite main verb before the colon: “reveals.” The other choices are nonfinite.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: In 1928, Scottish physician Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold contaminating one of his culture plates had killed the surrounding bacteria. More than a decade later, Howard Florey and Ernst Chain _______ on Fleming’s observation to develop penicillin into a drug that could be mass-produced.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject “Howard Florey and Ernst Chain” needs a finite main verb. “Built” is finite and in the simple past, matching “noticed” and “More than a decade later.”

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: How do monarch butterflies, which weigh less than a gram, navigate thousands of kilometers to the same mountain forests in central Mexico each autumn? Neurobiologist Steven Reppert suspected that part of the answer lay in the insects’ antennae. In 2009, Reppert and his colleagues _______ evidence that the antennae contain a light-sensitive clock that helps the butterflies orient themselves by the Sun.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject “Reppert and his colleagues” needs a finite main verb; “reported” is finite and past tense (“In 2009”). The other choices are nonfinite.

items.skill: Finite vs. nonfinite verb (main verb needed)
items.passage: In 1955, Marian Anderson became the first African American singer to perform a principal role at the Metropolitan Opera. Her decades of acclaimed concert tours across Europe and her celebrated 1939 recital on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial before a crowd of 75,000 _______ pave the way for the generations of Black opera singers who followed.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The long compound subject (“Her decades of... tours... and her... recital...”) still needs a finite main verb: “helped.” The other choices turn “help” into a participle, a relative clause, or an infinitive, leaving the sentence without a main verb.

items.passage: In summer, the hunting habits of polar bears along Hudson Bay are shaped more by ice conditions than by preference. Although the bears rely on sea ice as a platform for catching seals, that platform may disappear for months as the bay thaws, _______ the animals to come ashore and subsist on stored fat, bird eggs, and whatever carcasses they can scavenge.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The main clause (“that platform may disappear”) is already complete, so what follows the comma must be a nonfinite participial phrase showing the result: “driving the animals to come ashore.” “Drives” and “drove” are finite verbs with no subject or conjunction; “to drive” would wrongly suggest purpose.

items.skill: Parallel verbs after a modal (would + base form)
items.passage: To reduce the urban heat island effect, in which paved surfaces cause cities to be warmer than surrounding rural areas, some planners have proposed that reflective coatings be applied to rooftops and roads. Such coatings would lower surface temperatures during heat waves and _______ the amount of electricity that buildings consume for air conditioning.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two verbs share the modal “would”: “would lower... and (would) decrease.” After a modal, each verb must be in the base form, parallel to “lower.”

items.passage: Drawing on decades of research into how the immune system recognizes foreign molecules, biochemists Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman—recipients of the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine—chemically modified one of the building blocks of messenger RNA _______ a molecule that cells would accept without triggering a harmful inflammatory response.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The sentence already has its main verb (“modified”). The blank explains WHY they modified the RNA, so an infinitive of purpose is needed: “to produce a molecule.” “Produced” and “produces” add a second finite verb with no conjunction; “and producing” is not parallel to “modified.”

items.skill: Participial phrase as supplement (nonfinite) + paired commas
items.passage: Japanese artist Yayoi _______ her mirrored installations to give viewers the sensation of standing in a space without boundaries, lines the walls, floors, and ceilings of small rooms with reflective panels that multiply hanging lights into seemingly endless fields.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The main verb is “lines” (“Yayoi Kusama... lines the walls”). Everything between the commas is a supplement, so it must be a nonfinite participial phrase opened with a comma: “Kusama, designing her mirrored installations...,”. The other choices give the subject two finite verbs.

items.passage: The Rosenwald schools were among the most important educational institutions for Black children in the rural American South in the early twentieth century. _______ through a partnership between educator Booker T. Washington and philanthropist Julius Rosenwald, the schools eventually numbered nearly five thousand across fifteen states.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The opening phrase modifies “the schools,” which RECEIVED the action (they were established), so the past participle is required. “Establishing” would mean the schools did the establishing; the finite forms cannot begin a modifier.

items.passage: Built around a steady pulse and short melodic cells that shift gradually over time, Steve Reich’s 1976 composition Music for 18 Musicians is a landmark of minimalism, a style of music _______ by the repetition and slow transformation of simple patterns rather than by dramatic contrasts.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “A style of music...” is an appositive renaming “minimalism,” not a new clause, so it cannot take a finite verb. The past participle “defined” (= “that is defined”) correctly modifies “style.”

items.passage: Today, the marathon is fixed at 42.195 kilometers, a distance that runners around the world train for years to complete. Curiously, organizers of the 1908 London Olympics chose _______ the course so that it would begin at Windsor Castle and end in front of the royal box, and the resulting distance later became the official standard.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The verb “chose” is followed by an infinitive: “chose to arrange.” (Compare decide to, plan to, agree to.)

items.passage: Analyses of ancient DNA have led some geneticists to propose that farming spread across Europe mainly through the migration of farmers rather than through the adoption of agriculture by local hunter-gatherers. This model _______ that incoming populations almost entirely replaced existing ones cannot be accepted, some archaeologists counter, until evidence of intermarriage between the two groups has been accounted for.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Read to the end: the main verb of “This model” is “cannot be accepted.” The blank must therefore be a nonfinite modifier of “model”: “This model implying that... cannot be accepted.” Any finite choice gives the subject two main verbs.

items.passage: In the graphic memoir Persepolis, Iranian-born author Marjane Satrapi uses stark black-and-white drawings rather than conventional prose _______ her experience of growing up in Tehran during and after the 1979 revolution.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The main verb is “uses.” The blank gives the purpose of using drawings, so an infinitive is needed: “uses... drawings... to recount her experience.” The finite choices create a second main verb.

items.passage: In the mid-fifteenth century, Johannes Gutenberg’s workshop in Mainz produced roughly 180 copies of a Latin Bible using movable metal type. Regarded as the first major book printed in Europe by this method, the Gutenberg Bible is admired for the clarity and evenness of its pages, its surviving copies _______ by libraries and museums as among the most valuable books in the world.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: After the comma comes an absolute phrase (noun + participle): “its surviving copies now treasured by libraries.” A finite verb here (“are,” “were,” “have been”) would create a second independent clause joined only by a comma—a comma splice.

items.passage: In her 1962 book Silent Spring, marine biologist Rachel Carson documented how the pesticide DDT was accumulating in food chains and killing birds. Today, the book _______ widely credited with launching the modern environmental movement in the United States.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “Today” signals a present state, so the simple present “is” is required.

items.passage: Launched in 1977 to study Jupiter and Saturn, NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft completed its planetary flybys by 1980 and then continued toward the edge of the solar system. By the time it crossed into interstellar space in 2012, the probe _______ more than 18 billion kilometers from Earth.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “By the time it crossed... in 2012” sets a past reference point; the traveling was completed before that point, so the past perfect “had traveled” is required.

items.passage: Memory and its unreliability are recurring concerns in Kazuo Ishiguro’s fiction. In The Remains of the Day, for example, the butler Stevens reconsiders decades of loyal service during a drive through the English countryside, while in Never Let Me Go, the narrator Kathy _______ her years at a secluded boarding school whose true purpose she only gradually comes to understand.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Events in a literary work are described in the present tense, and the parallel verbs “reconsiders” and “comes” are present. “Recalls” keeps the tense consistent.

items.passage: In 1968, Spencer Silver, a chemist at the company 3M, was trying to develop an exceptionally strong adhesive when he instead produced a weak one that could be peeled away without leaving a residue. Years later, his colleague Art Fry realized that the adhesive could keep bookmarks from slipping out of his hymnal. Soon afterward, Fry _______ coating small sheets of paper with it, and the Post-it Note was born.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The passage narrates a sequence of completed past events (“realized,” “was born”). The simple past “proposed” keeps the sequence; the past perfect would wrongly place this event BEFORE Fry’s realization.

items.passage: Water droplets inside a cumulonimbus cloud are carried upward by powerful air currents, freezing and accumulating layer upon layer of ice until they _______ a weight the updraft can no longer support, at which point they fall to the ground as hailstones.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The sentence describes a general, repeated process in the simple present (“are carried,” “fall”). “Reach” matches.

items.passage: Unlike most desert mammals, the kangaroo rat (Dipodomys) can go its entire life without drinking, so during the hottest and driest months of the year, it _______ on the small amount of water its body produces when metabolizing the dry seeds it eats.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The sentence states a general fact about the species in the present tense (“can go,” “produces,” “eats”), so the simple present “relies” is correct.

items.passage: The Year Without a Summer followed the eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia in April 1815. During 1816, volcanic ash and gases in the atmosphere _______ temperatures across much of the Northern Hemisphere. Snow even fell in New England in June.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The event took place in 1816 and the neighboring verbs (“followed,” “fell”) are in the simple past, so “lowered” is correct.

items.passage: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington State was celebrated at its opening as the third-longest suspension bridge in the world. On November 7, 1940, the bridge’s deck _______ violently in a steady wind and then tore apart. No one died, but after only four months in service the original bridge was gone.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: A specific past date (“On November 7, 1940”) and the parallel verb “tore” require the simple past “twisted.” The present perfect cannot be used with a finished, dated time.

items.passage: The ancient Chinese game of Go is played on a grid of nineteen horizontal and nineteen vertical lines. Players take turns placing black or white stones on the grid’s intersections; surrounding a group of the opponent’s stones _______ a player to remove them from the board and claim the territory they occupied.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the gerund phrase “surrounding a group of the opponent’s stones,” which is singular (the nearby plural “stones” is not the subject). Only “permits” is singular.

items.passage: Colson Whitehead’s The Underground Railroad (2016), which imagines the historical network of safe houses as a literal subterranean train line, won both the National Book Award and the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. The awards brought Whitehead a far wider readership, but his fiction _______ praised before. His 2001 novel John Henry Days, for instance, was a finalist for the Pulitzer.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject “his fiction” is singular, and “before” signals experience up to now, so the singular present perfect “has been” is correct. The other choices are plural.

items.passage: Zora Neale Hurston’s Mules and Men (1935), a collection of African American folktales and songs that the author gathered in Florida and Louisiana, _______ folklorists’ understanding of the oral traditions that flourished in Black communities of the rural South.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the title Mules and Men, a single book, so the verb must be singular even though the title contains plural nouns. Ignore the appositive between the commas (“a collection of... folktales and songs”).

items.passage: Chemists Dmitri Mendeleev and Lothar Meyer independently developed early versions of the periodic table, a chart that _______ the chemical elements according to recurring patterns in their properties.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: In the relative clause, “that” refers to the singular noun “a chart,” so the verb must be singular: “arranges.” The plural “Mendeleev and Meyer” and “versions” are not the subject of this clause.

items.passage: The Harlem Renaissance of the 1920s saw the emergence of numerous literary magazines, publications that gave young Black writers a national audience. Among the magazines’ most influential editors _______ Jessie Redmon Fauset, literary editor of The Crisis.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The sentence is inverted: the subject follows the verb. The subject is “Jessie Redmon Fauset,” one person, so the singular “was” is correct. “Editors” is the object of the preposition “among.”

items.passage: In many of his woodblock prints from the 1830s, Japanese artist Katsushika Hokusai sought to convey the presence of Mount Fuji from dozens of vantage points, filling the foreground with fishermen, travelers, and laborers. Notably, the mountain framed by these busy human scenes _______ often among the smallest elements in the composition.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
