items.explanation: The subject is the singular “the mountain”; “framed by these busy human scenes” is a modifier whose plural noun “scenes” does not affect the verb. Only “is” is singular.

items.passage: A researcher who publishes findings without sharing the underlying data makes it difficult for others to verify the results. For this reason, many journals now encourage authors to deposit their data in public repositories. Making these data sets freely available _______ that other scientists can attempt to reproduce an experiment’s conclusions.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the gerund phrase “Making these data sets freely available,” which is singular. The plural “data sets” is the object of “making,” not the subject.

items.passage: In her 1974–79 installation The Dinner Party, artist Judy Chicago set a triangular table with thirty-nine elaborate place settings. These place settings, each crafted in a style evoking the era of the woman it honors and arranged along a table nearly fifteen meters long on each side, _______ figures ranging from the ancient poet Sappho to the painter Georgia O’Keeffe.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Cross out the long interrupter between the commas. The subject is the plural “These place settings,” so the plural “commemorate” is required; the singular nouns inside the interrupter (“woman,” “table,” “side”) are traps.

items.passage: In his 1983 book Imagined Communities, political scientist Benedict Anderson first developed at length his account of nationalism—the idea that the shared texts a population reads in a common language (newspapers, novels, official documents, etc.) _______ a sense of belonging among millions of people who will never meet one another.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject of the clause is the plural “the shared texts.” “A population reads in a common language” is a relative clause modifying “texts,” and the parenthesis is an interrupter. The verb must be plural: “foster.”

items.passage: “I came, I saw, I conquered.” This famous line is attributed to the Roman general Julius Caesar. It’s an example of asyndeton, a rhetorical device that _______ speed and force by omitting the conjunctions that would normally join a series of clauses.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “That” refers to the singular “a rhetorical device,” so the verb in the relative clause must be singular: “conveys.”

items.passage: In her photograph Migrant Mother, taken in California in 1936, Dorothea Lange shows a weary woman flanked by two of her children. Such stark images, made by Lange, a photographer employed by the federal Resettlement Administration, _______ the hardships endured by farmworkers during the Great Depression.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the plural “Such stark images.” Everything between the commas—including the singular nouns “Lange,” “photographer,” and “Administration”—is an interrupter. The plural “document” is correct.

items.passage: Milkweed plants produce bitter compounds called cardenolides to discourage animals from eating their leaves. However, in some cases, the compounds the plant makes to defend itself against herbivores actually _______ its appeal to certain insects. The monarch caterpillar, for example, not only tolerates cardenolides but stores them in its own tissues, becoming poisonous to birds.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the plural “the compounds”; “the plant makes to defend itself against herbivores” is a relative clause describing them. The verb must be plural: “enhance.”

items.passage: One of the oldest surviving star charts is a Chinese manuscript discovered in a cave near Dunhuang and thought to date from about 700 CE. The chart _______ more than 1,300 stars, groups them into constellations, and includes captions naming each one.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject “The chart” is singular, and the verb must be parallel to “groups” and “includes” (singular simple present): “depicts.”

items.passage: Laboratory methods for editing genes are transforming agricultural research, according to many plant biologists. The recent achievements of researchers at the International Rice Research Institute, the organization whose high-yield variety IR8 helped avert famine in Asia in the 1960s, _______ to the continuing importance of publicly funded crop science in feeding a growing population.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the plural “achievements,” not “Institute,” “organization,” or “variety.” Cross out the prepositional phrases and the appositive between the commas, and the verb must be plural: “testify.”

items.passage: Biologists studying humpback whales, the baleen whales known for their long migrations and complex songs, have long relied on the fact that the pattern of markings on the underside of each whale’s tail flukes, like the pattern of ridges on a person’s fingertips, _______ distinctive enough to identify an individual.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the singular “the pattern.” “Of markings on the underside of each whale’s tail flukes” is a chain of prepositional phrases, and “like the pattern of ridges...” is an interrupter. The singular present “is” is correct.

items.passage: Interest in bioluminescence, the process by which living organisms produce light through chemical reactions, is growing because of fieldwork by marine biologists—many of whom, like deep-sea researcher Edith Widder, _______ the phenomenon to learn how animals communicate in the darkness of the open ocean.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject of the clause is “many (of whom),” which is plural. “Like deep-sea researcher Edith Widder” is an interrupter and does not make the subject singular. The plural “investigate” is correct.

items.passage: The sonnet sequence, a form popularized in sixteenth-century England, balances unity and independence. Literary scholars note that each one of the 154 poems in Shakespeare’s sequence, while sharing the meter, rhyme scheme, and recurring concerns of the poems around it, _______ capable of being read as a complete work in its own right.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “Each one” is always singular, no matter what plural noun follows “of.” The singular “is” is correct.

items.skill: Subject–verb agreement ("in conjunction with" doesn't pluralize)
items.passage: Physicist Lise Meitner, together with her nephew Otto Frisch and the chemists Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann, _______ credited with the discovery of nuclear fission. Although Hahn alone received the 1944 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the work, it was Meitner and Frisch who first explained the physics behind his puzzling experimental results.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the singular “Physicist Lise Meitner.” A phrase beginning with “together with” (like “along with” or “in conjunction with”) does not make the subject plural. The singular “is” is correct.

items.passage: Programs designed to encourage retirement saving can be remarkably effective, behavioral economists have found, when the programs change the default option: for example, one large company saw participation rise sharply after new employees were enrolled automatically and then asked whether _______ wished to opt out.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun refers to the plural noun “new employees,” so “they” is required. “It” is singular; “one” and “you” shift the person.

items.passage: American astronomers Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson shared the 1978 Nobel Prize in Physics for detecting the cosmic microwave background, the faint radiation left over from the early universe, but it would be misleading to say that the two men set out to find it. _______ discovery began as an effort to eliminate a persistent hiss from a radio antenna in New Jersey.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: A plural possessive is needed to show that the discovery belongs to Penzias and Wilson: “Their.” “They’re” and “It’s” are contractions (they are / it is); “Its” is singular.

items.passage: Researchers report that, unlike most other fish, cleaner wrasses (Labroides dimidiatus) seem able to recognize _______ in a mirror, a capacity previously documented in only a handful of mammals and birds.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The wrasses are both the ones recognizing and the ones recognized, so a reflexive pronoun is needed, and it must be plural to match “wrasses”: “themselves.” “Them” would refer to some other group; “it/itself” are singular.

items.passage: Kenyan environmentalist Wangari Maathai, founder of the tree-planting Green Belt Movement, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in October 2004, making _______ the first time the committee had honored an African woman.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun refers to a single event (Maathai’s receiving the prize) and is renamed by the singular “the first time,” so the singular “this” is correct.

items.passage: When they were first carried on the streets of London in the mid-eighteenth century, umbrellas were met with open hostility. The city’s hackney coachmen, who earned much of their income on rainy days, denounced the devices because the drivers considered _______ unwelcome rivals to their covered carriages.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun refers to the plural “umbrellas” / “the devices” (and is renamed by the plural “rivals”), so the plural object pronoun “them” is required.

items.passage: Thousands of glass-plate photographs examined by astronomer Williamina Fleming and her colleagues at the Harvard College Observatory have recently been digitized. _______ photographs record the spectra of stars that Fleming used to develop an early system of stellar classification.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The determiner must agree with the plural noun “photographs” that follows it: “These photographs.”

items.passage: When a given ecosystem—coral reefs and kelp forests are two familiar examples—depends on a single species to keep the populations of other organisms in check, _______ dramatic changes if that species disappears. Such organisms are known as keystone species.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The antecedent is the singular “a given ecosystem” (the plural examples between the dashes are an interrupter), so the singular personal pronoun and verb are needed: “it often undergoes.” “This” is not used alone to refer back to a specific noun in this way.

items.passage: In 1960, British primatologist Jane Goodall recorded two chimpanzee behaviors that overturned long-standing assumptions about the species: toolmaking and meat eating. Within a few years, _______ accepted by most scientists as evidence that the boundary between humans and other animals was less sharp than previously believed.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun refers to the two behaviors (toolmaking and meat eating), so the plural “they were” is correct. “Some were” would illogically mean only part of the two.

items.passage: In architect Lina Bo Bardi’s 1968 design for the São Paulo Museum of Art, absent are the interior walls that typically divide a museum into separate rooms. In _______ place stand rows of glass easels, each holding a single painting that appears to float in the open hall.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun refers to the plural “the interior walls,” so the plural possessive “their” is needed. “They’re” and “it’s” are contractions; “its” is singular.

items.passage: In 1911, Polish-born physicist Marie Curie received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for isolating radium, eight years after sharing the prize in physics. When war broke out in 1914, she set her research aside. After equipping a fleet of vehicles with portable X-ray machines, _______ training some 150 women to operate the equipment and helping surgeons locate shrapnel in wounded soldiers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: Curie drove to the front lines herself,
options.B: the front lines were where Curie herself drove,
options.C: Curie’s drive to the front lines began,
options.D: it was Curie who drove to the front lines herself,

items.explanation: “After equipping a fleet of vehicles...” describes the person who did the equipping—Curie—so “Curie” must be the subject immediately after the comma. “The front lines,” “Curie’s drive,” and “it” did not equip anything (dangling modifier).

items.passage: Although prized for being lightweight, rechargeable, and capable of storing large amounts of energy, _______ they rely on cobalt and other metals that are costly to mine, and they can overheat dangerously if damaged.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: two notable drawbacks are associated with lithium-ion batteries:
options.B: there are two notable drawbacks to lithium-ion batteries:
options.C: lithium-ion batteries have two notable drawbacks:
options.D: lithium-ion batteries’ two notable drawbacks are that

items.explanation: The opening phrase describes the things that are prized for being lightweight and rechargeable—the batteries—so “lithium-ion batteries” must be the subject right after the comma. In the other choices the subject is “there” or “drawbacks,” so the modifier dangles.

items.passage: In evaluating the career of Mexican painter Frida Kahlo, _______ have overlooked her equally sustained interest in the conventions of Mexican folk art, such as the small devotional paintings known as retablos.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: Kahlo’s turbulent personal life has been the emphasis of many biographers, who
options.B: many biographers have emphasized Kahlo’s turbulent personal life but
options.C: there are many biographers who have emphasized Kahlo’s turbulent personal life, but they
options.D: the emphasis of many biographers has been on Kahlo’s turbulent personal life; they

items.explanation: The people “evaluating the career” are the biographers, so “many biographers” must directly follow the introductory phrase. The other choices begin with “Kahlo’s... life,” “there,” or “the emphasis,” none of which can evaluate.

items.passage: Scholars once believed that people first fermented beverages in the Middle East roughly 5,000 years ago. However, since analyzing residues on 9,000-year-old pottery fragments from the village of Jiahu in northern China, _______ arose much earlier and in more than one region.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: archaeochemist Patrick McGovern’s argument is that the practice
options.B: the argument archaeochemist Patrick McGovern has made is that the practice
options.C: archaeochemist Patrick McGovern has argued that the practice
options.D: the practice, archaeochemist Patrick McGovern has argued,

items.explanation: The one who analyzed the residues is McGovern, so “archaeochemist Patrick McGovern” must be the subject after the comma. In the other choices the subject is “argument” or “the practice”—neither analyzed anything.

items.passage: Chinese pharmacologist Tu Youyou was a researcher whose work has saved millions of lives. Recognized with a Nobel Prize in 2015 as one of the most significant medical advances of the twentieth century, _______ gave doctors a powerful new treatment for malaria.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: in 1972 Tu extracted the compound artemisinin, which
options.B: the compound artemisinin was extracted by Tu in 1972 and
options.C: Tu extracted the compound artemisinin in 1972; it
options.D: Tu’s 1972 extraction of the compound artemisinin

items.explanation: What was recognized as “one of the most significant medical advances” is the extraction (an achievement), not Tu herself, so “Tu’s 1972 extraction” must follow the comma. Beginning with “Tu” or “in 1972 Tu” wrongly makes the person the “advance.”

items.passage: In 2003, the city of Seoul began dismantling an elevated highway in order to uncover the Cheonggyecheon, a stream that had been paved over decades earlier, and to line its banks with vegetation. By drawing cooler air through the dense city center, _______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: the restored stream has lowered summer temperatures in the surrounding neighborhoods by several degrees.
options.B: the restored stream’s lowering of summer temperatures in the surrounding neighborhoods by several degrees has been achieved.
options.C: summer temperatures in the surrounding neighborhoods have been lowered by several degrees by the restored stream.
options.D: the lowering of summer temperatures in the surrounding neighborhoods by several degrees has been achieved by the restored stream.

items.explanation: What draws cooler air through the city? The restored stream. It must therefore be the subject right after the modifier. The other choices begin with “the lowering,” “the restored stream’s lowering,” or “summer temperatures,” none of which draws air.

items.passage: The first woman to earn a degree from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, _______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: the 1880s were the years in which Ellen Swallow Richards conducted pioneering surveys of water quality across Massachusetts.
options.B: Massachusetts was where Ellen Swallow Richards conducted pioneering surveys of water quality in the 1880s.
options.C: pioneering surveys of water quality across Massachusetts were conducted by Ellen Swallow Richards in the 1880s.
options.D: Ellen Swallow Richards conducted pioneering surveys of water quality across Massachusetts in the 1880s.

items.explanation: The opening phrase describes a person (“The first woman to earn a degree...”), so the person’s name must come right after the comma. “The 1880s,” “Massachusetts,” and “surveys” are not the first woman.

items.passage: Assembled from thousands of flattened liquor-bottle caps and stitched together with copper wire by teams of assistants in the artist’s Nigerian studio, _______ so supple and shimmering that viewers often mistake them for woven cloth.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: when he creates his wall hangings, Ghanaian sculptor El Anatsui makes them
options.B: the wall hangings of Ghanaian sculptor El Anatsui are
options.C: the Ghanaian sculptor El Anatsui creates wall hangings that are
options.D: El Anatsui is a Ghanaian sculptor whose wall hangings are

items.explanation: What is “assembled from... bottle caps and stitched together”? The wall hangings, not the artist. “The wall hangings” must be the subject after the comma.

items.passage: Hoping to solve the problem of determining a ship’s longitude at sea, _______ up with a practical method. Clockmaker John Harrison eventually claimed most of the reward for his marine chronometer.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: up to £20,000 would be paid to anyone by the British Parliament under a prize established in 1714 for coming
options.B: the British Parliament established a prize in 1714 that would pay up to £20,000 to anyone who came
options.C: a payment of up to £20,000 would go to anyone under a prize established by the British Parliament in 1714 for coming
options.D: a prize established by the British Parliament in 1714 would pay up to £20,000 to anyone who came

items.explanation: Who was “hoping to solve the problem”? The British Parliament. It must be the subject after the comma. A prize, a payment, and a sum of money cannot hope.

items.passage: Compared to that of a typical bony fish, _______ the animal’s tissues retain high levels of urea, keeping its internal fluids nearly as salty as seawater.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: a shark’s blood chemistry is far more concentrated, giving the shark a significant advantage in the ocean:
options.B: a shark has a significant advantage in the ocean due to its far more concentrated blood chemistry:
options.C: a significant advantage of a shark in the ocean is that its blood chemistry is far more concentrated:
options.D: a shark has far more concentrated blood chemistry, resulting in a significant advantage in the ocean:

items.explanation: “That of a typical bony fish” means “the blood chemistry of a bony fish,” so it must be compared with “a shark’s blood chemistry,” not with “a shark” or “a significant advantage.” Compare like with like.

items.skill: Semicolon between independent clauses ｜ 分號連接兩獨立子句
items.passage: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor. They support roughly a quarter of all known marine ______ many of these species are found nowhere else. Reefs also protect coastlines and support fishing and tourism industries. Rising ocean temperatures, however, threaten their survival. When water becomes too warm, corals expel the algae that live in their tissues and turn white.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses with no conjunction need a semicolon (or period). A comma = comma splice; nothing = run-on; "which" makes the sentence ungrammatical.
items.mk: [1|They support roughly a quarter of all known marine species]⟨;⟩ [2|many of these species are found nowhere else].

items.skill: Semicolon between independent clauses ｜ 分號連接兩獨立子句
items.passage: Rubber trees are native to the Amazon rainforest. In the nineteenth century, demand for rubber soared as factories began producing tires, hoses, and waterproof clothing. In 1876, the British explorer Henry Wickham shipped about 70,000 rubber tree seeds from Brazil to ______ seedlings grown from them were later sent to British colonies in Asia. The decision followed the discovery of other icy objects of similar size beyond Neptune. To be considered a planet, an object must clear other material from its orbit, which Pluto has not done.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Even though" introduces a dependent clause after the main clause; a comma is fine, but a semicolon, period, or colon leaves a fragment.
items.mk: [1|The International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006]⟨,⟩ «even though»[d|many people objected to the change].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: A cheetah can accelerate from 0 to about 95 kilometers per hour in roughly three seconds. Its flexible spine and long legs allow it to cover up to seven meters in a single stride. Though the cheetah is the fastest land ______ it can maintain its top speed for only about 20 to 30 seconds. After a chase, it must rest before eating, and larger predators sometimes steal its meal. For this reason, cheetahs often hunt during the day, when lions and hyenas are less active.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" (conjunction) + dependent clause + COMMA + main clause. Adding "however" is redundant and creates an error.
items.mk: «Though»[d|the cheetah is the fastest land animal]⟨,⟩ [1|it can maintain its top speed for only about 20 to 30 seconds].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: Titan is the largest of Saturn's many moons. It is even bigger than the planet Mercury. Though smaller than ______ Titan has an atmosphere that is denser than Earth's. items.explanation: "Though smaller than Mars" is a shortened dependent clause; follow it with a comma before the main clause.

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞

items.explanation: "Though" (= however) interrupts subject and verb: pair of commas.
items.mk: [1:Subject|Teenagers]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|need even more][p|, about eight to ten hours].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: Robots have taken over many repetitive tasks in car factories and warehouses. They can weld, paint, and lift heavy parts with great precision. items.explanation: "Though" (= however) ends the first clause → ", though;".

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: Koalas live in the eucalyptus forests of eastern Australia. Though it is often called a koala ______ koala is not a bear at all. To save energy, they sleep for up to 20 hours a day.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" already signals contrast; the dependent clause needs only a comma. Adding "however" is redundant and ungrammatical.
items.mk: «Though»[d|it is often called a koala bear]⟨,⟩ [1|the koala is not a bear at all].

why.D: “Though it is often called a koala bear.” = fragment.

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived. Though it can grow to about 30 meters long, it feeds almost entirely on krill, tiny shrimp-like animals. items.mk: [1:Subject|Recent studies]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|suggest] [d:noun clause|that blue whales remember the locations of past feeding grounds].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: Polynesian navigators settled islands across a vast area of the Pacific Ocean, from Hawaii to New Zealand. Genetic studies suggest that Polynesians and Native South Americans met around 1200 ______ exactly where and how they met remains uncertain. items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" here is a conjunction; a dash (or comma) can attach its clause. A semicolon, period, or colon leaves "though…" as a fragment.
items.mk: [1|Genetic studies suggest that Polynesians and Native South Americans met around 1200 CE]⟨—⟩«though»[d|exactly where and how they met remains uncertain].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the tallest mountain in Africa. Although it lies just south of the equator, its summit has been capped with ice for thousands of years. Rising temperatures and drier air are both thought to play a role.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: ", though." ends a sentence (though = however); a new sentence follows. ", though, more" = comma splice.
items.mk: [1|That ice is disappearing quickly]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨.⟩ [2|More than 80 percent of the mountain's ice has vanished since 1912].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: Mercury orbits closer to the sun than any other planet. Its daytime temperatures can reach about 430°C. Nevertheless, Mercury is not the hottest ______ even though it is the closest to the sun. That title belongs to Venus, whose thick atmosphere traps heat. Because Mercury has almost no atmosphere, its nighttime temperatures plunge to about –180°C.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Even though" clause after the main clause: comma OK; a period, semicolon, or colon creates a fragment.
items.mk: {Nevertheless}, [1|Mercury is not the hottest planet]⟨,⟩ «even though»[d|it is the closest to the sun].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: For decades, most scientists doubted that plants could communicate. In recent ______ studies have shown that some plants release chemicals that warn their neighbors of insect attacks. When caterpillars chew on certain plants, the plants release airborne chemicals. Nearby plants detect these signals and begin producing substances that make their leaves less tasty. Some researchers describe this as a kind of plant communication, though others prefer more cautious terms.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" (= however) follows the introductory phrase inside one clause: pair of commas. Compare the last sentence, where ", though others prefer…" uses "though" as a conjunction.
items.mk: [p|In recent years]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1|studies have shown] [d:noun clause|that some plants release chemicals that warn their neighbors of insect attacks].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: The heart beats roughly 100,000 times each day. Though only about the size of a ______ it pumps around 7,000 liters of blood through the body daily. Blood travels through a network of vessels that would stretch about 100,000 kilometers if laid end to end. That is long enough to circle Earth more than twice. The heart's steady rhythm is controlled by electrical signals from a small cluster of cells called the sinoatrial node.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though only about the size of a fist" is a shortened dependent clause; follow it with a comma.
items.mk: «Though»[d:shortened clause|only about the size of a fist]⟨,⟩ [1|it pumps around 7,000 liters of blood through the body daily].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: Chili peppers get their heat from a compound called capsaicin. Eating a hot pepper can make the mouth feel as if it is on fire. No real damage occurs in most ______ simply triggers the same nerve receptors that respond to actual heat. Birds, which spread pepper seeds, lack these receptors. As a result, they can eat even the hottest peppers without discomfort.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: ", though." ends the sentence; a new sentence begins. ", though, capsaicin…" = comma splice.
items.mk: [1|No real damage occurs in most cases]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨.⟩ [2|Capsaicin simply triggers the same nerve receptors that respond to actual heat].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: A desert is defined by how little precipitation it receives, not by its temperature. Many people picture deserts as places of burning sand and blazing sun. Though many deserts are ______ some, like the Gobi Desert in Asia, are bitterly cold in winter. Temperatures in the Gobi can drop below –40°C. Snow sometimes covers its dunes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" (conjunction) clause + comma + main clause.
items.mk: «Though»[d|many deserts are hot]⟨,⟩ [1|some, like the Gobi Desert in Asia, are bitterly cold in winter].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: On a clear night, most stars appear white to the naked eye. Viewed through a ______ stars display a range of colors from deep red to bright blue. A star's color reveals its surface temperature. Red stars are the coolest, while blue stars are the hottest. Our sun, a yellowish star, falls somewhere in the middle.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" (= however) follows the introductory phrase and needs commas on both sides. Never use "however" and "though" together.
items.mk: [p:intro phrase|Viewed through a telescope]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1|stars display a range of colors from deep red to bright blue].

items.skill: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞
items.passage: Penguins are usually associated with ice and snow. In fact, many penguin species live in temperate climates in South America, Africa, Australia, and New Zealand. Penguins are found almost entirely in the Southern ______ though one species, the Galápagos penguin, lives near the equator. Cool ocean currents bring cold, nutrient-rich water to the Galápagos Islands, allowing the penguins to survive there. No penguins live naturally in the Arctic.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" (conjunction) clause after the main clause: comma. Other marks create a fragment.
items.mk: [1|Penguins are found almost entirely in the Southern Hemisphere]⟨,⟩ «though»[d|one species, the Galápagos penguin, lives near the equator].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞
items.passage: Many deserts receive less than 25 centimeters of rain a year. Plants in these environments must store water whenever it becomes available. The saguaro cactus has pleated stems that can expand like an accordion after a ______ a single large saguaro can absorb hundreds of liters of water in a day. This stored water allows the cactus to survive months of drought. Its waxy skin and spines further reduce water loss.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "In fact" is a transition that begins the second independent clause: semicolon before, comma after. A comma before it creates a comma splice.
items.mk: [1|The saguaro cactus has pleated stems that can expand like an accordion after a storm]⟨;⟩ {in fact}⟨,⟩ [2|a single large saguaro can absorb hundreds of liters of water in a day].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞
items.passage: Penguins cannot fly, but they are superb swimmers. Their wings have evolved into stiff flippers that propel them through the water. Their bones are also denser than those of flying ______ the birds can dive deep without struggling against buoyancy. Emperor penguins have been recorded diving more than 500 meters below the surface. Some of their dives last over twenty minutes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Therefore" begins a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after. ", therefore," between clauses is a comma splice.
items.mk: [1|Their bones are also denser than those of flying birds]⟨;⟩ {therefore}⟨,⟩ [2|the birds can dive deep without struggling against buoyancy].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞
items.passage: Many animals use tools, a behavior once thought to be uniquely human. Chimpanzees strip leaves from twigs and use them to fish termites from their mounds. Some sea otters use rocks to crack open shellfish while floating on their backs. These examples suggest that tool use has evolved independently many times.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "For example" introduces a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
items.mk: [1|Birds can be skilled tool users as well]⟨;⟩ {for example}⟨,⟩ [2|New Caledonian crows shape twigs into hooked tools to pull insects out of tree bark].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞
items.passage: The kakapo is a large, flightless parrot found only in New Zealand. Introduced predators such as cats and stoats nearly drove it to extinction. By 1995, only about 50 birds remained. items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

items.mk: [1|The kakapo breeds slowly, and many of its eggs are infertile]⟨;⟩ {nevertheless}⟨,⟩ [2|conservationists have steadily increased its population by moving the birds to predator-free islands].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞
items.passage: Vampire bats are the only mammals that feed entirely on blood. They live in Central and South America and usually feed on cattle, horses, and birds. Their saliva contains a substance that keeps blood from clotting. Scientists have studied this substance, called draculin, as a possible medicine for stroke patients.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Instead" begins a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
items.mk: [p|Despite their reputation,] [1|vampire bats do not suck blood]⟨;⟩ {instead}⟨,⟩ [2|they make a small cut with their sharp teeth and lap up the blood with their tongues].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞

One such species, Coffea stenophylla, was rediscovered in the wild in Sierra Leone in 2018.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Consequently" begins a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
items.mk: [1|Rising global temperatures are making some traditional growing regions too hot]⟨;⟩ {consequently}⟨,⟩ [2|farmers in some countries are moving their coffee fields to higher, cooler elevations].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞
items.passage: Walking is one of the simplest forms of exercise. items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Moreover" starts a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
items.mk: [1|It requires no special equipment, and most people can do it almost anywhere]⟨;⟩ {moreover}⟨,⟩ [2|studies link regular walking to lower rates of heart disease, diabetes, and depression].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞

These borrowed words reflect centuries of trade, conquest, and cultural exchange.

items.explanation: "For example" interrupts subject and verb: pair of commas.
items.mk: [1:Subject|The word ketchup]⟨,⟩ {for example}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|probably comes from a Hokkien Chinese word for a fermented fish sauce].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞

Bamboo is now being promoted as a sustainable building material.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Period + "As a result," starts a new sentence. A comma before it creates a comma splice.
items.mk: [1|Some species can grow nearly a meter in a single day]⟨.⟩ {As a result}⟨,⟩ [2|bamboo can be harvested far more often than timber from trees].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞

There are exceptions, however, and some moths are as colorful as any butterfly.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "In contrast" interrupts subject and verb: pair of commas.
items.mk: [1:Subject|Most moths]⟨,⟩ {in contrast}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|are active at night and tend to have duller colors that help them hide].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞

Columbus survived only because the Americas lay between Europe and Asia.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Instead" begins the second clause: semicolon before, comma after.
items.mk: [1|The experts who doubted Christopher Columbus's plan did not think the Earth was flat]⟨;⟩ {instead}⟨,⟩ [2|they believed he had greatly underestimated the distance from Europe to Asia].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞
items.passage: In the 1960s, the United States and the Soviet Union raced to land people on the Moon. No one has returned since the final Apollo mission.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Meanwhile" begins the second clause: semicolon before, comma after.
items.mk: [1|The Soviet Union achieved many early firsts, including the first satellite and the first human in orbit]⟨;⟩ {meanwhile}⟨,⟩ [2|the United States invested heavily in the Apollo program].

items.skill: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞
items.passage: Beavers are sometimes called ecosystem engineers. Using branches, mud, and stones, they build dams across streams. These dams slow the flow of ______ they help reduce flooding and erosion downstream. The ponds that form behind the dams provide habitats for fish, frogs, birds, and insects. In some regions, conservationists have reintroduced beavers to help restore damaged wetlands.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Thus" begins the second independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
items.mk: [1|These dams slow the flow of water]⟨;⟩ {thus}⟨,⟩ [2|they help reduce flooding and erosion downstream].

items.passage: Within hours of hatching, the chicks of megapodes, a family of ground-dwelling birds, can run, feed themselves, and even fly. The chicks of most songbirds, _______ emerge blind and featherless and must be fed by their parents for weeks. This difference in development reflects a trade-off: megapode eggs are unusually large and rich in yolk, allowing the embryo to mature fully before it hatches.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Songbird chicks are helpless, the opposite of the independent megapode chicks; the next sentence even names “this difference.” “By contrast” is logical.

items.passage: In 1845, Frederick Douglass was enjoying what must have seemed like an extraordinary reception in Great Britain and Ireland. He was lecturing to enthusiastic crowds and, for the first time in his life, moving about without fear of being captured and returned to slavery. _______ Douglass was determined to go back to the United States; only there, he felt, could he work effectively for abolition.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Despite the ideal circumstances just described, Douglass wanted to leave. “Still” signals this concession/contrast.

items.passage: Before a performance, American pianist Keith Jarrett typically insists on a carefully selected concert grand piano. _______ for a 1975 concert in Cologne, Germany, he agreed to play an undersized, poorly tuned instrument with malfunctioning pedals; forced to avoid the piano’s weakest registers, he produced an improvisation whose recording became one of the best-selling solo piano albums in history.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The Cologne concert is an exception to Jarrett’s usual practice (“typically insists”), so a contrast transition is needed: “Nevertheless.”

items.passage: For decades, textbooks identified the Nile, at roughly 6,650 kilometers, as the longest river on Earth. _______ according to a 2007 expedition by Brazilian scientists who traced the Amazon to a more distant source in southern Peru, the Amazon is slightly longer, extending about 6,800 kilometers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The 2007 claim contradicts the long-accepted view stated in the first sentence, so “However” is logical.

items.passage: Scholars agree that Thomas Edison was overstating his role when he presented himself as the sole inventor of the incandescent light bulb. Few would dispute, _______ that Edison’s systematic testing of thousands of filament materials helped make electric lighting commercially practical.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence concedes a point in Edison’s favor after the first sentence criticized him. “Though” signals this contrast.

items.passage: According to Bergmann’s rule, populations of warm-blooded animals living in cold climates tend to have larger bodies, which lose heat more slowly relative to their volume. _______ populations of the same or closely related species living in warm climates tend to be smaller, a build that allows excess body heat to escape more readily.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence presents the opposite situation (warm climates → smaller bodies), so “Conversely” is logical.

items.passage: In his classic studies of tide pools on the coast of Washington State, ecologist Robert Paine observed that mussels crowded the rocks in the middle of the intertidal zone. In the lowest part of the zone, _______ sea stars that prey on mussels kept the rocks nearly clear of them.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The lowest part of the zone (few mussels) differs from the middle of the zone (crowded with mussels), so the contrast transition “on the other hand” is logical.

items.passage: Structures that carry water across valleys on rows of arches are known as aqueducts, from the Latin for “water conduit.” Although such elevated arcades are the most famous feature of ancient Rome’s water system, Roman engineers rarely built them when an alternative existed. _______ the water traveled through underground channels, which were cheaper to construct and easier to protect.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: “Rarely” in the previous sentence sets up a comparison of frequency: arcades were rare; underground channels were the usual solution. “More often” completes this contrast.

items.passage: Upon first seeing the ceiling of the church of Sant’Ignazio in Rome, a visitor might assume that a soaring dome rises above the crossing. _______ by skillfully applying the rules of perspective to a flat canvas, the painter Andrea Pozzo produced only the appearance of a dome.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence corrects the false assumption in the first (there is no real dome), so “On the contrary” is logical.

items.passage: When a Venus flytrap’s sensitive trigger hairs are touched twice in quick succession, the plant sends an electrical signal that causes its leaf lobes to snap shut around an insect, beginning the process of digestion. _______ when a hair is touched only once, as by a falling raindrop, the trap remains open.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence describes the opposite situation (one touch → trap stays open), so “By contrast” is logical.

items.passage: The feathers of a barn owl’s wings have comb-like serrations along their leading edges and soft fringes along their trailing edges. These structures break up the air flowing over the wing into smaller, quieter currents. _______ barn owls are able to approach their prey in near silence.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Silent flight is the consequence of the feather structures described in the previous sentences, so the cause-and-effect transition “As a result” is logical.

items.passage: Flight muscles are among the most energetically expensive tissues a bird maintains, and the benefits of flight depend largely on the need to escape predators. _______ from an evolutionary standpoint, birds on islands that lack ground-dwelling predators should invest less in these muscles. Island species such as the kakapo, a flightless parrot of New Zealand, offer a chance to examine this prediction.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence is a logical conclusion drawn from the first (costly muscles + no predators → less investment); the passage even calls it a “prediction.” “Thus” is logical.

items.passage: In the 1950s, experimental archaeologists in Denmark felled trees using replicas of 5,000-year-old polished flint axes. When they tested the tools, they found that three people could clear about 500 square meters of forest in four hours. _______ the researchers, aware that pollen records showed a sudden decline of forests in the region at the time such axes appeared, concluded that early farmers could have cleared the land themselves with stone tools.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The researchers’ conclusion follows from what they observed in the experiment, so “Therefore” is logical.

items.passage: Japanese craftspeople developed a repair technique known as kintsugi, in which a broken ceramic vessel is mended with lacquer mixed with powdered gold. This technique involves highlighting each crack rather than hiding it. _______ the repaired vessel displays a network of gleaming seams that record its history.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The gleaming seams are the result of the technique described in the previous sentence, so “As a result” is logical.

items.passage: Bats take to the air at dusk, flapping and gliding much as swallows and swifts do. _______ bats are often mistakenly grouped with birds, whose wings are supported by fused arm bones and covered in feathers, when in fact bats are mammals whose wings consist of membranes stretched between greatly elongated finger bones.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Because bats fly as birds do, people mistakenly group them with birds: the second sentence is a consequence of the first, so “Hence” is logical.

items.passage: To compare the brightness of stars reliably, astronomers need a scale that does not depend on how far a star happens to be from Earth. _______ they developed the concept of absolute magnitude, which describes how bright a star would appear if it were located exactly 10 parsecs away. The scale allows stars at vastly different distances to be compared directly.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The need described in the first sentence is the reason astronomers developed absolute magnitude, so “For this reason” is logical.

items.passage: In recent decades, one of the lessons of ecology has been that a species’ survival depends on many factors, not the least of which is its interactions with the other organisms that share its habitat. _______ rather than concentrating solely on individual endangered species, many conservation programs have begun to protect entire ecosystems, including the full range of plants and animals found in them.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Conservation programs changed their approach in response to the lesson described in the first sentence, so “Accordingly” (= as a consequence) is logical. The second sentence is an action, not a restatement or an example.

items.passage: In retrospect, given how many mathematicians in the 1600s were studying tangents, areas, and rates of change, the invention of calculus was a natural next step. It is perhaps unsurprising, _______ that Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz developed the method independently. Indeed, the history of science offers many instances of a major idea emerging from several thinkers at once.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence draws an inference from the first (calculus was a natural next step → no surprise that two people developed it). “Then” (= therefore) is logical.

items.passage: As the Sun heats the ocean near the equator, enormous quantities of water evaporate, and this warm, moist air rises and cools high in the atmosphere. The cooling air, _______ releases its moisture as the heavy rains that sustain tropical forests.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The passage describes a chain: heating → rising, cooling air → rain. “In turn” signals the next link in a chain of effects.

items.passage: Renowned for its prehistoric paintings of bulls, horses, and deer, Lascaux Cave was once a major tourist destination in southwestern France. However, by the early 1960s the carbon dioxide and moisture exhaled by more than a thousand daily visitors were visibly damaging the images. _______ French authorities closed the cave to the public in 1963 so that specialists could work to preserve the 17,000-year-old artworks.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The closure was a consequence of the damage described in the previous sentence, so “As a result” is logical.

items.passage: Biologist Lynn Margulis’s research on cell structure provided strong evidence that mitochondria and chloroplasts descended from free-living bacteria that were engulfed by other cells and survived inside them (rather than arising gradually within their host cells). _______ Margulis’s work is a challenge to the view that evolution proceeds solely through competition among organisms, since it shows that cooperation between species can produce major innovations.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Because of what her research demonstrated, Margulis’s work challenges the competition-only view. “As such” introduces this consequence.

items.passage: If the Moon had formed elsewhere in the solar system and later been captured by Earth’s gravity, its rocks would be expected to differ markedly from Earth’s in their mix of oxygen isotopes. The isotope ratios in lunar samples are nearly identical to those of Earth’s mantle, however. _______ the Moon most likely formed from material blasted out of the young Earth itself, probably during a collision with a Mars-sized body.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The final sentence is the conclusion drawn from the evidence (the capture model’s prediction fails), so “Hence” is logical.

items.passage: In 1987, the Montreal Protocol was adopted by dozens of nations. The treaty requires participating countries to phase out the production of chlorofluorocarbons, chemicals that damage the ozone layer. _______ the agreement, as amended in 1990, obliges wealthier nations to contribute to a fund that helps developing countries adopt safer alternatives.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence adds a second, separate requirement of the same treaty, so “In addition” is logical. The fund is not an example or a more precise statement of the phase-out.

items.passage: Florence Price was an American composer whose Symphony No. 1 was premiered by the Chicago Symphony Orchestra in 1933. Raised in Arkansas, Price drew openly on her African American heritage in her music. For example, she replaced the traditional scherzo movement of her symphony with a juba, a dance that originated among enslaved people. _______ she wove melodies in the style of spirituals into many of her works.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The last sentence gives a second way Price drew on her heritage, after the first example, so “In addition” is logical.

items.passage: Medieval European cathedrals relied on stained-glass windows to fill their vast interiors with colored light. _______ the windows served to teach biblical stories to worshippers who could not read, according to many historians.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence adds another function of the windows (teaching), different from the first (light), so “In addition” is logical.

items.passage: Mycorrhizal fungi are organisms that grow in close association with the roots of most land plants. These fungi help plants absorb phosphorus from the soil. _______ they help plants take up water during dry periods.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The last sentence adds a second benefit the fungi provide, so “Additionally” is logical.

items.passage: Some astronomers have opposed plans to launch tens of thousands of new communications satellites into low Earth orbit, concerned that the bright streaks the satellites leave in telescope images would obscure faint objects (and thus compromise long-term surveys of the sky). _______ the researchers worry that radio signals from the satellites would interfere with observatories designed to detect weak emissions from distant galaxies.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence gives another, separate concern of the same astronomers, so “Additionally” is logical.

items.passage: In the 1930s, federal relief programs employed artists across the United States to create works for public buildings. In San Francisco, painters covered the interior of Coit Tower with murals depicting California agriculture and industry. _______ in Harlem, artists led by Charles Alston painted murals for the wards of Harlem Hospital.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The Harlem artists did the same kind of thing as the San Francisco painters—a parallel case—so “Similarly” is logical. It is not an example OF the San Francisco sentence.

items.passage: In her novel Homegoing, Yaa Gyasi links the private lives of two half sisters’ descendants to major historical developments. She sets the experiences of one family line in what is now Ghana against the expansion of British colonial rule. _______ Gyasi places the other line’s story in the United States within the larger history of slavery, segregation, and the Great Migration.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Gyasi treats the second family line in the same way as the first (private story set within a larger history), so “Similarly” is logical.

items.passage: Although mammals and birds are usually regarded as the only warm-blooded animals, a few fish have evolved the ability to keep their bodies warmer than the surrounding water. The opah, _______ circulates heated blood throughout its body, allowing it to remain active in the cold depths where it hunts.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The opah is one specific case of the “few fish” described in the previous sentence, so “for example” is logical.

items.passage: Plants have evolved a number of remarkable strategies for scattering their seeds away from the parent plant. The seeds of the sandbox tree (Hura crepitans), _______ are flung as far as 40 meters when the tree’s ripe fruit explodes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sandbox tree is one specific instance of the “remarkable strategies” mentioned in the first sentence, so “for example” is logical.

items.passage: Most birds are active during the day and rest at night. That is, they are diurnal. However, not all bird species follow this pattern. The kiwi of New Zealand, _______ forages almost exclusively after dark.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The kiwi is an example of a bird species that does not follow the daytime pattern (the claim in the previous sentence), so “for instance” is logical. The contrast was already signaled by “However.”

items.passage: In 1980, physicist Luis Alvarez and his son, geologist Walter Alvarez, proposed that the mass extinction that ended the age of the dinosaurs was caused by an asteroid striking Earth. _______ their hypothesis held that dust thrown into the atmosphere by the impact blocked sunlight for months, halting photosynthesis and collapsing food chains.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence gives precise details of how the hypothesis worked, elaborating on the general statement before it. “Specifically” is logical.

items.passage: During the Tang dynasty, trade along the Silk Road reshaped daily life in the Chinese capital of Chang’an, driven largely by growing demand for imported goods and fashions. The popularity of Central Asian music, dance, and clothing, _______ gave the city’s elite a strikingly cosmopolitan culture.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence singles out certain imports (music, dance, clothing) from the general category just mentioned, so “in particular” is logical.

items.passage: In 1928, Indian physicist C. V. Raman discovered that a small fraction of light changes wavelength when it is scattered by molecules. His finding proved enormously useful to chemists. _______ it gave them a way to identify a substance by the distinctive pattern of light it scatters, a method now known as Raman spectroscopy.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The last sentence explains exactly HOW the finding was useful, so “Specifically” is logical.

items.passage: Ocean tides—the regular rise and fall of sea level along coastlines—result, generally speaking, from the Moon’s gravity. _______ the Moon pulls more strongly on the side of Earth nearest to it than on Earth’s center, drawing the ocean into a bulge. As Earth rotates, coastlines pass through this bulge and experience high tide.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence gives a general cause (“generally speaking”); the second gives the precise mechanism. “Specifically” is logical.

items.passage: In his 1962 book The Structure of Scientific Revolutions, US philosopher Thomas Kuhn disputed the prevailing account of how scientific knowledge advances. _______ Kuhn argued that instead of accumulating steadily through the addition of new facts, science periodically undergoes abrupt “paradigm shifts” in which one framework for understanding the world replaces another.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence states precisely how Kuhn disputed the prevailing account, so “Specifically” is logical.

items.passage: Urban planners report that although cities long treated rainwater as a nuisance to be channeled away as quickly as possible, attitudes have begun to move in the opposite direction. _______ municipalities are designing parks, plazas, and streets to absorb and store stormwater—a trend reflected in the growing number of so-called sponge city projects worldwide.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence describes a growing trend (“have begun to move,” “a trend,” “the growing number”), so “Increasingly” is logical. It is not a result, a parallel case, or an additional point.

items.passage: Jhumpa Lahiri’s 2003 novel The Namesake traces the experiences of the Ganguli family after Ashoke and Ashima emigrate from Calcutta to Massachusetts. Ashoke immerses himself in his work as an engineering professor. _______ Ashima struggles with isolation, longing for the relatives she left behind. Over time, however, she builds a community of fellow Bengali immigrants.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Ashima’s experience takes place during the same period as Ashoke’s, so “Meanwhile” is logical.

items.passage: Beneath the jungle canopy of northern Guatemala lie the remains of Maya cities so extensive that they cannot be fully mapped on foot. Archaeologists have known of the largest sites since the nineteenth century, when explorers first described their overgrown temples, and they have been surveying the region ever since. _______ researchers’ work is accelerated by lidar, an airborne laser technology that reveals structures hidden under the trees.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The passage moves from the past (“since the nineteenth century”) to the present situation, so the time transition “Currently” is logical. Nothing is being contrasted.

items.passage: Paleontologist Jack Horner has offered several reasons for thinking that the duck-billed dinosaur Maiasaura cared for its young. First, fossilized nests contain the remains of juveniles too large to be newly hatched, suggesting that the young stayed in the nest. _______ the worn teeth of these juveniles indicate that food was being brought to them.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: “First” introduces the first reason; the next sentence gives another reason in the same list, so “Second” is logical.

items.passage: In 1878, a constitutional amendment granting women the right to vote was first introduced in the US Congress. The measure failed, but suffragists persisted. Their allies had the amendment reintroduced in nearly every session of Congress for the next four decades. _______ in 1919, both chambers approved it, and it was ratified the following year.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Approval came at the end of a long series of attempts, so “Finally” is logical.

items.passage: During its first test flight in 1996, the European Space Agency’s Ariane 5 rocket suffered a catastrophic failure: a software error caused it to veer off course and self-destruct less than a minute after liftoff. _______ rather than concealing the cause, the agency convened an independent board of inquiry and published its findings in full, and the report became a standard case study for software engineers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The inquiry happened after the failure, so the time transition “Afterward” is logical.

items.passage: Around 1800, French confectioner Nicolas Appert devised a method of preserving food that became the basis of modern canning. In Appert’s process, a cook first packed the food into thick glass bottles. _______ the cook sealed the bottles tightly with cork and wax. Lastly, the cook submerged them in boiling water for several hours.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The steps are listed in order: “first... [blank]... Lastly.” The sequence transition “Next” is logical.

items.passage: In 1992, Mae Jemison became the first African American woman to travel into space, serving as a mission specialist aboard the space shuttle Endeavour. _______ in 1994, Jemison founded an international science camp, The Earth We Share, to encourage students to work on global problems.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second event (1994) happened after the first (1992), so “Later” is logical.

items.passage: When the Human Genome Project began in 1990, sequencing a single human genome was expected to take fifteen years and cost about $3 billion. _______ a human genome can be sequenced in about a day for less than $1,000.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The passage compares the situation in 1990 with the situation now, so the time transition “Today” is logical.

items.passage: After a site has been selected, the traditional construction of a Mongolian ger, or yurt, begins with the builders standing collapsible wooden lattice walls in a circle. Then, long poles are fitted between the top of the lattice and a central roof ring. _______ the frame is covered with layers of felt and tied down with ropes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: This is the last step in a process (“begins with... Then... [blank]”), so “Finally” is logical.

items.passage: When Kenyan runner Eliud Kipchoge completed a marathon in Vienna in 2019 in 1 hour, 59 minutes, and 40 seconds, he reached a milestone in athletics. _______ no one had covered the distance in under two hours, making Kipchoge’s run, though not eligible as an official world record, a historic first.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence describes the situation before Kipchoge’s run (note the past perfect “had covered”), so “Previously” is logical.

items.passage: Psychologist Elizabeth Loftus wanted to determine whether the wording of a question can alter a person’s memory of an event. She first showed volunteers films of automobile collisions. _______ she asked some of them how fast the cars were going when they “smashed into” each other and asked others the same question using the word “hit.”
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: “She first...” is followed by the next step in the procedure, so “Next” is logical.

items.passage: Art historians note that the painter J. M. W. Turner frequently reworked his canvases in the days before an exhibition opened, adding details while the pictures hung on the gallery wall. However, the change he made to one seascape in 1832 astonished even his fellow painters; _______ his rival John Constable compared Turner’s last-minute addition of a single red buoy to the firing of a gun.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Constable’s remark reinforces and intensifies the claim that the change “astonished even his fellow painters,” so “in fact” is logical.

items.passage: With his 2003 installation The Weather Project, Danish-Icelandic artist Olafur Eliasson succeeded in turning a vast industrial hall at London’s Tate Modern into a communal yet dreamlike space. _______ when visitors entered the hall and saw the enormous glowing sun suspended in mist at its far end, many lay down on the floor and gazed upward for long stretches—as if basking on a beach at sunset.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence confirms and emphasizes the claim in the first (the space was communal and dreamlike), so “Indeed” is logical.

items.passage: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, built into a mountainside on a Norwegian island in the Arctic, is known for the scale of its collection. _______ the vault holds more than one million seed samples from nearly every country in the world.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence supports and emphasizes the first with a specific figure, so “In fact” is logical.

items.passage: When, in the late 1950s, physician Cicely Saunders began planning a new kind of hospital in London, one of her aims was for dying patients to receive care focused on comfort rather than cure. _______ she founded St. Christopher’s Hospice, which opened in 1967 and combined expert pain relief with emotional support for patients and their families.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence states an aim; the second describes the action taken to achieve it. “To that end” (= for that purpose) is logical.

items.passage: When a crop is threatened by insect pests, farmers can spray their fields with chemical insecticides. _______ the pests can be managed through biological control: natural enemies such as parasitic wasps or lady beetles are released to prey on the insects, reducing their numbers without leaving chemical residues on the harvest.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Biological control is a different option from the one in the first sentence (spraying), so “Alternatively” is logical.

items.passage: In writing about the centuries after 1492, historian Alfred Crosby urged scholars to stop treating the movement of plants, animals, and diseases between the hemispheres as a series of isolated events. _______ he argued, these transfers should be understood as a single process, which he named the Columbian Exchange. The term, he held, captured how profoundly the two hemispheres had reshaped each other’s ecosystems.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Crosby wanted scholars to stop doing one thing and adopt a replacement view, so “Instead” is logical.

items.passage: In 1705, English astronomer Edmond Halley argued that the comets recorded in 1531, 1607, and 1682 were a single object and predicted that it would return in 1758. Halley did not live to see the prediction tested, but the comet reappeared on schedule. _______ the comet has been known ever since as Halley’s Comet, in honor of the man who first recognized its orbit.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Naming the comet after the person who predicted its return is an appropriate outcome, so “Fittingly” is logical.

items.skill: Comma + FANBOYS (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so)
items.passage: The archivist catalogued the damaged ______ scanned each page at high resolution.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Scanned" shares the subject "the archivist"; there is no second subject, so this is ONE clause with a compound verb. Do not put a comma (or semicolon) before "and" when it joins two verbs.

items.skill: The Semicolon Between Two Independent Clauses
items.passage: Radio astronomers detecting fast radio bursts initially struggled to isolate their stellar ______ subsequent observations using the CHIME telescope confirmed that magnetars were a primary source.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Both sides are independent clauses, so a semicolon works. A is a comma splice, C a run-on, and D puts an unnecessary comma after "and."

items.skill: Conjunctive Adverbs Starting the Second Clause: “; however,” / “. However,”
items.passage: Cognitive load theory posits that working memory can process only a limited number of information chunks ______ instructional designers must structure educational software to minimize unnecessary mental effort.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Therefore" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction; it cannot join clauses by itself. Use a semicolon before it and a comma after it. A is a comma splice; C and D are run-ons.

items.skill: Conjunctive Adverbs Starting the Second Clause: “; however,” / “. However,”
items.passage: Pine seedlings inoculated with ectomycorrhizal fungi demonstrate enhanced phosphorus ______ uninoculated seedlings in nutrient-poor soils exhibit severely stunted root development.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by the transition "by contrast": semicolon before, comma after. The contrast describes the second clause, so the transition belongs at its start. A is a comma splice; C is a run-on; D attaches "by contrast" to the wrong clause.

items.skill: Conjunctive Adverbs Starting the Second Clause: “; however,” / “. However,”
items.passage: Economists evaluating microfinance initiatives observed significant improvements in local ______ during periods of macroeconomic instability, small-business survival rates remained fragile.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "However" introduces a contrast with the second clause. Start a new sentence (or use a semicolon) before it, and put a comma after it. A and D are comma splices; C is a run-on.

items.skill: Conjunctive Adverbs Starting the Second Clause: “; however,” / “. However,”
items.passage: The expedition reached the summit two days ahead of ______ the descent took twice as long as planned because of a sudden blizzard.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses; "however" contrasts the second with the first: semicolon before, comma after. B is a comma splice; C is a run-on; D omits the comma after the adverb.

items.skill: Conjunctive Adverbs Interrupting One Clause: “, however,”
