items.passage: Quantum entanglement links pairs of particles so that measuring one instantly reveals information about the other, even across vast distances. This ______ cannot be used to send messages faster than the speed of light.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Here "however" sits inside a single independent clause ("This phenomenon...cannot be used..."), interrupting subject and verb. An interrupter takes paired commas. B and C put a semicolon between a subject and its verb; D leaves the interrupter unclosed.

items.skill: Conjunctive Adverbs Interrupting One Clause: “, however,”
items.passage: Everyone called the young linguist a walking dictionary; he ______ disliked the nickname and asked colleagues to use his name instead.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The semicolon after "dictionary" already separates the two clauses. In the second clause, "however" interrupts the subject ("he himself") and the verb ("disliked"), so it needs a comma on both sides.

items.skill: Conjunctive Adverbs Interrupting One Clause: “, however,”
items.passage: Most critics praised the film’s groundbreaking visual effects. Its ______ was widely considered weak and predictable.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: There is only one clause ("Its screenplay…was widely considered weak"), and "however" interrupts its subject and verb, so paired commas are needed. A semicolon (B, D) would split the subject from its verb.

items.passage: The new bridge was completed in record time. Its construction costs were far higher than originally ______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: A sentence-final "though" (= however) takes a comma before it and the period after it. A semicolon or colon cannot introduce a single adverb.

items.passage: ______ the museum is small, its collection of Ming dynasty ceramics is considered one of the finest in the world.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Here "though" means "although": it is a conjunction that begins a dependent clause, so no comma follows it. The comma after "small" ends the dependent clause. C creates a comma splice.

items.passage: The mountain trail is only three kilometers ______ it climbs nearly 900 meters from the parking lot to the summit.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Here "though" = "although" and begins a dependent clause, which is joined to the main clause with a comma. C and D cut the dependent clause off as a fragment; B puts the comma in the wrong place.

items.passage: Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein was published more than two centuries ago. The ______ still raises urgent questions about scientific responsibility.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" (= however) interrupts one independent clause between its subject ("The novel") and verb ("raises"), so it takes a comma on both sides. B and C put a semicolon between subject and verb.

items.passage: Most residents supported building a new public library. The city council rejected the ______ it cited rising construction costs as its main concern.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Though" contrasts the council's decision with the residents' support (the previous sentence), so it ends the first clause: comma before it, then a semicolon at the clause boundary. B wrongly makes the second clause contrast with the first; C and D are comma splices.

items.skill: The Colon Introducing a List or a Specific Item
items.passage: Traditional Mandé drumming ensembles rely on three bass drums, known collectively as dunun, to anchor their polyrhythmic ______ the dununba, the sangban, and the kenkeni.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: An independent clause announces "three bass drums," and a list names them. A colon introduces a list after a complete clause. A semicolon (B) cannot introduce a list that isn't an independent clause.

items.skill: The Colon Introducing a List or a Specific Item
items.passage: Industrial chemists searching for a cost-effective alternative to platinum catalysts focused their research on a single abundant ______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: A colon can introduce a single word that names or specifies what the clause announced ("a single abundant element"). A semicolon or period (B, C) would need an independent clause after it; D says the chemists studied two things, which is illogical.

items.skill: Colon Traps: No Colon After a Verb, “such as,” or “including”
items.passage: Among the primary advantages of early movable-type printing presses ______ rapid duplication of text, decreased production costs, and increased literacy across Europe.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The sentence is inverted: the subject is the list ("rapid duplication..., decreased costs, and increased literacy") and the verb is "were." No punctuation may separate a verb from its subject/complement. A colon needs a complete clause before it—"Among the advantages were" is not complete.

items.skill: Colon Traps: No Colon After a Verb, “such as,” or “including”
items.passage: The urban wetland restoration project aimed to preserve habitat for vulnerable bird species such ______ the blue heron, the snowy egret, and the belted kingfisher.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Such as" already introduces the examples; it is never followed by a colon, semicolon, or comma. A colon also requires a complete clause before it.

items.skill: Colon Traps: No Colon After a Verb, “such as,” or “including”
items.passage: The three finalists in this year’s international robotics competition ______ teams from Seoul, Nairobi, and Monterrey.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "The three finalists…were" is not a complete clause until the verb has its complement, so no colon (or any punctuation) may separate "were" from "teams from Seoul, Nairobi, and Monterrey."

items.skill: Colon Traps: No Colon After a Verb, “such as,” or “including”
items.passage: The museum’s new Asian art wing displays artifacts ______ jade carvings, bronze vessels, and silk scrolls from the Song dynasty.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Including" (like "such as") already introduces the examples, so no punctuation follows it.

items.skill: Colon Traps: No Colon After a Verb, “such as,” or “including”
items.passage: The bakery’s famous sourdough bread requires only three ______ flour, water, and salt.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "The bakery's famous sourdough bread requires only three ingredients" is a complete clause that announces a list, so a colon is correct. B uses a semicolon before a list; C puts a colon after "such as"; D creates a second verb with no subject.

items.skill: Commas After Introductory Elements and Dependent Clauses
items.passage: Although sauropod dinosaurs possessed air-filled bones that reduced overall skeletal ______ their massive body weight still required column-like limbs for support.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Although..." makes the first part a dependent clause. A dependent clause joins the main clause with a comma. A semicolon or period (A, C) would leave the "Although" clause as a fragment.

items.skill: Commas After Introductory Elements and Dependent Clauses
items.passage: Because synthetic RNA guides can target specific DNA sequences with unprecedented ______ bioengineers can disable defective genes without disrupting surrounding cellular structures.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Because..." is a dependent clause; it attaches to the main clause with a comma. A semicolon or period leaves a fragment, and a single dash may follow only an independent clause.

items.skill: Other Essential Elements: “that” Clauses, Titles of Works, Essential Phrases
items.passage: Students ______ the advanced literature course must complete a summer reading assignment before the first class.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Enrolled in the advanced literature course" tells WHICH students (essential), so no commas. With commas (C) the sentence would say that all students are enrolled; A separates the subject from its verb.

items.passage: Linguists studying ancient Sumerian cuneiform tablets, ______ have discovered that sentence syntax rules shifted rapidly during the Early Dynastic Period.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: many of whom were previously skeptical
options.B: many of whom were previously skeptical,
options.C: many of whom were previously skeptical;
options.D: many of whom, were previously skeptical

items.explanation: The comma after "tablets" opens a nonessential relative clause ("many of whom were previously skeptical"). It must be closed with a matching comma before the main verb "have discovered."

items.passage: Langston Hughes's poetry collection The Weary Blues, published in 1926 during the height of the Harlem ______ fused traditional verse structures with blues rhythms.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The comma after the title opens a nonessential participial phrase; it must close with the matching mark—another comma—before the verb "fused." A mixes a comma with a dash.

items.passage: Neural pathways governing motor-skill acquisition—once believed to solidify permanently during early ______ remain remarkably adaptable throughout adulthood.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The interrupter opened with a dash after "acquisition," so it must close with a dash before the verb "remain." Never mix a dash with a comma (B).

items.passage: The Great Barrier ______ the largest living structure on Earth—is visible from space.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The interrupter "arguably the largest living structure on Earth" closes with a dash, so it must also open with a dash. B mixes a comma with a dash.

items.passage: Three spices—cumin, coriander, and ______ form the base of many South Asian curries.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The list is an interrupter that opened with a dash after "spices," so it must close with a dash before the verb "form."

items.skill: Participial Phrases (分詞構句) at the End of a Sentence, Including “thus / thereby + -ing”
items.passage: Merchants traversing the Pamir Mountains during the Han Dynasty exchanged woven silk and lapis lazuli for Central Asian ______ significantly altering the economic trajectory of regional trade networks.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Significantly altering..." is a participial phrase (no subject, no finite verb) describing a result of the main clause. It attaches with a comma. A semicolon or colon (C, D) would need an independent clause after it; A runs the phrase into "horses."

items.skill: Participial Phrases (分詞構句) at the End of a Sentence, Including “thus / thereby + -ing”
items.passage: Engineers added a second spillway to the ______ the risk of overflow during spring floods.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Thus reducing the risk…" is a participial phrase showing a result, not an independent clause, so it attaches with a comma. A and C leave the phrase as a fragment; D adds an unnecessary comma.

items.skill: Participial Phrases (分詞構句) at the End of a Sentence, Including “thus / thereby + -ing”
items.passage: The city replaced its entire fleet of diesel buses with electric ______ its transportation emissions by nearly forty percent.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Thereby cutting…" is a result phrase: comma before "thereby," then the -ing participle. B leaves a fragment; C uses a verb with no subject; D misplaces the comma.

items.skill: Absolute Phrases and Appositives at the End of a Sentence
items.passage: The marathon runner crossed the finish ______ raised in triumph above her head.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Her arms raised in triumph" is an absolute phrase (noun + participle, no finite verb), so it attaches with a comma. B and C would leave it as a fragment.

items.skill: Absolute Phrases and Appositives at the End of a Sentence
items.passage: Deep-field images captured by space telescopes revealed galaxies forming merely 300 million years after the Big ______ discovery that challenged prevailing cosmological models.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "A discovery that challenged..." is a noun phrase that sums up the clause. A single dash (or a comma) attaches it. A semicolon or period (B, C) would require an independent clause; D runs the phrase in with no break.

items.passage: Reintroducing apex predators can trigger ripple effects across an entire ______ gray wolves, sea otters, and raptors all regulate herbivore populations and foster plant diversity.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: A single dash works like a colon: after a complete clause, it introduces an explanation or example. B is a comma splice; C is a run-on.

items.passage: After months of testing, the engineers finally identified the source of the ______ single loose wire in the control panel.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: After a complete clause, a single dash introduces a phrase that explains or specifies (here, what the source was). A semicolon or period (B, C) would need an independent clause after it.

items.passage: Because the storm had knocked out power across the ______ students finished their final exams by candlelight.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Because the storm had knocked out power…" is a dependent clause. It attaches to the main clause with a comma. A single dash, semicolon, or period can follow only an independent clause.

items.passage: For her solo hike across the desert, the explorer packed only what she truly ______ water, a compass, and a detailed map.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The clause is complete, and what follows is a list that specifies what she needed. A single dash (like a colon) introduces it. A semicolon cannot introduce a list; C and D run the clause into the list.

items.passage: The space telescope revealed something no astronomer had ______ appeared to orbit two stars at the same time.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: A single dash after the complete clause introduces the noun phrase that specifies the "something." B and C leave "a planet that appeared…" as a fragment; D inserts an incorrect comma before the essential clause "that appeared…"

items.skill: Where Punctuation Is Illegal: Subject–Verb, Verb–Object, Preposition–Object
items.passage: The dinosaur nests discovered in the Gobi Desert by the joint Mongolian-American research ______ that some species laid their eggs in large colonies.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The long subject is "The dinosaur nests discovered…by the joint Mongolian-American research team," and "reveal" is its verb. No punctuation may separate a subject from its verb.

items.skill: Semicolons + Commas in a Complex Series (Three Ideas)
items.passage: The international preservation team included Dr. Kenzo Sato, an urban preservationist from Tokyo ______ Dr. Maria Alvarez, an architectural historian from Madrid ______ and Thomas Wright, a structural engineer from London.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Each list item already contains a comma (name, description). To keep the three items distinct, separate them with semicolons at both blanks.

items.skill: Semicolons + Commas in a Complex Series (Three Ideas)
items.passage: The science fair’s top prizes went to Priya Nair, a ninth grader from ______ Marcus Lee, whose solar-powered water filter impressed the judges; and Elena Ruiz, a senior from Austin, Texas.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The items already contain commas (name, description), and the last item begins with "; and," so each item must end with a semicolon. The comma between the city and state stays inside the item: "Dayton, Ohio;".

items.skill: Apostrophes with Pronouns: its / it's, their / they're / there
items.passage: The machine-learning algorithm adjusts ______ internal parameters during training to minimize errors, ensuring that ______ capable of making accurate real-time predictions.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Blank 1 shows possession (the algorithm's parameters): its—no apostrophe. Blank 2 means "it is capable": the contraction it's. "Its'" is never correct.

items.skill: Apostrophes with Pronouns: its / it's, their / they're / there
items.passage: After three hours of debate, the selection committee announced that ______ decision on the scholarship winners would be final.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The decision belongs to the committee (a singular collective noun), so the possessive "its" is needed. "It's" = it is; "they're" = they are; "there" is a place word.

items.skill: Apostrophes with Pronouns: its / it's, their / they're / there
items.passage: Sea otters are among the few mammals that use tools; ______ able to crack open shellfish by pounding them against stones balanced on their chests.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The blank needs a subject + verb: "they are able." The contraction "they're" = they are. "Their" is possessive, "there" is a place word, and "its" is singular possessive.

items.skill: Question Marks: Direct vs. Indirect Questions
items.passage: Researchers wanted to understand ______ The team designed an experiment that offered bees identical sugar water in dishes of different colors.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: why do bees prefer blue flowers?
options.D: why do bees prefer blue flowers.

items.explanation: The question is reported inside a statement ("Researchers wanted to understand why..."), so it is an indirect question: statement word order (bees prefer) and a period.

items.skill: Question Marks: Direct vs. Indirect Questions
items.passage: Linguists have long debated ______ Some argue that it began with gestures; others believe it began with song.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The question is reported inside a statement ("Linguists have long debated how…"), so it is an indirect question: statement word order (language originated) and a period.

items.skill: Commas with Conjunctive Adverbs: however, though, thus, therefore
items.passage: The river’s water level had fallen below the town’s intake ______ had to be trucked in from a neighboring county for three weeks.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by "therefore": semicolon before, comma after. B is a comma splice, C a run-on, and D misplaces the comma between the subject "drinking water" and its verb.

items.skill: Participial Phrases (分詞構句) and Commas
items.passage: Having spent a decade studying coral reefs in the Indian Ocean, ______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: the bleaching event did not surprise marine biologist Ana Ruiz.
options.B: marine biologist Ana Ruiz was not surprised by the bleaching event.
options.C: Ana Ruiz’s surprise at the bleaching event was minimal.
options.D: there was little surprise for Ana Ruiz about the bleaching event.

items.explanation: The person who spent a decade studying reefs is Ana Ruiz, so she must be the subject immediately after the comma. A, C, and D make the event, her surprise, or "there" the one who studied reefs.

items.skill: Participial Phrases (分詞構句) and Commas
items.passage: The volcano erupted without ______ ash across three neighboring villages.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Scattering ash…" is a participial phrase describing a result of the eruption; it attaches with a comma. B and C leave a fragment; D creates a second verb with no subject.

items.skill: Participial Phrases (分詞構句) and Commas
items.passage: ______ in 1851, Moby-Dick sold poorly during Herman Melville’s lifetime but is now considered one of the greatest American novels.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The novel was published (passive meaning), so the past participle "Published" is correct. A and C would mean the novel did the publishing.

items.skill: Semicolons + Commas to Separate Three Ideas (Complex Series)
items.passage: He enjoys reading Shakespeare’s tragedies, such as Romeo and Juliet, a classic example of dramatic ______ Othello, a study of jealousy and racial ______ and Macbeth, an iconic portrait of destructive ambition.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Each item contains an internal comma (title, appositive), so the items are separated by semicolons at both blanks, with "; and" before the last item.

items.skill: Semicolons + Commas to Separate Three Ideas (Complex Series)
items.passage: The music festival featured three ______ Ana Tijoux, a Chilean rapper; Bombino, a guitarist from Niger; and Hiromi, a Japanese jazz pianist.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "The music festival featured three headliners" is a complete clause that announces a list, so a colon introduces it. A semicolon (B) cannot introduce a list; C and D run the clause into the list.

items.skill: Semicolons + Commas to Separate Three Ideas (Complex Series)
items.passage: During the survey, the research team visited ______ Quito, Ecuador; and La Paz, Bolivia.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Each item is "city, country." The comma stays inside the item (Lima, Peru), and a semicolon ends the item to match the "; and La Paz, Bolivia" pattern.

items.skill: Finite Verbs in Relative Clauses (who / that / which + verb)
items.passage: The Rosetta Stone, a granite slab discovered in 1799, bears a decree that ______ in three scripts: Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic, and ancient Greek. This feature allowed scholars to decipher hieroglyphs for the first time.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The relative clause "that ___ in three scripts" needs a finite verb, and "was written" is finite (past, passive). A, B, and D are nonfinite forms, so the "that" clause would have no verb.

items.skill: Finite Verbs in Relative Clauses (who / that / which + verb)
items.passage: Botanist Ynes Mexía, who began her scientific career at the age of fifty-five, collected more than 145,000 plant specimens, including some 500 species that ______ previously unknown to science.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The clause "that ___ previously unknown to science" describes "species" and needs a finite, plural verb: "were." "Being," "having been," and "to be" are nonfinite and leave the relative clause incomplete.

items.skill: Finite Verbs in Relative Clauses (who / that / which + verb)
items.passage: Hedy Lamarr is often remembered as a film star, but she was also an inventor. During World War II, she co-developed a frequency-hopping ______ later influenced Wi-Fi and Bluetooth technologies.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Later influenced" needs a subject; "that" provides it and connects the essential clause to "system." Without "that" (A, C), the sentence has two verbs with nothing joining them. D incorrectly separates restrictive "that" with a comma.

items.passage: Emperor penguins survive the Antarctic winter by huddling together in dense groups of thousands, their backs ______ against the relentless polar wind.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Their backs turned against the … wind" is an absolute phrase (noun + participle) that adds detail to the complete main clause. A, C, and D are finite verbs and would join two independent clauses with only a comma (comma splice).

items.passage: For years, Marie Curie processed tons of pitchblende ore in a converted shed at the School of Physics and Chemistry in Paris, her hands ______ by the radioactive materials she handled daily.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The main clause is complete ("Marie Curie processed …"). "Her hands scarred by …" is an absolute phrase; the past participle shows the passive meaning (the hands were scarred). A, B, and C are finite and create a comma splice.

items.passage: The ancient city of Petra was carved directly into rose-colored sandstone cliffs, its elaborate facades still ______ visitors more than two thousand years after their construction.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: After the comma, "its elaborate facades ___ visitors" must be an absolute phrase, so a participle is needed. The facades do the astonishing (active), so the present participle "astonishing" is correct. B and D are finite (comma splice); C is passive and would illogically mean the facades were astonished.

items.passage: The 2021 survey of urban commuters produced striking results, nearly 80 percent of respondents ______ that they had changed their travel habits within the previous two years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Nearly 80 percent of respondents reporting that …" is an absolute phrase that explains the "striking results." A, B, and D are finite verbs and would create a comma splice.

items.skill: Infinitives: Purpose and After Certain Verbs
items.passage: In 1953, before large-scale trials began, Jonas Salk agreed ______ his experimental polio vaccine on himself and his family to demonstrate his confidence in its safety.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Agree" takes an infinitive (agree to do something), so "to test" is correct. "Agreed testing" (A) is not standard English, and C and D are finite verbs that cannot follow "agreed" directly.

items.skill: Infinitives: Purpose and After Certain Verbs
items.passage: Iraqi British architect Zaha Hadid used sweeping curves and sharply angled surfaces ______ buildings that seem to be in motion even while standing still.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The main verb is "used," so the blank should explain the purpose of using the curves: "to create buildings." A adds a second independent clause with no punctuation (run-on), and B and D are finite verbs that would give the sentence two main verbs.

items.skill: Parallel Verb Forms (after modals and in compound predicates)
items.passage: According to the engineers’ proposal, the new seawall would shield the harbor from storm surges and ______ local fishers a safer place to anchor their boats.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Both verbs follow the modal "would": the seawall would shield … and (would) provide. The base form "provide" keeps the compound predicate parallel. A and C change the form, and B uses an -ing form that is not parallel with "shield."

items.skill: Parallel Verb Forms (after modals and in compound predicates)
items.passage: Octopuses can change the color of their skin in a fraction of a second and ______ its texture to match nearby rocks, coral, or seaweed.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The modal "can" applies to both verbs: octopuses can change … and (can) alter. The base form "alter" is parallel with "change." B, C, and D do not match the base form after "can."

items.skill: Parallel Verb Forms (after modals and in compound predicates)
items.passage: During the Crimean War, Florence Nightingale collected mortality data from military hospitals, analyzed the causes of soldiers’ deaths, and ______ her findings in innovative statistical diagrams.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The three verbs share the subject "Florence Nightingale" and must all be past tense: collected, analyzed, and presented. A and D are nonfinite and break the series; B shifts to the present tense.

items.skill: Parallel Verb Forms (after modals and in compound predicates)
items.passage: To earn the certification, a laboratory must document every step of its testing process and ______ its equipment at regular intervals.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Must" governs both verbs: a laboratory must document … and (must) calibrate. After a modal, the base form is required. A, B, and C are not base forms and break the parallel structure.

items.skill: Simple Present for General Facts, Processes, and “Today”
items.passage: Honeybees communicate the location of distant flowers through a movement known as the waggle dance. The angle of the dance relative to vertical ______ the direction of the food source relative to the Sun.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The passage explains how the dance always works (communicate), a general fact in the present, so indicates is correct. Indicated and had indicated move the fact into the past; will have indicated is a future perfect with no future time point.

items.skill: Simple Present for General Facts, Processes, and “Today”
items.passage: The Rosetta Stone was discovered by French soldiers in Egypt in 1799. Today, the stone ______ in the British Museum in London, where it attracts millions of visitors each year.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “Today” and the present-tense verb attracts call for the simple present is displayed. The discovery in 1799 is past, but that date controls only the first sentence. A and B are past forms; D is a future perfect.

items.skill: Simple Past for Completed Events and Specific Past Dates
items.passage: Mathematician Katherine Johnson calculated flight paths for many early NASA missions. In 1962, astronaut John Glenn ______ that Johnson personally check the computer’s calculations before his orbital flight.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “In 1962” is a specific past date, and the passage is in the past (calculated), so the simple past requested is correct. Has requested cannot go with a finished past date; requests and will request are present and future.

items.skill: Simple Past for Completed Events and Specific Past Dates
items.passage: The Roman city of Pompeii was buried under volcanic ash when Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 CE. The eruption ______ the city so completely that its ruins remained hidden for more than 1,500 years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The eruption is a completed event in 79 CE, and the other verbs are past (was buried, erupted, remained), so preserved is correct. B is present, C is present perfect (not used with a finished past event), and D is future.

items.skill: Simple Past for Completed Events and Specific Past Dates
items.passage: In 1869, Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev ______ the known chemical elements by atomic weight, leaving gaps in his periodic table for elements that had not yet been discovered.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “In 1869” marks a completed past action, so the simple past arranged is needed. Has arranged cannot be used with a specific past year; A is present and B is future.

items.skill: Past Perfect: “By + Past Time” and the Earlier of Two Past Events
items.passage: Construction on the first transcontinental railroad in the United States began in 1863. By the time the final spike was driven at Promontory Summit, Utah, in 1869, workers ______ nearly 1,800 miles of track.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “By the time… in 1869” sets a past deadline; the track-laying was finished before it, so had laid is correct. Have laid connects to the present, lay is present, and will lay is future.

items.skill: Past Perfect: “By + Past Time” and the Earlier of Two Past Events
items.passage: When archaeologist Howard Carter opened the tomb of Tutankhamun in 1922, he found evidence that ancient robbers ______ parts of the tomb long before his arrival.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two past events: Carter’s discovery in 1922 and the robbers’ entry, which happened earlier (“long before his arrival”). The earlier event takes the past perfect had entered. B and D are present forms; C is future.

items.skill: Past Perfect: “By + Past Time” and the Earlier of Two Past Events
items.passage: By the end of the eighteenth century, new water-powered machines ______ Britain’s textile industry, replacing many of the hand-operated looms that weavers had used for generations.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “By the end of the eighteenth century” is a past deadline, so the past perfect had transformed is needed. Have transformed links the change to the present; transform and will transform are present and future.

items.skill: Past Perfect: “By + Past Time” and the Earlier of Two Past Events
items.passage: Physicist and chemist Marie Curie received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911. She ______ the Nobel Prize in Physics eight years earlier, making her the first person to win the award in two different sciences.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The Physics prize (1903) came before the 1911 Chemistry prize, and “eight years earlier” signals the earlier past event, so had won is correct. Has won connects to the present; wins is present; will have won is future perfect.

items.skill: Present Perfect: Since, For, and Up to Now
items.passage: Since its launch in 1990, the Hubble Space Telescope ______ more than 1.5 million observations, contributing data to thousands of published scientific studies.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “Since its launch in 1990” describes a period from the past up to now, so the present perfect has made is correct. Made treats the observations as finished and cut off from the present; had made stops at a past point; will make is future.

items.skill: Present Perfect: Since, For, and Up to Now
items.passage: For more than a century, scientists ______ the migration of monarch butterflies, which travel up to 3,000 miles between Canada and central Mexico each year.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “For more than a century” describes research that began long ago and continues now, so have studied is correct. Had studied would stop at a past point, study does not show the long period, and will study is future.

items.skill: Present Perfect: Since, For, and Up to Now
items.passage: The Japanese art of kintsugi repairs broken pottery with lacquer mixed with powdered gold. Up to now, conservators ______ the technique mainly on ceramics, but some designers are beginning to apply it to glass and wood.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “Up to now” and the present are beginning show a period that reaches the present, so the present perfect have used is correct. Used and had used are past forms that do not reach “now”; will use is future.

items.skill: Present Perfect: Since, For, and Up to Now
items.passage: Linguists estimate that about 7,000 languages are spoken in the world today. Since 1950, more than 200 languages ______, according to researchers who track endangered languages.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “Since 1950” sets a starting point and the counting continues to the present, so have disappeared is correct. Had disappeared stops at a past point; disappear and will disappear are present and future.

items.skill: Present Perfect: Since, For, and Up to Now
items.passage: Primatologist Jane Goodall began studying wild chimpanzees in Tanzania in 1960. Her observations ______ scientists’ understanding of primate behavior ever since.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “Ever since” means from 1960 until now, so the present perfect have shaped is required. Shaped and had shaped do not connect to the present, and shape does not show the period that began in 1960.

items.skill: Tense Consistency and the Literary Present
items.passage: In Chinua Achebe’s novel Things Fall Apart, Okonkwo works tirelessly to build his reputation in the village of Umuofia. After he accidentally kills a clansman, however, he ______ into exile for seven years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The passage describes the plot of a novel in the literary present (works, kills), so the parallel verb must be present: is sent. A and C are past forms, and D is future perfect.

items.skill: Tense Consistency and the Literary Present
items.passage: In 1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first climbers confirmed to have reached the summit of Mount Everest. They ______ only about fifteen minutes at the top before beginning their long descent.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The passage narrates a completed event in 1953 in the simple past (became), so the next event in the sequence takes the simple past spent. Spend and will spend shift the time, and have spent cannot be used for a finished past event.

items.skill: Tense Consistency and the Literary Present
items.passage: William Shakespeare’s Hamlet opens on a cold night at Elsinore Castle, where guards see the ghost of the dead king. Later in the play, the ghost ______ Hamlet that it was his own uncle, Claudius, who murdered him.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The plot of a play is described in the literary present (opens, see), so the parallel verb must be tells. Told and had told switch to the past, and will tell switches to the future.

items.skill: Find the True Subject: Ignore Prepositional Phrases and Interrupters (Singular Subjects)
items.passage: The collection of ancient manuscripts housed in the monastery’s library ______ texts written in at least six languages, including Syriac and Ge’ez.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Cross out of ancient manuscripts housed in the monastery’s library; the true subject is The collection, a singular noun. Only contains is singular. A, B, and D are plural and agree with the trap noun manuscripts.

items.skill: Find the True Subject: Ignore Prepositional Phrases and Interrupters (Singular Subjects)
items.passage: Recent measurements show that the average temperature of the ocean’s surface layers, like that of the lower atmosphere, ______ risen steadily over the past century.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the average temperature (singular). Of the ocean’s surface layers is a prepositional phrase and like that of the lower atmosphere is an interrupter. Over the past century calls for the present perfect, so singular has (risen). B is plural; C and D are plural and cannot form the present perfect with risen.

items.skill: Find the True Subject: Ignore Prepositional Phrases and Interrupters (Singular Subjects)
items.passage: Neither of the two proposed explanations for the bird’s unusual migration route ______ fully supported by the tracking data that ornithologist Ana Ruiz collected in 2021.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Neither is the subject and is singular; of the two proposed explanations is only a prepositional phrase. The singular is is correct. A, B, and C are plural forms that agree with explanations.

items.skill: Gerund and Clause Subjects Are Singular; Titles of Works Are Singular
items.passage: Whether the ancient city of Cahokia was abandoned because of flooding or because of political conflict ______ still debated among archaeologists, who continue to analyze sediment cores from the site.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the whole noun clause Whether… political conflict, and a noun clause is singular. Is (debated) agrees. A, C, and D are plural forms.

items.skill: Gerund and Clause Subjects Are Singular; Titles of Works Are Singular
items.passage: Frida Kahlo’s The Two Fridas (1939), a double self-portrait showing the artist seated beside a second version of herself, ______ among the most frequently reproduced works in the collection of Mexico City’s Museo de Arte Moderno.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the title The Two Fridas, a single painting, so it is singular even though Fridas looks plural. Is agrees; present tense fits a current fact. A, B, and D are plural.

items.skill: Agreement in Relative Clauses: The Verb Agrees with the Antecedent
items.passage: Marine biologists have long studied cleaner wrasses, small reef fish that ______ parasites and dead tissue from the bodies of larger fish.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: That refers to small reef fish, which renames the plural cleaner wrasses, so the verb must be plural: remove. A, C, and D are singular.

items.skill: Agreement in Relative Clauses: The Verb Agrees with the Antecedent
items.passage: Mae Jemison, the first African American woman to travel in space, is one of the few astronauts who ______ also trained physicians.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: In one of the few astronauts who…, who refers to astronauts (the group that has this quality), so the verb is plural are. B, C, and D are singular and wrongly agree with one or Mae Jemison.

items.skill: Inverted Sentences (“Gone are…,” “Among X is/are…”), “Each One,” and “In Conjunction With / Along With”
items.passage: The Rosetta Stone, along with dozens of other artifacts seized during the French campaign in Egypt, ______ housed in the British Museum since 1802.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is The Rosetta Stone (singular); along with dozens of other artifacts… is an interrupter and does not make the subject plural. Since 1802 requires the present perfect, so singular has been. A, C, and D are plural.

items.skill: Inverted Sentences (“Gone are…,” “Among X is/are…”), “Each One,” and “In Conjunction With / Along With”
items.passage: For decades, textbooks described the Neanderthals as brutish and unintelligent. Gone ______ such simplistic portrayals: recent discoveries of jewelry, pigments, and cave art attributed to Neanderthals have convinced most researchers that they were capable of symbolic thought.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Inverted sentence: normal order is Such simplistic portrayals are gone. The subject portrayals is plural, so are. A, B, and C are singular.

items.skill: Agreement Combined with Tense and Parallel Verbs (has/have + Present Perfect)
items.passage: Since the 1990s, sensors aboard NASA satellites ______ tracked changes in Arctic sea ice, revealing a steady decline in the ice’s summer extent.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is sensors (plural); aboard NASA satellites is a prepositional phrase. Since the 1990s requires the present perfect, so plural have (tracked). A is singular; B and D are singular and do not form the present perfect.

items.skill: Agreement Combined with Tense and Parallel Verbs (has/have + Present Perfect)
items.passage: The octopus is a master of disguise. Using specialized skin cells called chromatophores, it rapidly ______ color, alters the texture of its skin, and mimics the shapes of nearby objects.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject it (the octopus) is singular, and the other verbs in the series (alters, mimics) are singular simple present. Changes agrees and keeps the series parallel. A and C are plural; D is not a finite verb.

items.skill: Agreement Combined with Tense and Parallel Verbs (has/have + Present Perfect)
items.passage: Although the individual findings were modest, the combined results of the three-year study ______ led the city council to expand its network of bike lanes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the combined results (plural); of the three-year study is a prepositional phrase with a trap singular noun. Plural have (led) forms the present perfect. A, B, and C are singular.

items.skill: Pronoun–Antecedent Agreement: Singular (it / its; Collective Nouns)
items.passage: The International Union for Conservation of Nature updates ______ Red List of Threatened Species several times a year, reclassifying species as new population data become available.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The International Union for Conservation of Nature is one organization (a collective noun), so the possessive must be singular: its. B treats the organization as plural. C is an object pronoun, not a possessive. D (one’s) refers to a general person, not the organization.

items.skill: Pronoun–Antecedent Agreement: Singular (it / its; Collective Nouns)
items.passage: After reviewing more than three hundred submissions, the selection committee announced that ______ had chosen a design by a young Brazilian architect for the new public library.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The selection committee is a collective noun that acts as one unit, so the SAT requires the singular pronoun it. A (they) treats the committee as plural. B (we) shifts to the first person. C (those) is plural and has no clear antecedent.

items.skill: Pronoun–Antecedent Agreement: Singular (it / its; Collective Nouns)
items.passage: Unlike most other mammals, the naked mole-rat can survive for up to eighteen minutes without oxygen by switching ______ metabolism to a fructose-based pathway that does not require oxygen.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The antecedent is the naked mole-rat, a singular noun (the words most other mammals are part of an introductory phrase, not the antecedent). An animal takes its. A and D are plural and wrongly agree with mammals. B (his) is used for people, not for an animal species.

items.skill: Pronoun–Antecedent Agreement: Singular (it / its; Collective Nouns)
items.passage: The Hubble Space Telescope, along with dozens of ground-based observatories, has transformed modern astronomy; among ______ best-known achievements is a precise measurement of the rate at which the universe is expanding.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is The Hubble Space Telescope; along with dozens of ground-based observatories is an interrupter and does not create a plural antecedent (the verb has confirms the subject is singular). The possessive must be singular: its. A and C are plural and agree with the trap noun observatories. D (there) is an adverb, not a possessive.

items.skill: Reflexive Pronouns and Determiner–Noun Number (this / these, that / those)
items.passage: Unlike most spiders, the diving bell spider spends nearly its entire life underwater, where it surrounds ______ with a bubble of air held in place by a web of silk.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject it (the spider) surrounds its own body, so a reflexive pronoun is needed, and it must be singular: itself. B is plural and agrees with the trap noun spiders. C would mean the spider surrounds something else. D is plural and not reflexive.

items.skill: Reflexive Pronouns and Determiner–Noun Number (this / these, that / those)
items.passage: Researchers compared the fossilized teeth found in the upper layers of the cave with ______ found in the lower layers and concluded that the animals from the two periods had eaten very different diets.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun replaces teeth, a plural noun, so it must be plural: those (= the teeth found in the lower layers). A, C, and D are singular and would compare teeth with a single thing.

items.skill: Dangling Modifiers I: The Subject Must Come Right After an Introductory -ing / -ed Phrase
items.passage: Discovered in 1856 by workers in a cave in Germany’s Neander Valley, ______ gave its name to an entire species of ancient humans.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: workers found the partial skeleton known as Neanderthal 1, which
options.B: the partial skeleton known as Neanderthal 1
options.C: scientists named the partial skeleton Neanderthal 1, and it
options.D: it was the partial skeleton known as Neanderthal 1 that

items.explanation: What was discovered in 1856? The skeleton. B places the partial skeleton known as Neanderthal 1 right after the comma, and it is also the subject of gave. A makes the workers the thing discovered; C makes scientists the thing discovered; D begins with the empty subject it, so the modifier dangles.

items.passage: The annual migration route of the Arctic tern, which can stretch roughly 70,000 kilometers from pole to pole, is far longer than ______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The sentence compares a migration route with another route. That of any other bird (= the route of any other bird) is singular and logical. A and D compare a route with a bird. C uses the plural those, which does not match the singular route.

items.passage: The cave paintings at Lascaux, in southwestern France, are often compared with ______ at Chauvet, which were created thousands of years earlier.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The pronoun replaces cave paintings, a plural noun, so the comparison needs those (= the paintings at Chauvet). A, B, and D are singular and do not match paintings.

items.passage: Unlike most mammals, whose mature red blood cells lack a nucleus, ______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: birds have red blood cells that keep their nucleus throughout their life span.
options.B: the red blood cells of birds keep their nucleus throughout their life span.
options.C: a bird’s red blood cells keep their nucleus throughout their life span.
options.D: keeping their nucleus throughout their life span is typical of birds’ red blood cells.

items.explanation: Unlike most mammals compares animals, so the noun right after the comma must be animals of another kind: birds. B and C compare mammals with red blood cells (in C, a bird’s is only a possessive). D compares mammals with an action (keeping…).

items.passage: Analysis of fossils showed that the wing bones of one extinct giant seabird were much lighter than ______ supporting the idea that the bird glided for long distances rather than flapping its wings.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The comparison is between wing bones, so the second item must also be bones: those of modern albatrosses (plural, matching bones). A and D compare bones with birds. B uses the singular that, which does not match the plural bones.

items.skill: Example and Illustration: for example, for instance
items.passage: Many desert plants have developed striking strategies for conserving water. The saguaro cactus, ______ can expand its pleated stem to store hundreds of liters of water after a single rainstorm.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: “Striking strategies for conserving water” is general; the saguaro cactus is one specific case. for instance fits. in contrast signals difference, in addition would need a parallel new point, and nevertheless signals concession.

items.skill: Example and Illustration: for example, for instance
items.passage: Several Renaissance painters experimented with unconventional materials, sometimes with unfortunate results. Leonardo da Vinci’s The Last Supper, ______ was painted in tempera on dry plaster rather than in the traditional fresco technique, and it began flaking within decades.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: “Several Renaissance painters experimented with unconventional materials” is general; Leonardo’s tempera on dry plaster is one case. for example is correct. similarly would need a second, parallel painter, however signals contrast, and as a result signals an effect.

items.skill: Emphasis and Confirmation: in fact, indeed, certainly
items.passage: Honeybees are remarkably skilled navigators. ______ a foraging bee can find its way back to its hive from more than five kilometers away, using the position of the Sun as a compass.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: “Remarkably skilled navigators” is the claim; finding the hive from more than five kilometers away is concrete proof. In fact strengthens the claim. Instead replaces, By contrast and Nevertheless signal a turn in direction.

items.skill: Emphasis and Confirmation: in fact, indeed, certainly
items.passage: Many early reviewers dismissed Zora Neale Hurston’s Their Eyes Were Watching God (1937) as a minor work. Over the following decades, however, the novel’s reputation grew steadily; ______ it is now widely regarded as a classic of American literature and is taught in classrooms around the world.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The novel’s reputation “grew steadily”; the next clause confirms and intensifies this (it is now a widely taught classic). indeed fits. for example would need one case of a group, instead replaces, and in contrast signals a difference.

items.skill: Similarity and Comparison: similarly, likewise, in the same way
items.passage: Honeybees perform a “waggle dance” to tell other members of the hive where food can be found. ______ many species of ants lay down chemical trails that guide their nestmates to a food source.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Bees and ants are two different insects that do the same thing: share the location of food with their group. Likewise fits. Instead would replace the bee behavior, For example would need ants to be a case of honeybees, and Consequently wrongly says the bees’ dance causes the ants’ trails.

items.skill: Similarity and Comparison: similarly, likewise, in the same way
items.passage: The Roman architect Vitruvius argued that a good building must be sturdy, useful, and beautiful. Centuries later, the Renaissance architect Leon Battista Alberti ______ insisted that great architecture must combine strength, function, and beauty.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Alberti held the same three-part view as Vitruvius. The mid-sentence likewise signals that a second person shares the idea. however signals contrast, for instance would make Alberti an example of Vitruvius, and meanwhile means “at the same time,” but Alberti lived centuries later.

items.skill: Similarity and Comparison: similarly, likewise, in the same way
items.passage: In the 1840s, Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis found that hand washing sharply reduced deaths in hospital maternity wards. ______ British surgeon Joseph Lister showed in the 1860s that sterilizing surgical instruments dramatically lowered infection rates after surgery.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Both doctors showed that cleanliness reduced deaths or infections, in two different medical settings. In a similar way links these parallel discoveries. Nevertheless signals contrast, In other words would restate Semmelweis’s finding, and Specifically would add detail about it.

items.skill: Alternative, Replacement, Purpose, and Comment: alternatively, instead, more often, to that end, fittingly
items.passage: For decades, biologists tried to count wild snow leopards by following their tracks on foot through the Himalayas, a slow and often dangerous method that missed many animals. ______ many researchers now rely on motion-activated cameras that photograph the leopards as they pass.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The old tracking method is being replaced by camera traps. Instead introduces the replacement. Similarly would make the cameras the same kind of method, For example would make them an example of tracking on foot, and In addition would keep both methods side by side rather than replacing the first.

items.skill: Every Clause Needs a Finite (Main) Verb
items.passage: The fossilized footprints discovered along a dry lakebed in New Mexico’s White Sands National Park, some dating back more than 21,000 years, ______ that humans reached North America earlier than once believed.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The long subject "The fossilized footprints..." still has no main verb. "Suggest" is finite and plural. The other choices are nonfinite and leave the sentence without a main verb.

items.passage: Since its founding in 1998, the observatory ______ more than 40 previously unknown near-Earth asteroids.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Since 1998" describes an action that began in the past and continues up to now, which requires the present perfect "has discovered." The past perfect (D) needs a later past reference point.

items.passage: The committee of researchers from three universities ______ its final report on coastal erosion next spring.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is the singular collective noun "committee" (not "researchers" or "universities"), and the pronoun "its" confirms it is treated as a single unit. Only "plans" is singular.

items.passage: After a two-year renovation of its concert hall, the city orchestra performed ______ first season in the restored building to sold-out audiences.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "The city orchestra" is a singular collective noun (note "its concert hall" earlier), so the singular possessive "its" is correct. "It's" means "it is."

items.skill: Modifiers: Dangling Modifiers and Logical Comparisons
items.passage: Buried under volcanic ash for nearly two millennia, ______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: archaeologists have found Pompeii’s frescoes remarkably intact.
options.B: Pompeii’s frescoes have survived remarkably intact.
options.C: the survival of Pompeii’s frescoes is remarkable.
options.D: there are frescoes in Pompeii that survived intact.

items.explanation: The frescoes were buried, so "Pompeii’s frescoes" must come right after the modifier. A says the archaeologists were buried; C says the survival was buried; D starts with "there."

items.skill: Modifiers: Dangling Modifiers and Logical Comparisons
items.passage: Researchers measuring bite strength found that the bite force of a saltwater crocodile is far greater than ______
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Compare like with like: bite force to bite force. "That of a lion" means "the bite force of a lion." A and C illogically compare a bite force to an animal.
